All these matters and subjects, as we have said before, are arrangements through which the Muslim society is to be brought out of the system of ignorance (Jahiliyyah) in commercial and economic affairs and brought into the Islamic system of life. Furthermore, the gradual removal of the remaining traces of the ignorant society, which were still present, is also intended. In their place, by highlighting the features of the Islamic society, the Muslim community as a whole is to be raised to that lofty station where it stands out in the whole world. Thus the Islamic system raises this Ummah above the level of ignorance and lifts it to ever greater heights.

In the second lesson, the principles of the Islamic concept of life are again established. In it, the definition of faith (iman) and its conditions are explained, and these principles of faith are restated so that, within the Muslim community, some other rules of collective support may be laid down. This system of collective support begins first within the limited sphere of the family and then its limits extend to the whole Muslim community. Along with commanding this collective support and spending, miserliness and stinginess are also condemned. Moreover, pride in wealth, concealing the blessings of Allah, and showing off in contrast to spending in the way of Allah are condemned. Also in this lesson, the method of purifying the self through the worship of Allah is taught, including the rules of bodily purity at the time of worship, and the command that intoxicants must be completely avoided at the time of worship, because drinking wine and worship are in contradiction. This was an initial command regarding wine-drinking; later, wine-drinking was completely prohibited. This is the particular method of the Qur'an in reform: the method of gradual reform.

In the third lesson, it is explained what your attitude towards the People of the Book should be. This is also one of the important themes of this surah, in which the deceit of their intentions and their evil plans concerning the Muslims are exposed. Expressing astonishment at their conduct, their cunning and malice are made clear, and it is established that they are enemies of the Muslims. They are warned that in the end they are going to be afflicted with a painful punishment.

In the fourth lesson, the definition of Islam, the meaning of religion and the conditions of faith are explained, and this is stated in extremely decisive and conclusive words. It is explained what the nature of the Islamic system of life is, and how in this system Muslims obey Allah alone, worship Him alone, and seek guidance from Him alone, and also decide all disputes of their lives in accordance with the Book of Allah and the commands of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). In this lesson it is also explained that it is an obligation upon Muslims to deliver trusts to their rightful owners, and that when the question of justice arises, they should judge with justice, and should implement the Islamic method in people's lives. These matters are presented in a manner as though they are the conditions of faith. At the same time, astonishment is expressed that there are some people who claim to have faith, yet do not even fulfil the first condition of faith, namely, that they do not get the disputes of their whole lives decided in accordance with the commands of Allah and His Messenger with complete submission and contentment. Then, again and again, it is emphasised that if this condition is not fulfilled, there is no faith, no matter how much verbal claim of faith is made, because this is a clear violation of the condition of faith.

Accordingly, in the fifth lesson, the Islamic community is commanded to prepare for fighting (jihad bil-qital) within the community of the Islamic system, and harsh criticism is directed at those who are hypocrites and place obstacles in the way of jihad, or who are believers but are lax in jihad. In this lesson, while explaining the real purpose of jihad and fighting and the need for them, the hearts of the believers are stirred up, telling them that jihad and fighting are necessary so that the weak among the Muslims and their children may be rescued from the Dar al-Kufr (abode of disbelief) and admitted into the Dar al-Islam (abode of Islam), and so that, by bringing them under the shade of this exalted and lofty Islamic system of life, they may be given the joys of life. In this lesson it is also explained that a day has been fixed for every human being on which they must leave this world, so they should not fear difficult conditions and circumstances. At the end of the lesson, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is commanded to begin jihad, even if he is alone, because there is no other course to make this religion dominant and to establish and secure the Islamic system of life.

Continuing the theme of jihad fi sabilillah (struggle in the way of Allah), the sixth lesson also mentions countless international principles. That is, on one side there is the Islamic camp, on the other side there is its enemy camp, and on a third side there is the neutral camp, or those people with whom the Islamic camp has treaties. The matter is not merely one of force, domination and seizure, but the practice of jihad is to be continued with realism, within the limits of law and ethics, keeping human relations in view, and taking into account the tendencies of the various international camps with differing outlooks.

Along with the theme of jihad fi sabilillah, the types of jihad with wealth (jihad bil-mal) and jihad with the self (jihad bin-nafs) are also explained. This is the seventh lesson, and in it harsh criticism is directed at those who sit in the Dar al-Kufr and do not migrate and take part in the battle between truth and falsehood, even though their religion is not safe in the Dar al-Kufr, while the Dar al-Islam has been established and Islamic banners are flying in it with great honour and justice. At the end of this lesson, the Muslims are urged to fight in the way of Allah, and they are commanded to pursue the enemy and not to show the slightest laxity in pursuing and searching for the enemy. Finally, it is made clear what the position of the Muslims is and what the position of the enemies of Islam is; what the destiny of the believers is going to be, and with what frightful end the people of disbelief are going to be confronted.

In the eighth lesson, we reach the pinnacle of the Islamic system of justice. What happens is that a Jew is falsely accused, testimony goes against him, the Qur'an is revealed from the exalted assembly (al-mala' al-a'la), and the Jew is declared innocent. This justice is administered in circumstances where the Jews are, on every side, busy night and day with conspiracies against the Muslims. But in the Islamic system of justice, judgement is not influenced by anyone's friendship, nor can anyone's enmity deprive it of justice. This is the standard of justice and equity upon which humanity has never fully measured up. Yes, humanity reached this station only under the shade of the exalted and unparalleled Islamic system of life.

Now comes the ninth lesson, in which a contest is conducted with shirk (associating partners with Allah) and the polytheists. Discussion is held on polytheistic superstitions and their effects, misguiding religious symbols, and outdated and corrupt polytheistic notions, and the notions of the people concerning Allah's system of justice, their carnal desires, false thoughts and illusions are corrected. In it, it is explained that reward and punishment with Allah depend on deeds, not on illusions and good wishes. And at the end it is explained that Islam is the only accepted religion, and that this is the Millah of Ibrahim (the creed of Abraham).

In the ninth lesson, again women are made the subject. Their rights, especially the rights of orphans and the weak, are discussed, particularly concerning children. The beginning of this surah was also on this theme. It was explained what arrangements and actions will be taken when a husband boycotts his wife and when a wife disobeys. The rules of just treatment of women are given, without which the conjugal system cannot be set right at all, and if reform cannot be achieved, it is better that the two parties separate.

The conclusion of the rules that came concerning the family is such that the purpose of conjugal rules and the establishment of justice in society is linked to the Being of Allah, and it is said that Allah is the owner of the heavens and the earth. He has power to destroy all existing creation and to create, in their place, an entirely new creation. Therefore, the command to act upon Allah's commands and guidance is not a trivial matter. And these commands are connected with the Being of the Creator, who is a Great Being. Consequently, the fear of God naturally arises in hearts, and for those who believe in Allah it becomes necessary to act justly in their affairs, and the fear of God dominates them in all their dealings. This is in keeping with the manner of the Qur'an, which presents even a specific and limited subject by bringing it within a broader and more general scope.

Now comes the last lesson of this part, which is almost confined to criticism of hypocrisy (nifaq) and the hypocrites. The believers are invited to become true Muslims and to walk upon the straight path. They are warned not to establish friendly relations with any circle other than the Muslim community and its leadership, and not to show laxity or softness in matters of religion because of the hypocrites and enemies of the faith, or for the sake of collective relations and personal interests, because doing so would in reality be hypocrisy. The hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of Hell on the Day of Resurrection, and the hypocrites are in reality friends of the disbelievers. This lesson concludes with a description of the attributes of Allah, and of what the relationship of Allah with His servants is, and what the wisdom is in punishing those who go astray and deviate. If they believe and become grateful, Allah has no interest, without reason, in inflicting punishment.

﴿Why should Allah punish you if you are grateful and believe? And Allah is ever Appreciative, All-Knowing.﴾ (4:147)

This is a strange style of speech. Mercy showers upon the heart. What concern is it of Allah to punish? He is the self-sufficient King, provided people come onto the straight path. Allah is Shakir, that is, Appreciative; He showers His grace and favour, provided they are grateful. But the fault lies with themselves, for they bring Allah's punishment upon themselves, because of their disbelief and denial, and because of the corruption on the earth, and in human self and human life, which is brought about by their disbelief and denial.

Thus this part has spread its wings and concealed within itself countless purposes and themes. In short, these are very long and broad discussions. Here in this commentary, only brief indications are intended. God willing, we shall soon take up these themes in detail.

**Lesson No. 32 at a Glance:**

This lesson is the completion of the subjects that were mentioned in this surah concerning the organisation of married life and its formation in accordance with the rules of nature. After this lesson, there will be complementary discussion on this important theme in only two more places. This theme is important in Islam because the rectitude and stability of the whole of human life depend upon its rectitude. If it is set right in a society, the whole of human life continues with great tranquillity and peace, and its structure is built upon healthy foundations. And if married life is ruined and deviates from the straight path, it causes a great and all-encompassing corruption on this earth.

In this lesson, the complete list of women with whom marriage is forbidden is given. After that, the method is laid down on the basis of which the union of a woman and a man is made lawful in the form of a pure family, and it is explained that by observing this method, apart from purity and chastity, great ease and facilities are created for people. Then the organising rules are laid down upon which the structure of the institution of the family is built, and the rights and responsibilities placed upon the spouses in this institution are clarified. Along with this organisation of the family, rules are given in the Islamic society concerning certain financial rights, whether these relate to acquired rights or inherited rights. These rights relate both to collective relations and to the inheritance rights of men and women within a family. Likewise, the matters have been explained that relate to inherited rights of guardianship (wilayah), beyond kinship.

This matter is generally noteworthy: between all these regulations and commandments there is a subtle connection. This connection is in fact the first principle: that all these commandments and regulations have been issued by Allah, glory be to Him, and they are the inherent requirement of His divinity and sovereignty, because among the attributes specific to the Being of Allah is His sovereignty, and a manifestation of this sovereignty is legislation for mankind. It is the social system upon whose foundation they will establish their lives and form their collective relationships.

This subtle connection is repeatedly mentioned in the context of the discussion, and this particular attribute of Allah is repeatedly mentioned, and it is said that all these commandments are being sent down and issued from the Being of the One who is All-Knowing and All-Wise. This indication is a wise one, full of meanings, because in the Islamic system of life, the One from whom commands and prohibitions are issued is the One who possesses perfect knowledge and comprehensive knowledge, and who possesses wisdom and insight. These are divine attributes which are not found in human beings, because man does not have the capacity to establish for himself a code for human life. This is why whenever man has deviated from the code made by the All-Knowing, All-Aware God, mountains of calamities have fallen upon him, and he has become lost in a barren wilderness, wandering without any guide or mentor. Yet, out of his ignorance, his obstinacy and his carnal desires, he has continued to think that he would cross this desert and find for himself, and for his salvation, a better path than the one to which Allah is calling.

The other truth to which the context repeatedly points is that the Islamic way of life is extremely easy for man, extremely realistic, and in exact accordance with natural inclinations, in contrast to those systems of life which man makes for himself and believes to be easy, whereas, considering human weakness, the Islamic system is Allah's pure mercy and compassion, in that He has laid down for man this system and method, which is so balanced that a slight deviation from it destroys balance and moderation, and the punishment of Allah descends upon man, and he is afflicted with a hardship and severity which he has no strength to bear. Moreover, because of this self-made system, man loses his human station and falls face-down into a pit of filth.

When we discuss the texts of the Qur'an in detail in the following pages, we will, as occasion arises, point to the realization of this truth in the light of the historical stages of mankind, because it is a historical fact. Yes, when ignorance casts veils over hearts and blinds the eyes, then the light of the eyes is extinguished, hearts become lightless, and a person cannot perceive any reality, however bright it may be.

Earlier, at the end of the fourth part (Para), a list was given of the women who were forbidden on the basis of permanent and inherent prohibition. It is appropriate that this list be kept in view again.

(Verse) "Wa la tankihu ma nakaha aba'ukum minan-nisa'i illa ma qad salaf, innahu kana fahishatan wa maqtan wa saa'a sabila." (22) "Hurrimat 'alaykum ummahatukum wa banatukum wa akhawatukum wa 'ammatukum wa khalatukum wa banat al-akhi wa banat al-ukhti wa ummahatukumu-llati arda'nakum wa akhawatukum min ar-rada'a wa ummahat nisa'ikum wa rabaa'ibukumu-llati fi hujurikum min nisa'ikumu-llati dakhaltum bihinna fa in lam takunu dakhaltum bihinna fala junaha 'alaykum wa halaila abna'ikumu-lladhina min aslabikum wa an tajma'u bayna al-ukhtayni illa ma qad salaf, inna Allaha kana Ghafuran Rahima." (23) (4:22-23)

And do not marry those women whom your fathers have married, except what has already passed; indeed it is an indecency, detestable, and an evil way. Forbidden to you are your mothers, daughters, sisters, paternal aunts, maternal aunts, nieces (brother's daughters), nieces (sister's daughters), your mothers who nursed you, your milk-sisters, your wives' mothers, and your stepdaughters who are in your guardianship, born of your wives with whom you have consummated marriage; but if you have not consummated marriage with them, there is no blame upon you (in marrying their daughters); and the wives of your sons who are from your loins, and it is also forbidden that you combine two sisters in marriage, except what has already passed. Indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. (23)

Thus these verses of the fifth part are a completion of the final verses of the fourth part. (Wal-muhsanatu minan-nisa') "And the women who are married (to others)."

They are included among the forbidden because they are within the protective bond of marriage to other men; therefore they are forbidden to all except their husbands, and marriage with them is not permissible. Since the social system of Islam is founded upon the family, marriage and the prohibition of marriage hold the first brick's rank in the construction of the Islamic system. Thus, in the Islamic system the family is the first unit, and the family must be safeguarded from every kind of mixing, especially the mixing of lineage, which generally results from unrestrained sexual relations, through which obscenity spreads and the whole society becomes implicated in it.

The family formed from the unit of Islamic society is established upon open marriage, in which a woman becomes dedicated to one man. Thus she comes under this man's protection and becomes muhsana, that is, protected and safeguarded. This system is the most complete system, which is in harmony with human nature and the real needs of man, the needs that are necessary for man as man. It is worth noting here that there are certain purposes of human life which are more important, greater and broader than its animal purposes, although animal purposes are also fulfilled within them. In short, the social system of Islam fulfills the lofty aims of human society in full, and it provides complete means of peace and tranquility for that society: peace of the human self and conscience, and through the human household and through it the peace and calm of human society.

It is a plain observation that a human child requires care for a longer period than any other animal, and after childhood it requires yet a long period for its intellectual and moral training, so that it may comprehend the demands of collective human life in a way by which man can be distinguished from animals.

When sexual union takes place among animals and the purpose of procreation and multiplication is fulfilled, their sexual purposes are fulfilled. But the case of man is that his purposes are not fulfilled merely by these matters; his purposes go beyond them. He needs a lasting companionship of man and woman and an enduring bond between husband and wife, so that the child born may be trained and prepared for the preservation of self, the preservation of human life, and the provision of its food and needs. Besides this, the most important purpose is that the experiments which humanity has carried out up to that time in the fields of knowledge and technology should also be transmitted to him, so that he may take a full part in human society and be able to discharge his duty in this continuous process of human progress, which has been going on for centuries, and in his own age in which he was born.

This is why, as far as the human species is concerned, the place of sexual pleasure in the relations between man and woman is very low. Sexual pleasure has been placed by the divine power in man and woman merely so that they may come together with joy and interest, and thus bear their responsibilities cheerfully in the task of the continuation of the human race. In the basis of the union of man and woman, sexual pleasure is not the primary factor; rather, the real factor is the discharge of the obligations toward the species, that is, the care of the weak coming generation which is brought into existence through this sexual union. Also, the discharge of rights toward that society upon which lies the responsibility of training the present generation, so that this generation may discharge its human and collective duties, and thus fulfill the essential purposes of human existence.

All these purposes are fulfilled in such a way that sexual relations are organized in the form of a family, and this is the method which has been proven correct as a result of human experience. In this method, one woman is dedicated to one man, and thus this relationship is founded on constantly stable foundations. In the formation of the family, sexual pleasure alone is not the real factor, nor is sexual licentiousness alone the decisive and determining element; nor in the maintaining of this relationship, in its continuance and in the resolution of difficulties that arise in its survival, does this factor alone operate; nor does this sexual act alone lie behind the process of breaking up a family.

I consider that there can be no greater insult to the sacred system of the family than to organize it merely on the basis of lust, the satisfaction of temporary sexual desires and mere pleasure-seeking, instead of as a sacred factor of fulfilling duty, while all these factors are very temporary. I consider that to present such a conception is a criminal endeavour against man and humanity. For in this way, evils such as obscenity, anarchy, social licentiousness and social unbridledness spread like a storm through society, and thus the whole society collapses and its foundations shake.

At present in the world, some writers are writing against the family system. A vast media has been set against it, which constantly engages in broadcasting against marriage and the family system, and encourages those relationships which are based solely on sexual pleasure and casual enjoyment, while the permanent family system is belittled. From this discussion it will be well understood what a great crime those writers who work along these lines are committing against humanity. Through the efforts of these gentlemen, the form of the family system has been distorted and its importance has been destroyed.

On this subject, a saying of Hazrat Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) contains great depth. A man wished to divorce his wife merely because he no longer had any love for her. Hazrat Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Is the foundation of the family upon love alone? If that is so, then what will become of the upbringing of the children, and who will then bear the responsibilities?" And Hazrat Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) derived this outlook on life from the guidance and training of the Holy Qur'an. The Holy Qur'an had trained the chosen servants of Allah in this way:

(Verse) "Wa 'ashiruhunna bil-ma'ruf, fa in karihtumuhunna fa 'asa an takrahu shay'an wa yaj'alu Allahu fihi khayran kathira." (4:19)
"Live with them in kindness. If you dislike them, it may be that you dislike something while Allah has placed in it much good."

And this command has been given so that, as far as possible, a household may be maintained, and that emotional feelings and inclinations may be contended with and kept under control, and that this sacred relationship between man and woman may not be broken until the final efforts to sustain it have failed. The Islamic system has made this effort so that the young children born in this family will not have their future destroyed. They should not fall within the blows of the coming storm, the rage of unruly emotions, and the whirlwinds of carnal desires.

In the light of this lofty and profound viewpoint, the superficiality of the babbling of shameless people, who speak about the family system, becomes self-evident. These people are against every relationship between man and woman which imposes certain duties and rights upon the spouses, whose connection is with the precious commodity of humanity, namely the young generation, or with the training of that young generation which fits it for the natural function of discharging its human duties in modern, advanced life, and in which the interests of all generations are kept in view; while these people praise and extol every relationship whose foundation is passing emotions and fleeting pleasure, and which they consider to be a sign of progress.

In today's age, filthy and cheap films and the misguided, corrupt media channels teach every married woman that whenever her heart becomes estranged from her husband, she should immediately seek a friend for herself, and these media outlets regard the act of such a woman as a sacred act, while they call the relationship with her lawful husband a "contract for the sale of the body," although Allah, in the discussion of the forbidden women, says: (Verse) "Wal-muhsanatu minan-nisa'" "And the women who are in the protective bond of marriage," and because they are within the protective bond of marriage, He declares them forbidden to other men. This is the word of Allah; and that is the word of those shameless people whom the enemies of Islam have brought under their control so that they may break this sacred bond, and by breaking the bond of marriage they wish to spread obscenity in the Islamic society.

(Verse) "Wallahu yaqulu al-haqqa wa huwa yahdi as-sabil." "It is Allah who speaks the truth, and it is He alone who shows the straight path."

The world today is investing enormous, highly organised effort in inventing values of life, moral standards and concepts that run counter to the pleasure of Allah, jalla shanuh, and in establishing social ties and social foundations in human life that differ from those which Allah has ordained. Those who are busy day and night in these thankless endeavours believe that their aim is limited to demolishing the foundations of Islamic society inside Islamic countries, so that by disrupting the system of collective life in those countries they may remove every obstacle that stands in the way of their particular objectives. Under these aims they are destroying the beliefs, morals and social order of the Muslims, but they do not reflect on how far-reaching the harm of these misguided endeavours is for themselves. They are not merely destroying the Islamic order of society; in truth they are destroying the values of the whole of humanity, the values upon which the lofty collective values of all humankind rest. Through this policy, these people have deprived all of humanity of the elements because of which humanity had carried the great trust upon its shoulders. That is, the raising of the finest and most advanced generation on this earth. Because of their policy, humanity has been deprived of the wealth of children trained in their mother's lap. Let it be remembered that for a child, the mother's lap is the soft, contented and peaceful cradle, and through such upbringing the child is protected from unbridled sexual passions. Moreover, he does not fall prey to changing inclinations and desires, nor does he become the plaything of desires that turn with every breath of wind. A child trained in his mother's lap is able to discharge the collective responsibilities of the human race, and these aims are entirely separate from and sacred compared to the aims of raising children in the impious nurseries of the coupling of two individuals for the sake of mere lust and of specific breeding, and these aims are based on steady, tranquil and far-reaching human duties.

In this situation the whole human race becomes deserving of curse and blame, because one limb of humanity is destroying the other limbs, and in it the present human generation is ruining the future of coming generations, merely so that its own self may benefit and its own present desires may be fully satisfied, even if nothing remains in the destiny of future generations except ruin and devastation. And the punishment of Allah becomes the decisive judgement upon those generations who are disobeying the commands of Allah, who maintain a course contrary to the nature He created, and who go against His clear guidance, and because of whom the whole of humankind is gripped by these calamities. Yes, from this ruin and divine punishment, only a handful of believers will surely be safe, those who acknowledge the commands of Allah, who strive to establish the kingdom of Allah on this earth, who call people to it by seizing them, and who wish to save them from that destroying corruption which humanity itself is preparing for itself, and which it believes is a conspiracy it is carrying out only against Islamic countries, so that the obstacles standing in its path may be removed. For this purpose they have engaged the men of pen and media workers of the Islamic world themselves, and they consider their endeavours to be confined only within the Islamic world, whereas this is not so.

(Wal-muhsanat min an-nisa' illa ma malakat aymanukum) ﴿And the married women are forbidden to you, except those whom your right hands possess.﴾ The exception in this phrase concerns the captive women who were taken prisoner in the Islamic wars, but who, in the land of war and the land of disbelief, had been married to other men. In that case their marriage bond with their former husbands was severed, because upon their coming from the land of disbelief into the land of Islam their marriage breaks; therefore by this change they no longer remain married women. And in the land of Islam they have no husband, and with the arrival of a single menstrual period their womb is considered free of the traces of the former husband. That is, it is concluded that their womb is free of pregnancy. If they now embrace Islam, marriage with them is lawful, or for the person to whose share they fall, intercourse with them also becomes lawful, because they become his possession. In this case, whether they accept Islam or not, intercourse is permitted.

In the second part of Zilal al-Quran we have discussed in detail the Islamic position on the question of slavery, and a detailed discussion in this regard has been given under the verse of Surah Muhammad: ﴿Until, when you have thoroughly subdued them, then bind the captives firmly; after that either grace or ransom, until the war lays down its burdens﴾ (47:4). Let it be consulted there.

It is sufficient here to note that at that time the Islamic camp was dealing with slavery in the same manner as the opposing camp was dealing with it towards itself, while the Islamic camp treated the slaves of its opponents well. The conduct of the Islamic camp was based on noble human morality, and the Islamic camp had no other option, because the law of enslavement was an internationally prevailing law, and it was not possible for Islam to unilaterally announce the abolition of that law. Had this been done, those Muslims who became slaves would have remained slaves forever, while those from among the disbelievers who were enslaved would have been freed. Thus the balance of the enemy camp would have become heavier than the Islamic camp, and the enemy camp's courage to attack the Islamic camp would have increased, since they would have been fully satisfied with the outcomes of such attacks, and the opposing camp would have profited in every case.

Now an important question arises: if, for Islam, it had become necessary to keep the captive disbelieving women within its society, then how were they to be treated? For these women, mere provision of food and drink could not suffice, because alongside that they were bound to another natural need. It was also necessary to arrange for the fulfilment of this need, for otherwise this corruption would have spread. Furthermore, since they were in a state of polytheism, it was not lawful for the Muslims to marry them, nor was it lawful to force them into Islam. Therefore only one course remained: that those who possessed them might lawfully have intercourse with them even in their state of polytheism, so long as they remained polytheistic, provided that the condition of the purity of the womb was fulfilled for those among them who had been married in the land of war, and that their bond with their husbands in the land of disbelief was severed.

After these prohibited women, and before the explanation of the other prohibitions and before the announcement of the status of all remaining women, it is necessary to remind here that in the Islamic system of life the authority to declare things forbidden and lawful belongs to Allah alone. No one other than Allah has these powers. It is Allah's task to legislate for human beings regarding the affairs of their lives.

(Kitaba Allahu 'alaykum) ﴿This is the decree of Allah upon you﴾: this is the law of Allah, the observance of which is made binding upon you. This is the covenant and compact of Allah with you, which has been firmly settled between Him and you, and this is His command upon it. The matter is not merely of some desire to be pursued, nor is it a matter of custom or tradition to be followed, nor a matter of family custom that must be practised. Rather, it is the requirement of Allah's compact, His covenant and His Book, and this is the very source from which the believers derive the laws of lawful and unlawful. Whatever He makes obligatory must be acted upon, what He writes is the final word, and beyond that, He will hold you accountable for what He has written and will demand that you act upon it.

It is also worth noting that the Qur'an, in the list of women it has included among the prohibited, mostly were forbidden in the days of ignorance as well. Among them, in the age of ignorance, only the wife of one's father was forbidden, and marriage to two sisters simultaneously was lawful. However, marriage to the "wife of a living person" was also generally disapproved of. Their custom called this type of marriage "maqt", meaning a reprehensible act. Islam made forbidden almost the same prohibitions that were forbidden in the age of ignorance. Islam did not state as the reason for prohibition that these were forbidden in the days of ignorance too; rather, the Qur'an explicitly gave the command: "This is the law of Allah, the observance of which is obligatory upon you."

At this point we should pause a little and reflect upon what is the foundation of concepts, beliefs and ideas in Islam, and also what are the sources and origins of jurisprudence and law in Islam. In this reflection, Allah's statement is very beneficial for us in many matters.

(Due to its great length, the complete commentary on this verse could not be included. We apologise for this. Please read the remaining part of the commentary of this verse in Fi Zilal al-Quran.)

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 4, verse 25 (part 1 of 2):

(Verse) "And whoever among you does not have the means to marry free, believing women (muhsanat), let him marry from among those believing slave girls whom your right hands possess. And Allah knows best your faith; you are of one another. So marry them with the permission of their guardians, and give them their dowries according to what is reasonable, as chaste women, not unlawful lovers nor those who take secret paramours. And when they are married, if they commit immorality, they shall receive half the punishment of free women. This is for him among you who fears falling into sin; but if you are patient, it is better for you. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful." (4:25)

The Islamic system of life adopts a attitude towards man that is within his natural limits, proportionate to his capacity and strength, commensurate with his actual circumstances, and in harmony with his true needs and requirements. Islam takes a misguided person by the hand and lifts him out of the pits of misguidance, grants him the elevation and loftiness of the Islamic way of life, and throughout this process it keeps in view his nature, his strength, his real circumstances and his true needs in every situation. Rather, it also fulfils the demands of all these motives, and carries him step by step to a lofty station. However, it is a fact that Islam never accepts, in any situation, a state of jahiliyyah (ignorance) as a circumstance from which there is no alternative, because jahiliyyah is by name a descent, and it drags man down too, whereas the very purpose of Islam's existence is to raise humanity from this descent and take it to a lofty station. Yes, Islam is certainly realistic, taking into account man's nature and reality. And the reality of the matter is that man has both the capacity to rise to the station of height and excellence and the natural impulse to do so. Realism does not mean that if a man is steeped in the filth of jahiliyyah, he should be left in that condition (whatever that jahiliyyah may be). Rather, the reality is that it lies within man's capacity and scope to attain exaltation and to progress, and it is also his natural impulse; and Allah, the Exalted, is well aware of man's circumstances, for He is man's Creator, and knows his reality well.

It is Allah alone who knows all the things that stir in the hearts of people. "Does not He who created know? And He is the Subtle, the Acquainted." (67:14)

In the early Islamic society there were slaves. These slaves came into being as a result of the battles between Muslims and unbelievers, and they remained slaves until the matter of their slavery was settled on an international basis, that is, either these prisoners of war were released free as a favour, or they were exchanged for Muslim prisoners, or they were released upon receipt of a ransom; that is, in accordance with the conditions that prevailed between the Muslims and the opposing power. Until the final decision regarding prisoners and slaves was made, Islam resolved the problem of these slaves by making lawful the intercourse of the owner with the female prisoner or slave, the explanation of which we have already given in the previous verse, so that the natural needs of the women in ownership might be fulfilled in accordance with a regulated system. The second way is that these slave women be given in marriage to a believer, provided they have accepted Islam. In both of these cases, intercourse with them can take place only after they have migrated from the Dar al-Harb to the Dar al-Islam, and after a full investigation of the cleanliness of their wombs following one menstrual period. However, for persons other than the owners of these slave girls, there is only one way of having intercourse with them, namely, that a marriage contract be concluded with them. Apart from this, it is not permissible for them to engage in prostitution in society and take wages, nor is it permissible for their owners to set them free and then have them roam about prostituting themselves for those owners. This verse prescribes this method of marrying such women.

(Verse) "And whoever among you does not have the means to marry free, believing women (muhsanat), let him marry from among those believing slave girls whom your right hands possess." (4:25)

Islam prefers that marriage be contracted with a free woman, provided one has the capacity to marry a woman of noble birth. This free woman is called muhsanah because she is protected within the fortress of freedom. Dignity and freedom teach her how to safeguard her chastity and purity. Moreover, the nobility of freedom also teaches her how to protect her husband's honour. Therefore, the term muhsanat is used here for noble-born and free women. Here, muhsanat does not mean women who are married and are within the fortress of someone's marriage; it has already been explained earlier that other men's wives, that is, muhsanat, are forbidden to all men. Here, the term muhsanat is used for free women because they are enclosed within the fortress of freedom. Because of freedom and nobility, the sense of self-respect exists in the human conscience and consciousness, and in life free women enjoy certain rights. A free woman has a family, she has a household, she has a reputation, she has guardians, and she too keeps the honour of her family in view. Then her self-respect also restrains her from base conduct. Therefore she avoids adultery and fornication. These restraints and barriers do not apply to common prostitutes or slave women, which is why they are not muhsanat. Even if they marry, traces of the times of slavery remain within them; hence, like a free woman, there is not in their character dignity of self, chastity and self-respect. Moreover, the feeling of hereditary nobility does not dominate their heart and mind, so that they would have any fear of being stained by it. In addition, consideration has also been given to the feelings of the coming generation, because the offspring of a slave woman used to be regarded as inferior compared with the offspring of a free and noble woman, and thus the stigma of slavery clung to them in one form or another; and these notions were generally prevalent in Arab society, in which the Holy Qur'an was being revealed. These were the reasons why Islam preferred that, as far as possible, Muslims marry free and noble women. It permitted marriage with women who are not muhsanat, that is, slave girls, on the condition that marriage with a free woman (hurrah) is not possible, or one does not have the means, or one would have to spend agonizing moments waiting and could not wait any longer.

When these difficulties exist, and there is also the danger of a man going astray, and waiting is hard for him, Islam does not block his path; rather, it permits him to marry slave girls with ease, tranquillity and comfort. Marriage with slave girls is permitted only with those who have already accepted faith and who belong to another's ownership. The form of faith is definitively fixed here as well: just as faith was made a condition in marriage with free and muhsanah women earlier, so too marriage with an unbelieving slave girl is in no way permissible. Therefore, the first mandatory condition imposed is that they must be believers (mu'minat). (Verse) "from among those believing slave girls whom your right hands possess" (4:25). The second condition is that their dowries be paid, which are obligatory, and the right to receive them does not belong to their owners; it is their own pure right. (Verse) "So give them their dowries" (4:25). The third condition is that their compensation be given as a dowry, and that enjoyment of them be by way of marriage, not by way of friendship or as prostitutes. Mukhadanah means friendship with a man or woman, and sifah means the profession of prostitution, which is open to everyone. (Verse) "as chaste women, not unlawful lovers nor those who take secret paramours" (4:25).

When Islam came, this kind of licentiousness was also known among free women in Arab society, as you have already read in the hadith of Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her) cited earlier. Moreover, in that period prostitution among slave women was also widespread; the chiefs of the time would leave their slave girls in the markets, and they would earn money for them. Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, the chief of the hypocrites, kept four slave girls in Madinah for this purpose, although he was the chief of his people, and they would earn money for him through prostitution. These traces of the filth of jahiliyyah remained even in Madinah. Islam, by way of favour to the Arabs, eradicated this custom, raised the station of the Arabs, cleansed them of this filth, and after the Arabs, cleansed all of humanity of this impurity.

Islam has permitted only one form of intercourse between men and these young believing women, and that is that one man be designated for one woman, that is, the method of marriage, so that two persons forming one family live together. And this is not a situation in which there is mere animal-like gratification of lust. Since wealth is in the hands of men, Islam has fixed a dowry for the woman, which is obligatory by the law of the Shariah, so that this relationship between man and woman is not based merely on friendship or professional wages. Likewise, in the world of slaves Islam also cleansed this relationship of the filth of jahiliyyah. Whenever mankind adopted jahiliyyah, it became afflicted with this filth. Today, in this modern age, since mankind carries the banners of jahiliyyah and has abandoned Islam, it is thoroughly steeped in this filth.

Before concluding the discussion on this subject under this verse, we consider it appropriate to reflect also on the mode of expression of the Holy Qur'an, in which it speaks about the establishment of human relations in the Islamic society between slaves and free people. The Holy Qur'an does not use the terms rafiqat, jawari and amah for slave women, which were in currency at that time; Islam uses the word fatayat for them. (Verse) "from among those believing slave girls whom your right hands possess" (4:25), "young believing women" (4:25).

Islam does not make a distinction between free women and slave women such that they would be considered separate groups, whereas according to the notions prevalent at that time, slave people formed a separate world and were regarded as citizens of a second class. Islam regards all human beings as having one origin and lineage, among whom there is a bond, namely the bond of humanity and faith, which in Islam becomes the foundation for social relations. (Verse) "Allah knows best your faith; you are of one another" (4:25).

Likewise, Islam does not use the words sayyid or malik for their owners, but uses for them the word ahl (people/guardians). (Verse) "So marry them with the permission of their guardians" (4:25). And after this, Islam does not make the owners entitled to the dowry; the dowry belongs solely to the woman. Therefore the dowry is excluded from the general rule by which all earnings of slaves belonged to their owners, because the sum of the dowry does not fall within the definition of earnings; rather, the dowry is a sacred obligation in the relationship between man and woman. (Verse) "So give them their dowries according to what is reasonable" (4:25).

Islam grants slave women the honour that they should not generally wander about in prostitution, and that they establish sexual relations by marrying in the recognized manner. (Verse) "as chaste women, not unlawful lovers nor those who take secret paramours" (4:25).

All these features and aspects carry a station of honour and dignity for these young slave women, and, as the demand of the time required, no diminution has been made in their true station of humanity.

If this honour and esteem is compared with the conditions prevalent and current at the time of the revelation of the Qur'an, in which slaves were looked upon with contempt, were deprived of exalted human dignity, and were deprived of all the human rights that accrue on the basis of that human dignity, it will be seen how far-reaching the transformation Islam brought about in this regard. Islam ennobled these women with human dignity, always observed their station of humanity, regardless of the fact that this creature was temporarily confined in the bondage of slavery, which Islam regarded merely as a temporary and transitional condition.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 4, verse 25 (part 2 of 2):

In today's modern and civilised age too, if one studies how conquering armies treat the women and girls of conquered peoples, and compares this with the dignified treatment Islam gave to enslaved women under the circumstances of that time, it will become clear that Islam, within the temporarily existing institution of slavery, introduced reforms of considerable far-reaching scope. We are well aware of the stories and reports of the "sexual union" of the conquering armies of the modern age and of their filth, in which these sons of modern jahiliyyah (ignorance) became involved wherever they achieved conquest. And when they left the conquered regions, they left behind such filth that those regions could not be restored for years and years.

Thus, if after this marriage these young women commit any indecency or adultery, a lighter punishment has been prescribed for them compared with free and honourable women, because the circumstances and conditions of these enslaved women are such that they have more opportunities to commit indecency and adultery, and these women have less capacity for defence compared with free women, because in slavery a person's conscience changes and they do not feel a sense of self-respect. They also do not feel the dishonour of the family's honour being destroyed, because it is the sense of personal and family honour that keeps alive in free women the spirit of protecting their chastity. Moreover, a person's social standing and economic condition are also an important factor in whether or not one falls into indecency and adultery, and the social status and economic condition of an enslaved woman are, in any case, lower than those of a free woman. For this reason, an enslaved woman can in any case be lured very easily in this matter, that is, because of lack of wealth and lineage. On the basis of these causes and reasons, Islam set the prescribed punishment (hadd) for enslaved women, when they are married, at half of the hadd for those free women, and when they have not yet been married. He says:

(Verse) "Fa-idha uhsina fa-in atayna bi-fahishatin fa-'alayhinna nisfu ma 'ala al-muhsanati mina al-'adhab" (4:25) — "Then if they are protected in the fortress of marriage and then commit any misconduct, upon them is half the punishment prescribed for free women."

The meaning of this is that half of the punishment for free women which is divisible, and that is the punishment of lashes, while in the punishment of stoning (rajm) division is not possible. Therefore the punishment intended here is not stoning; the meaning is that when a married slave-girl commits adultery, half of the punishment for a free woman (who is not married) becomes binding upon her. As for the punishment of a slave-girl who is not married, the jurists differ on whether this same hadd will be applied to her, namely half the punishment of an unmarried free woman, or whether she will merely be given a disciplinary punishment, and this discipline will be carried out only by her owner, and there will be no half-hadd. The details of this difference can be learned from the books of jurisprudence.

Here in Fi Zilal al-Quran we only wish to explain this point: the Islamic system of life makes decisions according to people's circumstances and conditions, and thus guides them in their actual conditions towards progress and purity. It does not leave people in that fallen state of helplessness by assuming that their circumstances are their destiny and that they are forever lost in them. Allah the Exalted knew well what bad conditions enslaved people were passing through in the early period of Islam, what pressures were upon them, and with what ease a slave-girl could be incited to adultery and indecency under such circumstances. Therefore Islam neither ignored these circumstances, nor prescribed for these slave-girls the punishment that it prescribed for free women, nor did Islam accept this real and actual situation in the sense that no disciplinary punishment at all should be set for enslaved women in these circumstances. In short, by fixing half the punishment, Islam both took into account those circumstances which were important factors at that time, and prescribed a punishment, and thus adopted a just method.

Also note that Islam did not, by regarding slaves as of lower rank, show harshness in their punishment. Just as in the pre-Islamic jahiliyyah the prevailing laws were very harsh for those classes who were lowly in status and rank, while for the advanced classes these jahili laws were extremely lenient, Islamic laws are lenient towards the weak and the helpless and strict towards the nobles.

In the laws of Rome this attitude was adopted: the more lowly and inferior-ranked a defendant was, the greater the severity of the punishment inflicted. This law says: "If a person commits adultery with a chaste widow or a virgin, if that person is a member of a respectable family, half of his property shall be confiscated, and if he belongs to a base family, his punishment shall be lashes and exile." (See Digest of Justinian, translation by Abdul Aziz Fahmi.) The law of Manu, which was enacted in India and is called the Manusmriti, records that if a Brahmin becomes liable to execution, he shall not be executed; the judge may only order that his head be shaved. However, if the person liable to execution is anyone other than a Brahmin, he shall be executed. If someone from the common and lowly classes raises his hand against a Brahmin, his hand shall be cut off. (Maza Khasira al-Alam, Nadwi.) And the law of the Jews was that if a noble among them stole, they would let him go, and when a person of lower rank stole, they would enforce the hadd upon him.

It was under these circumstances that the Islamic system was revealed; it placed truth in its proper position. It enforced punishment upon the offender, but in the enforcement of punishment it took into consideration the circumstances of the offence. It fixed the punishment of a married slave-girl at half that of a noble young woman who has not yet been married. Nor did it altogether pardon her, so that her intention to sin would be disregarded and she would be regarded as compelled by circumstances, for if this were so it would be entirely contrary to fact and reality. Nor, ignoring the circumstances of her offence, did it prescribe for her a punishment equal to that of free and noble women, although the circumstances of her offence were entirely different from those of a noble woman. Nor did Islam continue those unjust laws of jahiliyyah under which the nobles were pardoned while the people of lower rank were subjected to the hadd.

In America, South Africa and other such countries, to this day this class discrimination is maintained against offenders even in this advanced age, where white nobles are pardoned while coloured weak and helpless people receive no pardon. This is jahiliyyah, and jahiliyyah wherever it is, whenever it is and however it is, is still jahiliyyah.

Marriage of free men to slave-women is merely a concession, for the person who fears falling into temptation, or who is facing very great hardship. Whoever can endure without hardship, or without the likelihood of falling into adultery, it is better for him, because marrying slave-women may in any case corrupt the environment of the family.

(Verse) "Liman khashiya al-'anata minkum wa an tasbiru khayrun lakum wallahu ghafurun rahim" (4:25) — "This concession is granted to those among you who fear that by remaining unmarried they may fall into sin; but if you are patient, it is better for you. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful."

Allah does not place upon His servants a burden beyond their capacity, nor does He place them in hardship, nor does He place them in temptation. Indeed, the system of life which Allah has chosen for those people requires of them that they progress, rise and become exalted, but He makes all these demands within the natural limits of human beings. These demands lie within their capacity and within the sphere of their genuine needs. This is why the Islamic system of life is an easy system of life. It keeps human nature in view, it is aware of human genuine needs, and it knows well the measure of human necessity. Yet Islam by no means adopts the attitude of encouraging people who keep falling into filth, nor does it tolerate that people should lie wallowing in filth before it while it praises or congratulates them upon that filth and encourages them. Rather, it imposes upon them the duty to strive to come out of that filth and to endeavour to rise, or else they bear no responsibility for the consequences that result from that degradation and from not resisting that deception.

Here the Muslims are also being exhorted to be patient until they gain the ability to marry free women. For bringing free women into the fortress of marriage is their first right. They are entitled that the building of the family should rest upon noble women, that they should bear noble sons, that these noble women should be kind to the new generations, and that they should preserve the honour of their husbands. Yet if anyone fears that he will fall into adultery and will not be able to resist, and that he cannot bear the hardship of patience and waiting, then for him there is a concession to marry slave-women, and in this concession too an effort has been made to raise the status of slave-women. And they have again been granted this honour: that they are your young women, you are their rightful guardians, you are one group, there is a firm bond of faith between you, and Allah knows well their state of faith. Furthermore, dower is obligatory and binding upon them again, and with slave-girls too you must contract marriage; there shall be neither free licentiousness nor secret friendship. And if these slave-girls commit adultery after marriage, they too will be held accountable. Yes, it is certain that their punishment will be somewhat lighter according to their circumstances, because (Verse) "wallahu ghafurun rahim" (4:25) — "Allah is Forgiving and Merciful." That is, He is forgiving in that He permitted you, in a state of necessity, to marry slave-women; and He is merciful in that He lessened the punishment of slave-girls in view of their circumstances. Wherever there is mention of some error committed, or of some matter of personal human weakness and necessity, there the words "Ghafur wa Rahim" follow at the end.

After this there comes a comprehensive conclusion to all these discussions and rulings, that is, all the commands which Allah issued concerning the organisation of a family in Islamic life, so that He might lift this nascent Islamic society out of the depths of jahiliyyah and raise its psychological, moral and collective level to a bright, pure and distinguished station. So now comes this comprehensive conclusion, in which it is explained what Allah the Exalted desires for the Muslim community through these rulings within the Islamic system of life, why He organises and regulates it, and what the aims are of those who, in opposition to it, advocate free sexual indulgence (Free Sex).

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 4, verse 26:

"Allah desires to make clear to you and to guide you to the ways of those before you, and to turn to you in forgiveness. And Allah is Knowing and Wise. And Allah desires to turn to you [in mercy], but those who follow their desires want you to deviate with a great deviation. Allah desires to lighten [the burden] for you, for man was created weak." (4:26-28)

Allah, glorified is His majesty, deals with His servants with great gentleness, and therefore He also explains to them the wisdom of His legislation openly. He tells them that the system of life He prescribes for His servants contains nothing but good for them and nothing but ease. By placing them in this distinguished and exalted position, He honours them: a position in which He Himself speaks with them, explains to them His legislative wisdom, and tells them that He is ready to discuss matters before them. (Verse) "Yurīdu Allāhu liyubayyina lakum" (4:26), "Allah desires to make clear to you": He intends to reveal to you His wisdom and understanding. He wants you to see this wisdom with your own eyes, to reflect upon it, and to accept it with your eyes open, your hearts willing, and your intellect acknowledging it. This is because the rulings of the Islamic system of life are not based on riddles and enigmas. They are not mere arbitrary commands devoid of wisdom or purpose. You can understand these rulings well, and you can also grasp the wisdom and philosophy that lies beneath them. You know well that Allah is Wise. This is a great honour for man, and only the one who truly knows the reality of divinity and the reality of servitude can know its true nature. In short, whoever possesses this understanding can comprehend this magnificence of Allah's generosity and this station of His kindness and grace.

(Verse) "Wa yahdīkum sunana alladhīna min qablikum" (4:26), "and to guide you to the ways of those who were before you": Thus, this is the methodology of life that Allah has established for all believers. It is a methodology whose foundations are very firm, whose principles are one, and whose aims and objectives are harmonious. This methodology is the system of life of the community of believers, in the past as well as in the future, and it is the methodology of the Muslim ummah, which has for centuries continued as one ummah.

Thus, in the sight of the Qur'an, all those who have attained the path of guidance are one, wherever and whenever they may be. The Qur'an further declares that in every age and every place the Islamic system of life has remained one. Likewise, on the long highway of life, the caravan of faith is also one, and it is in constant motion. This is the glimpse that grants a Muslim the awareness of what his reality is, what his ummah and party are, and what his methodology and way of life are. A believer comes to realise that he is a member of the ummah of those who believe in Allah, and that the bond linking this ummah is the "divine methodology" of life. Despite great differences of time and place, this bond endures, and despite differences of colour, country and distance, this relationship remains firm and lasting, and among the believers of every nation and every tribe this divine way (sunnah) serves as a strong bond.

(Verse) "Wa yatūba 'alaykum": "and to turn to you in forgiveness." Allah, glorified is His majesty, explains to you every matter in detail, and points out the good paths upon which those before you have walked. He does this because He is Merciful: He does it so that you may return, abandon the path of disobedience, and come onto the open highway of life that He has prepared for you in beauty, and He is also your helper in walking upon that path.

(Verse) "Wallāhu 'Alīmun Ḥakīm" (4:26), "And Allah is Knowing and Wise": Therefore, the legislation He is establishing for you is based upon knowledge and wisdom, and the guidance He is giving is based upon knowledge and wisdom. He is aware of your psychology, and your circumstances are within His sight. He also knows the measures through which your reform can be achieved, and which are beneficial for you. He is acquainted with the temperament of the Islamic system, and He knows well the method by which it is to be implemented.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 4, verse 27:

(Verse) "Allah desires to turn to you in mercy, but those who follow their desires desire that you should swerve away to a great deviation." (4:27) "Allah wishes to turn towards you with mercy, but those who follow their carnal desires want you to turn away from the right path and go far astray."

In this brief verse, within a single ayah, Allah has made clear what Allah desires for mankind, through what system, and by what means. And what are those doing who want to found the system of life solely upon sexual relations (sex), and who want to turn people away from the Islamic system of life? The truth is that whoever adopts any other way apart from the Islamic way has a system based upon desires. Only the Islamic system of life is founded upon seriousness, truthfulness, rectitude and a sense of responsibility. All the other systems are founded upon following the self, submission to lust, immorality and wickedness, crookedness and misguidance.

Allah is informing people well of His way and explaining His methods with clarity. So what is His purpose in this? Simply that He intends to show mercy and compassion to mankind. He points you to the right path. He makes you aware that along the paths of life there are particular places where there is a danger of slipping. He wishes to help you in elevation and progress, so that you may touch the heights of greatness. In contrast, those who keep their systems solely for the pursuit of lusts, and who prescribe for people systems of life based on lust and adorn them well, for which there is no room in the Islamic system of life, Allah has neither permitted them nor declared them lawful. These people only want Muslims to swerve from the right path and set out far onto the roads of misguidance, and to be deprived of the Islamic system of life and its supreme heights.

In this sphere of life concerning which guidance was given in the preceding verses, namely the consolidation of the family, the purity of society, the determination of the sole pure and clean method for relations between men and women, and the prohibition of sexual intercourse by any means other than this, and the creation of awareness of their condemnation and of their baseness in the thought and outlook of Muslims, what is Allah's plan in this sphere, which Allah approves, and what is the plan of those people who want to found human society solely upon lustful indulgence?

As for Allah's plan in this regard, its explanation has been given in detail in the preceding verses, from which it is apparent that Allah wishes to regulate this relationship between men and women, wishes to make this relationship pure, clean and sacred, and wishes to establish it in such a way that it is nothing but good for the Muslim community in every circumstance.

As for those who want only lustful indulgence, they only want these natural inclinations to be unrestrained in every way. There should be no religious restraint upon them, no moral restraint, and no collective restraint. They want this furnace of lust to blaze hotter and hotter without hindrance or check, and it should be so hot that every heart becomes restless, control over the nerves is lost, and in this way no home is at peace, no one's honour remains safe, the existence of no family remains, and humans become a herd of animals, and then their males pounce upon their females the moment they see them, with no rule for them other than strength, resources and scheming. Thus the whole society is shaken. Corruption is everywhere, and in the name of freedom evil and mischief are established everywhere. If the meaning of freedom is only this, then it is only freedom of lusts, and the system based upon it is purely a system of lust.

This is the misguidance and crookedness against which Allah warns Muslims. He cautions them about what the callers to this lustful system of life are inviting them towards. The callers to the lustful system were at that time striving to turn the nascent Islamic society back towards the system of moral lawlessness into which they had gone far, and because of the pure, clean and firm social system of Islam they had been left alone in it. This is the very goal towards which the misguided writers and literati of today are calling, and in which all of today's media and entertainment are busy day and night. They want to remove even the few modest barriers that exist in the Islamic society today against the path of animal lust. The truth is that only the Islamic system of life can deliver mankind from this animality, when the revolutionary forces of Islam, if Allah wills, establish this system in the world.

In the final glimpse of this concluding section, it is shown that man is a weak creature, and it is because of these very weaknesses that Allah has mercy upon him. Therefore, in the way of life He prescribes for him and in the law He makes, He takes his weakness into account, so He sends down light and easy commands, and instead of creating difficulties for him, He creates ease for him. He protects him from hardship, hardship and harm.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 4, verse 28 (part 1 of 2):

﴿Allah wishes to lighten your burden, for man was created weak.﴾ (4:28)

In the rulings, legislation and instructions concerning the family system given in the preceding verses, this lightening is clearly visible. For example, human natural inclinations and sexual desire have been acknowledged. Merely by regulating this impulse, one of its aspects has been turned towards constructive channels, and a pure and clean sphere has been set for its use. A pure and excellent environment has been created for it. And it has not been commanded that a person must suppress this natural desire, or eliminate it, or leave it so free that it falls to the level of animals, with no limit or restriction.

Beyond the family life, in the other spheres of the Islamic system of life too, ease and lightness in legislation is clearly evident everywhere. Human nature has been taken into account. The strength and capacity of man has been kept in view. Human needs and necessities have been kept in view, and all of man's constructive powers have been left free. Nevertheless, limits and restrictions have been set for their use, due to which the occasion for their misuse does not even arise.

Some people think that the restrictions Islam has placed on sexual relations between men and women are very difficult to observe, and that it is easy and pleasurable to go along with those who follow the principle of unrestrained lust. This is a great misunderstanding, because leaving sexual relations completely free, adopting mere sensual pleasure in the relationship between men and women, bringing sexual union in human society down to the level of sexual union among animals, thereby ending all duties, obligations and collective responsibilities, and freeing this relationship between men and women from every kind of restraint, whether moral or social, all these things may appear on the surface to be very easy, enjoyable and pleasing. But in the light of their real consequences, they are very heavy, crushing and destructive, and their evil effects on an individual and a society produce results that are extremely painful, deadly and ruinous. A glance at the conditions of those societies that have adopted this path of sexual freedom and have been freed from religious morality and the restraints of modesty makes the heart tremble, provided there is still a spark of life left in the heart.

Among the ancient civilizations that were destroyed in the world, the fundamental factor in their ruin was their sexual licentiousness. Whether this civilization was the Greek civilization, the Roman civilization or the ancient Persian civilization, the fundamental cause of the decline of all of them was their sexual licentiousness. Today, in our age, the collapse and disintegration taking place in Western civilization is also due to this sexual anarchy. Especially, the signs of destruction of today's French society are quite evident, which was the first to adopt this sexual anarchy. In other countries of modern civilization, America, Sweden, Britain and other so-called developed Western societies, signs of this disintegration have appeared. The signs of this sexual anarchy appeared in France much earlier. After 1870, in whatever wars France took part, it had to bend its knees before the enemy. All the evidence and proofs point to this: French society stands completely on the brink of destruction, and after the First World War these signs have become clearly visible. Maulana Maududi (rh) writes:

"The first result of this domination of sensuality is that the physical strength of the French is gradually giving way; constant sexual excitements have weakened their nerves. Bondage to desires has left them with little capacity for self-control and endurance. The abundance of venereal diseases has had a most deadly effect on their health. From the beginning of the twentieth century, the situation has been such that the French military authorities are compelled, every few years, to lower the physical fitness standard for new recruits, because the young men of the standard that existed earlier are becoming fewer and fewer in the nation. This is a reliable measure which, almost with the certainty of a thermometer, shows how rapidly the physical powers of the French nation are gradually declining. Venereal diseases are one of the important causes of this decline. In the first two years of the First World War, the number of soldiers who had to be given leave and sent to hospitals solely because of syphilis was 75,000. In a single medium-sized military garrison, two hundred and forty-two soldiers were afflicted with this disease at the same time. On the one hand, look at the gravity of that time, when the life and death of the French nation was at stake, and the utmost exertion of every single soldier was needed for its existence and survival. Every franc was precious, and every amount of time, strength and resources needed to be spent in defence. On the other hand, look at the youth of that nation: how many thousands of individuals, because of debauchery, not only became idle for many months themselves, but also wasted the wealth and resources of their nation on their own treatment in that critical hour."

A French expert in the field, Lirede, states that in France every year thirty thousand lives are lost because of syphilis and the diseases it produces, and after tuberculosis this disease causes the most deaths. This is the condition of only one venereal disease, and the list of venereal diseases is not limited to this one disease alone."

"In France, the annual average of men and women who enter the marriage bond is only seven or eight per thousand. This average is itself so low that one can easily gauge how large a portion of the population is unmarried. Then, of that small number who marry, very few are those who remain chaste and marry with the intention of living a pure moral life. Apart from this one aim, every other possible aim is before them. Indeed, among the common aims is this: that after a woman has given birth to a child out of wedlock, she marries so as to make that child legitimate. Thus Paul Bureau writes that it is a common custom among the working class of France that before marriage the woman takes a promise from her prospective husband that he will accept her child as his own. In 1917, before the civil court of the Seine, a woman gave a statement: 'At the time of marriage I had already informed my husband that the purpose of this marriage was only that the children born from our pre-marital free relations should be made "legitimate". As for whether I would live with him as a wife, that was neither in my mind then nor is it now. Accordingly, on the very day of the marriage, at half past five, I separated from my husband, and to this day I have not met him, because I had no intention of fulfilling the duties of marriage.'"

"The principal of a well-known college in Paris stated to Paul Bureau that generally young men keep in view in marriage only this purpose: that they may also engage the services of a mistress at home. For ten or twelve years they go about tasting freedom everywhere, then a time comes when, tired of this kind of unregulated, wandering life, they marry a woman so that the comforts of home may also be somewhat provided, and the enjoyment of unrestrained pleasure may also continue."

(See Al-Hijab by Maulana Sayyid Abul A'la Maududi (rh), Amir of Jamaat-e-Islami Pakistan, pp. 113–114; Sayyid Qutb (rh), see Parda, published by Islamic Publications, Lahore, 27th edition, pp. 91–95, Lahore, June 1985.) Thus France was destroyed, and as a result France suffered defeat in every war in which it took part. And now its condition is such that it is gradually disappearing from the stage of civilization and culture, and at any moment it will lose its very existence. This manifestation of the Divine Law (sunnah Ilahiyyah) takes place at a very slow pace. Although man acts hastily in every matter, the Divine Law has its own pace.

As for those countries that still appear powerful, or in which the signs of destruction and ruin have not yet appeared openly, their examples are these:

A journalist who recently visited Switzerland, discussing its socialist society, its collective facilities, its material progress and prosperity, expresses its freedom of love in these words:

"If our dream is that we want for our nation the same distinguished economic position that exists in those Western countries, and that, in accordance with those successful socialist tendencies, we eliminate the distinctions between the various classes of society, and remove from the path of every citizen of this country, Egypt, all those difficulties of life whose removal cannot even be imagined, if we reach this pleasant dream for the realization of which we are exhausting our full strength and all our possibilities, then the important question arises: will we also accept all the other consequences of this material progress? Will we be ready to accept the dark side of this ideal society? Will we accept free relations between men and women, and will we also accept their harmful effects on the family system?"

"Let us speak in the language of statistics. Despite the present encouragements for creating peace and tranquillity in life, and the recent efforts to form families, the population graph of Sweden is continuously falling, even though the present government is giving great assistance to a woman for marrying. Furthermore, the child of the woman is maintained free of cost until it graduates from university. Despite these facilities, every Swedish family is completely avoiding having children. The situation is the opposite: the number of those who marry is continuously decreasing, and the birth of illegitimate children is continuously increasing. Twenty percent of adult boys and girls do not marry at all. The industrial era in Sweden begins in 1870, and along with it the socialist era also begins in 1870. In 1870 the number of unmarried mothers was seven percent, while in 1920 this number became sixteen percent. I have not been able to obtain the statistics after that, but there is a continuous increase in them. According to the statistics published by academic institutions, it appears that men establish sexual relations at the age of eighteen and women at the age of fifteen, and by the age of twenty-one, ninety-five percent of young people have already established sexual relations. Further details show that seven percent of relations are with girls who are already engaged, thirty-five percent are with friends, and fifty-eight percent are with women who are casual acquaintances.
