Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 4, verses 41:

(Verse) "So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness, and We bring you (O Muhammad ﷺ) as a witness over these people? (41) On that Day those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth were leveled over them, and they will not conceal from Allah any statement." (42) (4:41-42)

"Then consider what these people will do on that day when We bring a witness from every nation and bring you (that is, you, O Muhammad ﷺ) as a witness over these people. On that day, all those who did not accept the Messenger's message and kept disobeying him will wish that, if only the earth would split open and they could sink into it. And there they will not be able to hide from Allah any of their words."

In the first verse, by way of introduction, it was said that Allah does not wrong anyone even to the extent of an atom's weight. Therefore, on the Day of Resurrection there will be complete justice, and not even a hair's weight of deficiency will be found in Allah's scale. It was also said that Allah will multiply good deeds many times over, and beyond that, Allah's grace and generosity will be shown to the believers. There will be Allah's mercy, but only upon those who deserve mercy, and there will be Allah's bounty, but only upon those who hope for Allah's bounty through their faith.

But what will be the condition of those others who did not present the capital of faith and did not accumulate the wealth of deeds? They accumulated disbelief and evil deeds. What then will their condition be on that Day? On the day when We bring a witness from every nation against that nation, and bring you, O Muhammad ﷺ, as a witness over the Muslim community.

Here the scene of the Resurrection comes clearly before the eyes. It is a vast field. All the nations are present in their places, and a witness will be presented over the deeds of each nation. These people who disbelieved, boasted, showed arrogance, were stingy, and called others to stinginess, who concealed Allah's bounty, who made a show of things and did no deed for the sake of Allah's pleasure. This depiction is such that from within the words it is almost as if we can see them. They stand in the field; the messenger of every nation is called to bear witness, and our Messenger ﷺ is also called. These people stand in the court of their Creator with their full disbelief, with all their hidden and open deeds, with their complete pride and arrogance, with their complete miserliness and their call to stinginess. They will be in the court of the Provider whose bounty they concealed and from whose provision they did not spend. Now before them stands that Day (the Resurrection) in which they did not believe. Then justice will be done in the presence of the very Messenger whom they denied. What then will their condition be?

Indeed these people will be afflicted with great shame and humiliation. Their heads will be bowed in shame and regret, and they will confess their sins, for denial will profit them nothing.

The words of the Qur'an do not describe these themes merely in an outward manner; rather, they are presented in the style of a psychological portrait, and the shadows of shame, disgrace and remorse are clearly visible upon these people. Let us observe the words.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 4, verse 42:

﴿On that Day, those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth were leveled over them, and they will not be able to conceal from Allah any statement.﴾ (4:42)

They will then be those who rejected the Messenger and persistently disobeyed him, and they will wish that the earth would split open and swallow them up.

Amid these glimpses of this vivid and dynamic mode of expression, we perceive all these meanings and see with the eye of imagination all the impressions that will show on the faces of those who stand in the Gathering. We find these impressions alive and moving, with a remarkably deep perception. Survey all the literary masterpieces of the world! You will not find in any narrative discourse or analytical writing the impression that the Qur'an, when describing the scenes of the Resurrection, adopts this particular style; and in some other passages of the Qur'an, too, examples of it are found.

The lesson of this discourse began with the theme that you should worship Allah and associate nothing with Him. Since prayer (salah) is the most tangible form of the worship and servitude of Allah, the next verse mentions some rulings concerning prayer. Along with this, some rulings concerning purification (taharah), which are preparation for prayer, are also stated.

This is also a link in the chain of training the Muslim community received, which the Islamic system of life raised up from the depths of jahiliyyah (the pre-Islamic age of ignorance). Alcohol drinking was a common and fundamental habit of the jahili society, and indeed it has been a distinguishing feature of both ancient and modern jahiliyyahs. When Roman society was at the peak of its development, alcohol drinking was among its most prominent characteristics. Likewise, among the important features of the jahili society of Persia, alcohol drinking was an important feature. Today American and European civilization and jahiliyyah are at their peak, and alcohol drinking is their most prominent attribute. Among the developed societies that have existed in Africa, this too has been an important feature.

Sweden is the most developed of today's developed jahili countries. In the second half of the last century, the situation there was that every family used its own specific alcohol, and each individual drank an average of twenty litres of alcohol. The Swedish government became concerned by these figures, because as a result people were becoming dangerously addicted to intoxication. The government adopted the policy of buying alcohol and storing it, and of trying to reduce the figures for individual consumption. Along with this, the government banned alcohol drinking in public places. But the government quickly retreated from its measures, and the restrictions imposed were relaxed. Alcohol drinking was permitted in hotels, on the condition that one could drink alcohol if one ate a meal. After this, permission was given at some public places, and this permission was granted only until midnight. After midnight, the use of nabidh (a mild fermented drink) and beer was permitted, but the habit of alcohol drinking among the youth continues to increase steadily.

In America, the government once decided to end this bad habit. In 1919 it passed the Prohibition law of alcohol. This law was called the "Dry Law," because it prohibited irrigation through alcohol. This law could only last fourteen years, and the government abolished it in 1923. In support of this law, the American government used radio, cinema, speeches, publication and the most modern means of propaganda. On publicity against alcohol alone, the government spent sixty million dollars at that time, and the books, journals and pamphlets that were published ran to tens of billions of pages. Because of the passing of this law, the government had to bear expenses in the form of compensation amounting to 250 billion pounds. Three hundred people became the prey of death. 335, 32 and 5 people were imprisoned. Fines of 61 million pounds were imposed, and property worth four billion and 400 million pounds was confiscated. But despite these measures, the government was compelled to abolish this law, and it retreated.

In jahiliyyah, alcohol drinking was a habit, but Islam ended it by revealing a few verses. This is the difference between the Islamic and jahili approach to the human soul and human society, and to the method of training. This difference existed in ancient times as well, and it remains in place today.

The question is: what was the state of alcohol drinking in the jahiliyyah before Islam? Its real condition will be known to the person who studies the poetry of the jahiliyyah somewhat deeply. Among literary subjects, wine has been the most important theme, just as it was an important characteristic of jahili life. Wine was sold in such quantities that the word for trade became specifically associated with the sale of wine rather than general trade. The famous poet Walid says:

"I spent many nights of revelry and story-telling, and wine came to me through merchants who had newly planted their banners over their colonies, and the prices of old wine rose very high."

Amr ibn Qami'ah says:

"Remember the time of youth, when, dressed in fine silk garments, I would go to my nearest wine-seller, and shake my long hair with the movement of my head, out of intoxication, wine and pride."

Verses on gatherings of drinking and poems of pride in drinking filled the poetry of the jahiliyyah, and this is one of its most important characteristics. Imru' al-Qays says:

1. "Morning came, and he bade farewell to wine. But as for me, I greatly love four qualities of life."
2. "The first of them is that I say to my boon companions, 'Be gentle,' while I pour out a brimming cup of wine."
3. "Another of them is that I spur my horse and, hurling arrows, swoop upon a herd of wild cattle grazing in complete peace and safety, startling them."

And Tarafah ibn al-Abd says:

"Were it not for three things which are the comforts of youth, by your head I would never have attended any gathering as long as I lived."
"Among them is that I take up, before the blaming women, a cup of liver-coloured wine which, when water is poured into it, foams up."
"I have ever been drinking wine, and my pleasure, my wealth, my spending of new and inherited possessions."
"Until my whole clan turned against me, and I was left alone like a mangy camel that is driven away."

And A'sha says:

"You surely know that I drink wine on days of rest and on days of travel."
"And I drink it in the green fields, in spring, for it has long been overcast in the green fields."

Mukhassal al-Layathi says:

1. "I have drunk wine with the small and with the great."
2. "When I am intoxicated, I am lord of the fortresses of Khawarnaq and Sadir."
3. "And when I am sober, I am lord of sheep and camels."

(Meaning: in the first line, he drinks in every gathering; in the second, when drunk he regards himself as lord of the castles and lives in luxury as a king; in the third, when sober he slaughters and herds sheep and camels.)

Regarding the various stages of the prohibition of alcohol, the events that occurred and the people connected with them, such as Umar, Ali, Hamza, Abdur Rahman ibn Awf and other well-known companions (may Allah be pleased with them all), show how widespread alcohol was before its prohibition. Especially in the jahiliyyah, some incidents are sufficient as examples from a large store.

Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), narrating his account of accepting Islam, said: "I was accustomed to drinking alcohol in the jahiliyyah. I thought I would go to a certain wine-seller and drink..." Even in Islam, Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) continued to use alcohol until this verse was revealed:

﴿They ask you about wine and gambling. Say: In both there is great sin and some benefit for people, but their sin is greater than their benefit.﴾ (2:219)

Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) then prayed: "O Allah, reveal for us a clear and sufficient statement about wine." He continued drinking until the explicit command of prohibition was revealed:

﴿O you who believe, wine, gambling, stone altars and divining arrows are an abomination from the work of Satan. So avoid it that you may be successful. Satan only wants to cause enmity and hatred among you through wine and gambling, and to prevent you from the remembrance of Allah and from prayer. So will you not desist?﴾ (5:90–91)

Upon this, Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said, "Yes, we have desisted, we have desisted," and after that he refrained from drinking alcohol. Regarding the verse ﴿O you who believe, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated﴾ (4:43), there are two narrations in which, from the Emigrants, Ali and Abdur Rahman ibn Awf, and from the Helpers, Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, were involved in the incident.

Ibn Abi Hatim, Yunus ibn Habib, Abu Dawud, and Mus'ab ibn Sa'd narrate from his father Sa'd that four verses were revealed concerning him. Once an Ansari prepared a feast; he invited some of the Emigrants and some of the Helpers. We ate and drank until we became intoxicated, and then we began to boast about ourselves. One man took the jawbone of a camel and struck Sa'd on the nose with it, so that Sa'd's nose was broken. This incident occurred before the prohibition of alcohol, and upon it this verse was revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated﴾ (4:43). This is a lengthy hadith which Imam Muslim narrated from Shu'bah.

Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Ammar, Abdur Rahman ibn Abdullah Dasht-ki, Abu Ja'far, Ata, and Abu Abdur Rahman (may Allah be pleased with them all), by way of chain, narrate from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) that Abdur Rahman ibn Awf (may Allah be pleased with him) prepared food for us. He invited us and gave us wine to drink; the wine took hold of us, and the time for prayer came. People put a certain person forward, and he recited: "Say: O disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship, and we do not worship what you worship." Upon this, from Allah, this verse was revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated, until you know what you are saying﴾ (4:43).

I believe that for proof of the abundance and wide use of alcohol in the jahiliyyah, there is no need to narrate more reports than these; these reports are sufficient. The practice of alcohol drinking and gambling was extremely widespread, and these two habits were among the most distinctive of the customs and traditions of the jahiliyyah.

The question is: how did the divine system of life deal with this distinctive and deeply rooted attribute and habit, and how was the calamity removed, the calamity which, while it existed, no serious, stable, righteous and wise society could possibly arise? How did Islam end this ancient and evil addiction at once, after which some parts were connected with collective social habits, and some parts were connected only with personal and national economics?

The Qur'an uprooted this evil habit through only a few verses: with great gentleness, great sympathy and great gradualness. Without any war being fought, without any battle having to be waged for it, and without any great sacrifice being made for it, or any bloodshed. If any sacrifice was made in this regard, it was only that the wine jars and goblets and flagons were broken, or the sips of wine that were in the mouths of drinkers were spat out, and no loss of life or property occurred. It should be remembered that some people, when they heard the verse on the prohibition of wine while they were drinking it, did not even swallow the sip that was in their mouths. The details are coming later.

In Makkah, where there was no Islamic government and the Muslims had no power, a passing reference was made to the Islamic view of wine. This reference was made incidentally within the context of the discourse, but it was only an allusion. For example, in Surah an-Nahl it says:

﴿And from the fruits of date palms and grapes you derive intoxicants and good provision.﴾ (16:67)

In this verse, Allah described wine, which they made from dates and grapes, in contrast with good provision. It was as if wine was not good provision, or was something separate from good provision. This was a distant hint, and through it a point was planted subtly in the consciousness of a young Muslim. But the habit of alcohol drinking was not merely an individual wrongdoing; it was a far greater and deeper social crime and an evil habit, and since it was also connected with economic matters, it could not be eradicated through such indirect hints.

In Madinah, where an Islamic state had been established and where Islam had authority behind it, even then Islam did not enforce the rulings on the prohibition of wine merely through the force of law in the form of a government decree. The greatest work in this was done by the persuasive power of the Qur'an. This process was begun with great gentleness and love, and it was begun on the basis of a deep study of human psychology. Moreover, it was carried out after collective matters, in accordance with the genuine demands of insightful wisdom. First of all in this regard, there comes this verse of Surah al-Baqarah:

﴿They ask you about wine and gambling. Say: In both there is great sin and some benefit for people, but their sin is greater than their benefit.﴾ (2:219)

This was the answer to a question, through which the conscience and awareness of the Muslims against wine and gambling began to be awakened.

This was the first bell sounded against wine-drinking in Islamic society. A tremor arose in the Islamic consciousness and sense, and Islamic understanding and perception were awakened against wine-drinking and gambling. It was made clear that in Islam the permissibility and prohibition of things rests on sin and reward. If the harm of a thing far outweighs its benefits and its sin is very great, then the path is that it should be made forbidden.

But this matter was very deep. People like Umar (رضي الله عنه) were addicted to wine. Upon the revelation of this verse, he (رضي الله عنه) prayed: "O Allah, give us a sufficient and healing explanation regarding wine." This prayer came from Umar (رضي الله عنه), and from it one can well gauge how deeply wine-drinking had penetrated the veins and marrow of the Arabs. After this came the events we have mentioned above, and after them this verse was revealed:

﴿O you who believe, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated﴾ (4:43). And this wise and insightful system of life continued doing its work, very gently. This was an intermediate stage. First, aversion was created against this abominable act, that it is a sin and an impure deed; but now a limited restriction was imposed, and the times of intoxication were restricted. This is because the times of prayer are very close to one another, and they spread over the whole day, and the gap between two prayers is not so long that someone could drink, have the intoxication wear off, and then pray in congregation and return in a state where he would have full knowledge and awareness of what he recites in the prayer. Since it is known that drinking wine has particular times, namely morning and evening: as soon as morning comes the time of prayer arrives, and in the evening too the times of three prayers come together. Therefore, the conscience of a Muslim had to decide whether to drink or to pray. And since prayer had by then become the central pillar of religion in their view, they would decide in favour of prayer. Yet despite this, Umar (رضي الله عنه) felt the need for a healing and sufficient explanation.

Time continued to move on in this way. Some further events arose, and the time came for wine-drinking to be absolutely prohibited. This was done in complete accordance with the Quranic system of life, and at a most fitting moment this decisive blow was struck against the habit of wine-drinking:

﴿O you who believe, indeed wine, gambling, idols and divining arrows are an abomination of Satan's work, so avoid it that you may be successful. Satan only wants to cause enmity and hatred to arise among you through wine and gambling, and to hinder you from the remembrance of Allah and from prayer. Will you not then desist?﴾ (5:90–91). (Those who believe and do righteous deeds: for them is forgiveness and a great reward (5:9).) All Muslims desisted from these things. The wine-skins were emptied, and wine jars everywhere were broken. This action was carried out merely upon hearing the verse, and those whose mouths held sips of wine spat them out, at the very moment they were drinking and the cup was at their lips. This was the victory and success of the Holy Quran and the success of the Islamic system of life. There was neither compulsion nor violence.

But how did this come about? By what means did this miracle take place, for which no parallel is found in human history? There is no example of it in legislation, codification and governmental measures, in any era or any age. Nevertheless, this miracle took place, because the divine system of life treated the human soul, in its own particular manner; it imposed divine authority over the human self, placed over it a watchman of God-fearing piety, and the fear of Allah is such a fear that whoever has it in his heart cannot for a moment, at any time or place, be heedless of it. This divine system of training takes the human being as a whole and trains him in a most natural manner.

The void that arose in their collective life because of the prohibition of wine, Islam filled by granting them certain lofty aims, and it left them no occasion, in their leisure hours, for the intoxication of wine or the display of ignorant pride and boasting, nor any need to act arrogantly in gatherings.

What were those lofty aims? For instance, Islam rescued this misguided and rejected humanity from the waterless desert of ignorance, its scorching noon, its darkest gloom, its contemptible slavery and the constriction of its narrow paths, and brought it into the fresh garden of Islam, its dense shade, its bright days, its honourable freedoms, and the vastness of this world and the Hereafter.

Islam filled that void in the lives of the Arabs with fresh faith. A new and tender consciousness arose in the hearts of the Arabs, which was most dear to them. Through it they no longer had any need to seek refuge in the embrace of wine-drinking, to find peace by being lost in false imaginings. Their hearts, with the torch of faith, soared towards the bright world of the exalted assembly, and they lived in the light of Allah, in union with Him and in His recognition. They tasted the delight of union with the Lord, and because of that delight they were casting upon the ground the sip of wine that was in their mouths, disregarding its intoxication and pleasure, and ultimately hating both its excitement and its calm.

Islam took the personality of a Muslim out from beneath the thick layers of ignorance. It opened for him paths which could not open without the key of Islam. He moved with his inclinations and tendencies and, walking upon the ways and paths of Islam, adopted a pleasing conduct: spreading light, giving new life, spreading cleanliness and purity, creating resolve and wakefulness, advancing towards goodness, and keeping before his eyes the covenant with Allah and the conditions of faith.

Wine is like gambling, and both are like the modern manifestations and spectacles of frivolous amusement: for example, the frenzied ways of gymnastics and their stadiums and other expenses, horse-racing competitions, cinema and the mixing of men and women, bull contests, and all the new forms of amusement that are the accessories of modern ignorance, which would more fittingly be called industrial ignorance.

All these phenomena are in truth manifestations of a spiritual void. They are a futile attempt to fill the deficiency of faith, the result of not keeping lofty aims and noble objectives before oneself. This is the proclamation that modern civilisation is an impoverished and empty-handed civilisation, and that within this modern culture the means for meeting all of man's needs are not present. It is precisely this spiritual void and this emptiness of lofty aims that makes people seek refuge in the lap of gambling and wine. Efforts are being made to fill this void with gambling, wine and other frivolous pursuits. Besides this, Western culture is filling this void with every kind of frivolity and unnatural activity, as we explained in detail above. These two matters are such that through them a human being becomes afflicted with countless psychological diseases and adopts moral waywardness.

These few words were the means through which the miracle of eradicating wine occurred. This was a system of life, a method, and this method was expressed in these words, and this method was devised by Allah, the Lord of the worlds. It was not devised by humans, and this is the distinguishing point between the systems of life made by people and the system that is made by Allah. It is evident that human systems do not succeed.

This is not merely a matter of speech and the manner of expressing an aim. For expressing what is in the heart there are countless styles. Some philosophers write very well, a certain poet composes very fine verse, or a certain one among thinkers is a writer of a very high order. This one is a king of literature and writes in such a way that he has a distinctive style; he is a master of ideas and the founder of a new branch of philosophy. But the words of such a person have no effect on people's consciences, because there is no power of divine inspiration upon that speech: "that for which Allah has sent down no authority" (Quran). The truth is that behind every matter there is a purpose which gives it force and grip; this is why every human way of life is weak, based on ignorance, full of defects, and founded on the personal desires of the human who made it.

I do not know when those people will realise this truth who devise for people's lives systems of their own, which are entirely separate from the system of Allah, the All-Knowing, the All-Aware; who make laws that the All-Wise and All-Aware did not make, and who erect for people signposts which the Creator of the heavens and the earth did not erect.

I do not know when these people will come to their senses. When will they give up this pride and arrogance of theirs? Now we come to the text of this noble verse:

﴿O you who believe, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated, until you know what you are saying, nor while you are in a state of janabah, except those passing through (the mosque), until you have washed yourselves﴾ (4:43).

Just as in the verse the believers are forbidden from prayer while in a state of wine-intoxication, so too they are forbidden from prayer while in a state of janabah, except for those passing through. Ritual bathing is obligatory in a state of janabah. There are various opinions regarding the meaning of the phrase ʿābirī sabīl (passing through). Likewise, there is also difference of opinion regarding the meaning of "do not approach prayer."

One view is that in a state of janabah one should not enter the mosque nor stay in the mosque until a person performs ghusl, except if someone is merely passing through the mosque. Some people's doors opened onto the Prophet's Mosque, and their route for coming and going passed through the mosque itself; such people were granted permission to merely pass through the mosque in a state of janabah, but not to stay there, and prayer was in any case forbidden to them until they performed ghusl.

According to another view, the meaning is that it refers to prayer itself. That is, it is prohibited to approach prayer in a state of janabah until one performs ghusl. However, if you are a traveller, then without ghusl you may enter the mosque and offer prayer, but after tayammum, which will serve in place of ghusl, just as when water is not available tayammum is permitted in place of wudu.

The first view is more apparent and easier to understand, because according to the second view, the case described is clarified in the following verse itself. If ʿābirī sabīl is interpreted as meaning travellers, then in that case there would be repetition, and repetition without necessity within a single verse would occur.

﴿And if you are ill, or on a journey, or one of you comes from the place of relieving oneself, or you have touched women, and you find no water, then take clean earth and wipe your faces and your hands with it. Indeed Allah is Pardoning, Forgiving﴾ (4:43).

This verse sets out rulings concerning the condition of a traveller: when a person comes to need ghusl, or needs wudu, and wishes to perform prayer... Likewise, if someone is ill and needs wudu or ghusl, or someone has come from relieving himself and needs wudu, or has touched women... in all these cases, if no water is found, he should perform tayammum with clean earth and then pray.

Al-ghā'iṭ means a low-lying place. Since rural people go to low-lying places for relieving themselves, the act of relieving oneself was expressed by the place of the act. And regarding the phrase lamastum al-nisā' (you have touched women) there are also several opinions: one view is that it means sexual intercourse, which makes ghusl obligatory. Another view is that it means actual touching, that is, one touches a part of a man's body to a woman's body. According to some schools of jurisprudence, this necessitates wudu, but according to some it does not nullify wudu; its details are found in the books of fiqh. Here we mention some results in summary.

(a) Touching in any case makes wudu obligatory.

(b) Touching makes wudu obligatory only when the one who touches experiences desire in his body, and it is also a condition that the woman touched is capable of arousing desire.

(c) Touching makes wudu obligatory only when the one who touches perceives that his self has been stirred by that touch.

(d) Touching does not make wudu obligatory in any case, nor does embracing or kissing one's wife make wudu obligatory.

Each of those holding these views has argued from the sayings and actions of the Prophet ﷺ, as is generally done in the derivation of legal rulings. In my view, by lamastum al-nisā' is meant, by way of metaphor, the act which makes ghusl obligatory; therefore there is no need to mention the differences found in the books of fiqh regarding wudu.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 4, verse 43 (part 3 of 3):

In all these situations, whether ghusl or wudu is obligatory and water is available, or water is not available, or its use would be harmful and it is not possible for a person to use it, then instead of performing wudu or ghusl, tayammum is permissible for the person. The mention of tayammum appears in the words of the verse: ﴿then seek clean earth and wipe your faces and hands with it﴾ (4:43). Tayammum literally means to intend, that is, to intend clean earth. Sa'id refers to anything that is of the kind of earth, such as soil, stone, or a wall, even if the soil is on the back of a riding animal, or on a floor or other things on which there is dust, and when a hand is struck on them, dust rises.

The method of tayammum is that one strikes clean earth with the hands, then shakes off the hands and rubs them over the face. Then one strikes a second time, shakes off the hands, and wipes them over the two hands up to the elbows. Or, with only one striking, one may wipe the face and both hands (according to the differing opinions of the jurists). Beyond this, there is no room here for further jurisprudential disputes, because tayammum was legislated purely for the ease of people, and this is a clear example of creating ease.

﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving﴾ (4:43). The purpose of this concluding statement is to show that Allah is gentle with His servants. He shows mercy to the weak, pardons faults, and forgives shortcomings.

Before we conclude discussion of this verse, it is necessary to reflect upon a few matters. The verse is extremely brief, but it requires consideration. For example, reflection on the wisdom of tayammum is necessary, to see how much leniency Allah has shown in our religion.

Some people, when they speak about the wisdom of the Islamic Shari'ah and the secrets of Islamic worship, go so far, and while stating the causes and reasons of rulings, give the impression as though they have exhausted all the secrets of the Shari'ah and that there is no need to seek any further wisdom behind these rulings and acts of worship. This manner of discussing Qur'anic verses, Shari'ah rulings and Islamic worship is extremely unhealthy. Yes, the matter is different if the cause and wisdom of a Shari'ah ruling are themselves stated and its explanation has been given by the Lawgiver himself. It is appropriate that we say: this is the matter which we have been able to understand as the wisdom of the ruling or as the cause of the ruling. There may be further secrets which Allah has not yet revealed to us. Only in this way can we keep human reason within its proper place with respect to the Shari'ah texts, without excess or deficiency, and remaining within its own sphere and limits.

I would say that some Muslims present verses and hadiths to people and also state their specific wisdom with them, and among these people are some sincere ones. This wisdom is based on human knowledge or on modern scientific discoveries. This by itself is not a bad thing, but this wisdom should remain within its limits. Those limits are the ones to which we have pointed in the preceding lines.

Very often it is mentioned that wudu before prayer has been made obligatory because it is a means of cleanliness. This purpose may indeed be in view, but to say that the sole purpose of wudu is cleanliness and nothing else would be an unhealthy mode of discourse, and in any case it is not a sound method of argument. This is because now there has come a time when some so-called intellectuals have begun to say that this was a very primitive concept and method of achieving cleanliness and that it is no longer needed. Nowadays other means of cleanliness and health are very common. Today people are making cleanliness and health part of their daily programme. If the purpose of wudu is only the attainment of cleanliness, then what is the need for wudu now, and indeed, then there is no need even for prayer.

Many people, regarding the wisdom of prayer, say that these are exercise movements in which the whole body moves. Some have written that because of prayer a person's life becomes organized and he becomes accustomed to living an organized life, since prayer is performed at a fixed time and within it there are bowing and prostration in a fixed manner. In it there are rows and leadership of the imam. There is also the wisdom that through prayer a person reaches God and there are intimate conversations with Allah. All these wisdoms may be intended, but we cannot say with certainty which of these wisdoms is meant or whether this very wisdom is the purpose. If we were to specify something definite and state it, this manner would be unhealthy, because a time has also come when some people have said that there is now no need for the exercise movements of prayer. Now exercise has become an art, and every person can practise it.

In the same way, it may also be said that now, merely for organizing life, we have no need of prayer, since life can be organized and made regular even more through a military system than through prayer.

Some people have even arisen who have declared that prayer is not needed for connection with Allah, since union with Allah is possible through solitude and meditation, and there is no need now for physical movements like prayer, because bodily movements sometimes obstruct spiritual contemplation and meditation.

If on these lines we were to specify the secrets and mysteries of every act of worship and every ruling, and begin to determine the cause of every ruling by our own understanding, or search for wisdoms within modern scientific discoveries, and then announce that this is the very wisdom contained in that ruling or this is its very cause and reason, then certainly we would depart from the healthy path and open the way for those who are so-called intellectuals. And then our own resolutions and decisions would not necessarily be correct. Error is also possible in them, especially when we link these wisdoms with scientific discoveries, because scientific sciences and theories change day by day, and at every time these theories are liable to correction and change, and this process of amendment and abrogation continues constantly.

The topic under discussion here is tayammum. From this it is evident that the wisdom of wudu and ghusl is not only cleanliness. If this were the case, tayammum would not have replaced them, because through it no cleanliness is attained. Therefore it is necessary that we seek some wisdom of wudu and ghusl other than cleanliness, which is present in tayammum as it is in wudu and ghusl.

We do not wish to commit ourselves the same error which we ourselves are pointing out. But we shall say that perhaps the wisdom is that a person should consider himself psychologically prepared for prayer. This preparation is based on a signal, and through this signal a person abandons his daily movements and rest and enters the atmosphere of presence and meeting before Allah's court, and wudu, ghusl and tayammum are the signals for this entry, and if wudu and ghusl are not possible, then tayammum itself becomes the signal.

The real truth lies in Allah's perfect knowledge which encompasses everything, which encompasses even the inner hidden matters of man. Only He is aware of the ways and hidden paths of man, He who is Subtle and All-Aware. Our duty is to obey the commands of Allah with utmost reverence and respect, He who is most exalted, high and great.

Here, our second point for reflection is that in the Islamic system prayer has very great importance. Islam strives to remove every kind of excuse and obstacle. Tayammum is a clear example of this series, that permission was given in place of wudu and ghusl when difficulties arise. This is a clear example from which it becomes known that Islam creates ease in every matter. For instance, if there is no water, or there is illness, or water is scarce and not beyond the needs of drinking. In travel, according to some opinions, tayammum is permissible even when water is present.

Keeping these matters in mind, and studying in this same surah the conditions of the prayer of fear, especially on the battlefield, it becomes easily evident how greatly the Islamic system of life gives importance to prayer. A Muslim cannot be separated from prayer in any state and for any reason. Even in illness, a provision has been made for performing prayer seated. In case of disability, it may be prayed lying on one side, and if movement is not possible at all, prayer can be performed even by a sign of the eyes.

This is a connection between God and His servant. It is a connection which Allah does not wish to be broken in any way for a believer, because Allah knows that the servant himself needs this connection. Allah is free of need from both worlds. The worship and prayer of people benefit Him nothing. The benefit, if any, is for the servant, who is composed through prayer. It is also a benefit for the servants that they establish a connection with Allah and seek help from Allah in their difficulties. They may attain inner joy, their bodies and personalities may be filled with light, they may have the awareness and feeling that they are under Allah's protection, near to Him, in His care, and on a path which is in exact accordance with their nature, because Allah has the most knowledge of the cause of their nature, and Allah also knows what is beneficial and what is harmful for them and for their nature. For He is the Creator and Fashioner, and He is more aware of His creations and products than anyone else. He is most subtle in observation and All-Seeing.

There is also a lesson in other expressions of this verse. Although it is an extremely brief verse, in it meanings flow in an excellent manner of expression. For the act of relieving oneself, the words ﴿or one of you comes from the place of relief﴾ (4:43) are used. It does not say that you have done this act, but only says that you have returned from a low place. The allusion and metaphor is that you have come from relieving yourselves. In this too it does not say to those addressed "you have come", but says ﴿or one of you has come from the place of relief﴾ (4:43). It does not say ﴿you have come from the place of relief﴾. The words of the Qur'an are more refined and courteous, and in them there is a subtle euphemism. The purpose is that people should conduct their conversation among themselves in this same refined manner.

Lesson No. 43

Commentary on verses 44 to 57

The nascent Islamic movement in Madinah was surrounded by hostile camps opposed to Islam, and with this lesson a confrontation with those camps begins. In this lesson, wonder is expressed at the crude tactics the Jews of Madinah were employing against this new religion and the community of Muslims. The next lesson explains the duties of the Muslim community, the nature of the Islamic system, the definition of Islam, and the conditions of faith, by which Islamic life and the Islamic system of living are distinguished from the lives and systems of other people. The lesson after that warns the Muslim community and commands it to take steps to establish the Islamic system, to correct its circumstances, and to protect its existence. It states that its hypocritical enemies are engaged in secret conspiracies against it. The Muslim community is told to attend to its internal differences and also to consider the defensive measures it must take against the hostile camps surrounding it. There are also certain instructions regarding international law in it. In the lesson that follows, the case of a Jew comes up, which was dealt with in the Islamic society rising above all enmities. In the lesson after that, shirk and the mushrikin are confronted, and the foundations on which the polytheistic society stood are described in a contemptuous manner. In the midst of this confrontation, some instructions regarding internal organization are also given, which relate to the themes at the beginning of the Surah concerning the family system. Now comes the last lesson of this part, which is specific to hypocrisy and the hypocrites. This lesson decides that the hypocrites will be in the lowest level of the Fire.

From these brief indications it becomes well understood how many-sided a struggle the Islamic movement faced at that time on its internal and external fronts, and how the first Islamic movement had to work simultaneously on internal and external fronts, because the internal and external fronts were linked and interconnected with each other. And this same struggle is faced by the global Islamic movement today, and will continue to be so in the future, because the foundation and reality of the Islamic movement is one.

(Verses) 44 to 46.

(Sami'na wa 'asayna) and (wasma' ghayra musma') and (ra'ina), whereas if they had said (sami'na wa ata'na) and (wasma' wanzurna), it would have been better for them and a way of uprightness. But they have been cursed by Allah for their baseless perversity, so they seldom believe.

In this Surah, of the several places where wonder is expressed, the first place of wonder is that its address is to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the People of the Book refers to the Jews, whereas in meaning all those who adopt a stance that is unique and wonder-provoking are included.

(Verse 44) "Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Book? They purchase error and desire that you too should lose the way."

Since they had been given the Book, it was fitting for them that they should accept guidance immediately. Musa (peace be upon him) was their great prophet, and Allah had given him the Torah so that he might bring them out of their error, and that it might be a light and guidance for them. But they deny this their destiny and have abandoned guidance and become purchasers of error. Purchase means that they have firmly resolved to take error; their intention is precisely this, and therefore they have abandoned guidance and preferred misguidance. Guidance is in their hands, yet they abandon it and take misguidance. It is as if they are making this bargain deliberately, not out of ignorance and mistake. Therefore such an act from an intelligent person is wonder-provoking, entirely unique, and deserving of reproach.

Yet despite this wonder-provoking state of affairs, they think that they are the guardians, whereas in fact they are engaged in the effort to make the guided people go astray, and to mislead those among the Muslims who are on the right path. For this very purpose they adopt many means and resources, the details of which have passed in Surah al-Baqarah and Surah Al 'Imran, and some examples of which come forward in this Surah too. The error they have purchased for themselves they are not content with; rather, they want to extinguish the light of guidance that has been kindled around them, and they are bent on erasing even its traces, so that neither guidance remains nor those who would be guided.

In this first and second glimpse, Allah the Exalted has warned the Muslims that the Jews want to play what game against you, and what measures they want to adopt against Islam. How fine a plan it is that Allah wants to instil hatred in the hearts of the believers against those who wanted to mislead the Muslims. At that time the Muslims took pride in this guidance, and they considered as their enemies those who wanted to snatch them from this honoured and proud position and return them to jahiliyyah, which they knew well, and which Islam also knew thoroughly, and whoever was returning them to jahiliyyah they regarded as very evil. In that age the Qur'an was addressing these people, being revealed according to Allah's knowledge, and it had worth and importance in the hearts of the Muslims.

Therefore after this the Qur'an explicitly tells that this is a conspiracy of the Jews, and it is made clear that these Jews are enemies of the Muslims. The believers are told that against their malicious endeavour they should rely only on Allah's guidance and support.

(Verse 45) "And Allah knows your enemies well, and Allah suffices as a Protector, and Allah suffices as a Helper."

Thus it is openly announced that between the Muslim community and the Jews in Madinah there is enmity, and that their respective lines become clearly defined. Although the expression of wonder concerns all the People of the Book, in this verse only the Jews of Madinah are meant.

The Word of Allah did not suffice with a mere allusion; rather, it mentioned the Jews explicitly and then described in detail their activities, their conspiracies, and their insolence towards the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. It appears that these events belong to the early period of the Hijrah, when Islam had not yet attained such strength and dominance in Madinah.

(Verse 46) "Among those who have adopted Judaism are some who displace words from their places, and who, twisting their tongues and attacking the religion, say (sami'na wa 'asayna) and (wasma' ghayra musma') and (ra'ina). Going beyond bounds in distorting the Word of Allah, they also insulted Allah's majesty, and in this way turned the straight meaning of Allah's Word into something else."

Among the preferred interpretations of the meaning of this verse is that they would alter the passages of the Torah in such a way that the meaning of its words would change. The principal aim of this distortion was to alter the proofs in the Torah concerning the prophethood of the Messenger ﷺ, and to change the rulings and laws that Islamic Shariah retained, and through which it became evident that the same source from which the Torah was revealed is the source from which the Noble Qur'an is being revealed, and as a consequence it was being established that the prophethood of the Prophet ﷺ is true. They would change those matters from their intended meaning so that the meaning became according to their desires. This characteristic is found in all those who deviate from their religion and make distortions so as to please those who hold power, or to please the common people who wish to free themselves from religion. The Jews have always been expert in this task, although in our age some people among the Muslims too have begun this work, and these people have surpassed the Jews even in this trait.

Then these people went so far in insolence toward the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that they said, "We heard and disobeyed," therefore we neither believe, nor follow, nor obey. This too shows that these verses were revealed in the early days of Madinah, when the Jews could have such fearless audacity against the Prophet ﷺ. After this outward denial they descended into extreme disrespect and extreme ill manners, and began to insult the Prophet ﷺ.

Outwardly they say (isma'), (listen), (ghayra musma'), you should not be given any such command as "listen." Outwardly this was a word of courtesy, and (ra'ina) meant "give us consideration, take our condition into account," that is, they are People of the Book, and they should not be invited to Islam in the same way as the general polytheists are invited. Through twists of language they would distort these real meanings, so that (ghayra musma') became to mean that no one should hear your words and you should not be able to hear. (May Allah disgrace them.) And they would derive the word (ra'ina) with arrogance. Such was their shamelessness, their lack of modesty, their disrespect, their twisting, their compromise, changing the meaning of words, and changing the place of words.

After mentioning these weaknesses of the Jews, the Qur'an explains that the Jews, being People of the Book and people of culture, had the duty to conduct themselves respectably and to speak within the bounds of courtesy, because those who have been given a portion of the Book should be far more refined than those who are not People of the Book. Having said this, they are given hope that if they accept guidance they will deserve good recompense, goodness and grace from Allah, provided they come onto the straight path. But their very temperament has not been of this kind, and Allah's curse has fallen upon them, and their condition is this:

(Verse 46 continued) "If only they had said, 'We heard and obeyed,' and (isma') and (unzurna), it would have been better for them and more upright. But Allah has cursed them for their disbelief, so they seldom believe."

But they do not speak plainly and definitively in the face of the truth. Had they accepted this truth clearly and spoken plainly, saying "We heard and obeyed," or saying "Listen, and please wait for us," it would have been better for them and more suited to their temperament, their psychology, and their circumstances. But because of their disbelief they flee from guidance, and few among them believe.

The word of Allah is very true. Very few among the Jews accepted the Islamic system of life, as the long history of Islam bears witness, and even this small number was the one for whom Allah had written this good in destiny, and had resolved that they would attain the path of guidance. This is because they struggled to reach the truth, and strove to attain guidance. As for the Jewish sect, it has been at war against Islam for fourteen hundred years. From the time Islam was revealed in Madinah, in their neighbourhood, until today, their conspiracies against Islam have never ceased, and the enmity they bear toward Islam has not ended to this day. Yes, its form, its colour, and its technical style have kept changing. And all the conspiracies carried out against Islam to this day, including the Crusades and modern imperialism, have had the hand of the Jews behind them, and these conspiracies have taken various forms. If not directly, then the share and hand of the Jews have certainly been present in them.

After this the address turns to the Jews, the People of the Book. They are invited to accept the Book which confirms the Book that is with them. They are severely threatened that if they turn away from accepting the truth without any cause, then because of their evil deeds Allah will disfigure them, turning their faces around, and a curse will fall upon them just as it fell upon those who violated the Sabbath. They are forbidden from committing shirk and are invited to accept pure monotheism, upon which their own religion too was founded. Allah does not forgive shirk, whereas all other sins may be forgiven; shirk is, in any case, a great sin.

Very few among the Jews accepted the Islamic system of life, as the long history of Islam bears witness, and even this small number was the one for whom Allah had written this good in destiny, and had resolved that they would attain the path of guidance. This is because they struggled to reach the truth, and strove to attain guidance. As for the Jewish sect, it has been at war against Islam for fourteen hundred years. From the time Islam was revealed in Madinah, in their neighbourhood, until today, their conspiracies against Islam have never ceased, and the enmity they bear toward Islam has not ended to this day. Yes, its form, its colour, and its technical style have kept changing. And all the conspiracies carried out against Islam to this day, including the Crusades and modern imperialism, have had the hand of the Jews behind them, and these conspiracies have taken various forms. If not directly, then the share and hand of the Jews have certainly been present in them.

After this the address turns to the Jews, the People of the Book. They are invited to accept the Book which confirms the Book that is with them. They are severely threatened that if they turn away from accepting the truth without any cause, then because of their evil deeds Allah will disfigure them, turning their faces around, and a curse will fall upon them just as it fell upon those who violated the Sabbath. They are forbidden from committing shirk and are invited to accept pure monotheism, upon which their own religion too was founded. Allah does not forgive shirk, whereas all other sins may be forgiven; shirk is, in any case, a great sin.

Lesson No. 43

Commentary on verses 44 to 57

The nascent Islamic movement in Madinah was surrounded by hostile camps opposed to Islam, and with this lesson a confrontation with those camps begins. In this lesson, wonder is expressed at the crude tactics the Jews of Madinah were employing against this new religion and the community of Muslims. The next lesson explains the duties of the Muslim community, the nature of the Islamic system, the definition of Islam, and the conditions of faith, by which Islamic life and the Islamic system of living are distinguished from the lives and systems of other people. The lesson after that warns the Muslim community and commands it to take steps to establish the Islamic system, to correct its circumstances, and to protect its existence. It states that its hypocritical enemies are engaged in secret conspiracies against it. The Muslim community is told to attend to its internal differences and also to consider the defensive measures it must take against the hostile camps surrounding it. There are also certain instructions regarding international law in it. In the lesson that follows, the case of a Jew comes up, which was dealt with in the Islamic society rising above all enmities. In the lesson after that, shirk and the mushrikin are confronted, and the foundations on which the polytheistic society stood are described in a contemptuous manner. In the midst of this confrontation, some instructions regarding internal organization are also given, which relate to the themes at the beginning of the Surah concerning the family system. Now comes the last lesson of this part, which is specific to hypocrisy and the hypocrites. This lesson decides that the hypocrites will be in the lowest level of the Fire.

From these brief indications it becomes well understood how many-sided a struggle the Islamic movement faced at that time on its internal and external fronts, and how the first Islamic movement had to work simultaneously on internal and external fronts, because the internal and external fronts were linked and interconnected with each other. And this same struggle is faced by the global Islamic movement today, and will continue to be so in the future, because the foundation and reality of the Islamic movement is one.

(Verses) 44 to 46.

(Sami'na wa 'asayna) and (wasma' ghayra musma') and (ra'ina), whereas if they had said (sami'na wa ata'na) and (wasma' wanzurna), it would have been better for them and a way of uprightness. But they have been cursed by Allah for their baseless perversity, so they seldom believe.

In this Surah, of the several places where wonder is expressed, the first place of wonder is that its address is to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the People of the Book refers to the Jews, whereas in meaning all those who adopt a stance that is unique and wonder-provoking are included.

(Verse 44) "Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Book? They purchase error and desire that you too should lose the way."

Since they had been given the Book, it was fitting for them that they should accept guidance immediately. Musa (peace be upon him) was their great prophet, and Allah had given him the Torah so that he might bring them out of their error, and that it might be a light and guidance for them. But they deny this their destiny and have abandoned guidance and become purchasers of error. Purchase means that they have firmly resolved to take error; their intention is precisely this, and therefore they have abandoned guidance and preferred misguidance. Guidance is in their hands, yet they abandon it and take misguidance. It is as if they are making this bargain deliberately, not out of ignorance and mistake. Therefore such an act from an intelligent person is wonder-provoking, entirely unique, and deserving of reproach.

Yet despite this wonder-provoking state of affairs, they think that they are the guardians, whereas in fact they are engaged in the effort to make the guided people go astray, and to mislead those among the Muslims who are on the right path. For this very purpose they adopt many means and resources, the details of which have passed in Surah al-Baqarah and Surah Al 'Imran, and some examples of which come forward in this Surah too. The error they have purchased for themselves they are not content with; rather, they want to extinguish the light of guidance that has been kindled around them, and they are bent on erasing even its traces, so that neither guidance remains nor those who would be guided.

In this first and second glimpse, Allah the Exalted has warned the Muslims that the Jews want to play what game against you, and what measures they want to adopt against Islam. How fine a plan it is that Allah wants to instil hatred in the hearts of the believers against those who wanted to mislead the Muslims. At that time the Muslims took pride in this guidance, and they considered as their enemies those who wanted to snatch them from this honoured and proud position and return them to jahiliyyah, which they knew well, and which Islam also knew thoroughly, and whoever was returning them to jahiliyyah they regarded as very evil. In that age the Qur'an was addressing these people, being revealed according to Allah's knowledge, and it had worth and importance in the hearts of the Muslims.

Therefore after this the Qur'an explicitly tells that this is a conspiracy of the Jews, and it is made clear that these Jews are enemies of the Muslims. The believers are told that against their malicious endeavour they should rely only on Allah's guidance and support.

(Verse 45) "And Allah knows your enemies well, and Allah suffices as a Protector, and Allah suffices as a Helper."

Thus it is openly announced that between the Muslim community and the Jews in Madinah there is enmity, and that their respective lines become clearly defined. Although the expression of wonder concerns all the People of the Book, in this verse only the Jews of Madinah are meant.

The Word of Allah did not suffice with a mere allusion; rather, it mentioned the Jews explicitly and then described in detail their activities, their conspiracies, and their insolence towards the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. It appears that these events belong to the early period of the Hijrah, when Islam had not yet attained such strength and dominance in Madinah.

(Verse 46) "Among those who have adopted Judaism are some who displace words from their places, and who, twisting their tongues and attacking the religion, say (sami'na wa 'asayna) and (wasma' ghayra musma') and (ra'ina). Going beyond bounds in distorting the Word of Allah, they also insulted Allah's majesty, and in this way turned the straight meaning of Allah's Word into something else."

Among the preferred interpretations of the meaning of this verse is that they would alter the passages of the Torah in such a way that the meaning of its words would change. The principal aim of this distortion was to alter the proofs in the Torah concerning the prophethood of the Messenger ﷺ, and to change the rulings and laws that Islamic Shariah retained, and through which it became evident that the same source from which the Torah was revealed is the source from which the Noble Qur'an is being revealed, and as a consequence it was being established that the prophethood of the Prophet ﷺ is true. They would change those matters from their intended meaning so that the meaning became according to their desires. This characteristic is found in all those who deviate from their religion and make distortions so as to please those who hold power, or to please the common people who wish to free themselves from religion. The Jews have always been expert in this task, although in our age some people among the Muslims too have begun this work, and these people have surpassed the Jews even in this trait.

Then these people went so far in insolence toward the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that they said, "We heard and disobeyed," therefore we neither believe, nor follow, nor obey. This too shows that these verses were revealed in the early days of Madinah, when the Jews could have such fearless audacity against the Prophet ﷺ. After this outward denial they descended into extreme disrespect and extreme ill manners, and began to insult the Prophet ﷺ.

Outwardly they say (isma'), (listen), (ghayra musma'), you should not be given any such command as "listen." Outwardly this was a word of courtesy, and (ra'ina) meant "give us consideration, take our condition into account," that is, they are People of the Book, and they should not be invited to Islam in the same way as the general polytheists are invited. Through twists of language they would distort these real meanings, so that (ghayra musma') became to mean that no one should hear your words and you should not be able to hear. (May Allah disgrace them.) And they would derive the word (ra'ina) with arrogance. Such was their shamelessness, their lack of modesty, their disrespect, their twisting, their compromise, changing the meaning of words, and changing the place of words.

After mentioning these weaknesses of the Jews, the Qur'an explains that the Jews, being People of the Book and people of culture, had the duty to conduct themselves respectably and to speak within the bounds of courtesy, because those who have been given a portion of the Book should be far more refined than those who are not People of the Book. Having said this, they are given hope that if they accept guidance they will deserve good recompense, goodness and grace from Allah, provided they come onto the straight path. But their very temperament has not been of this kind, and Allah's curse has fallen upon them, and their condition is this:

(Verse 46 continued) "If only they had said, 'We heard and obeyed,' and (isma') and (unzurna), it would have been better for them and more upright. But Allah has cursed them for their disbelief, so they seldom believe."

But they do not speak plainly and definitively in the face of the truth. Had they accepted this truth clearly and spoken plainly, saying "We heard and obeyed," or saying "Listen, and please wait for us," it would have been better for them and more suited to their temperament, their psychology, and their circumstances. But because of their disbelief they flee from guidance, and few among them believe.

The word of Allah is very true. Very few among the Jews accepted the Islamic system of life, as the long history of Islam bears witness, and even this small number was the one for whom Allah had written this good in destiny, and had resolved that they would attain the path of guidance. This is because they struggled to reach the truth, and strove to attain guidance. As for the Jewish sect, it has been at war against Islam for fourteen hundred years. From the time Islam was revealed in Madinah, in their neighbourhood, until today, their conspiracies against Islam have never ceased, and the enmity they bear toward Islam has not ended to this day. Yes, its form, its colour, and its technical style have kept changing. And all the conspiracies carried out against Islam to this day, including the Crusades and modern imperialism, have had the hand of the Jews behind them, and these conspiracies have taken various forms. If not directly, then the share and hand of the Jews have certainly been present in them.

After this the address turns to the Jews, the People of the Book. They are invited to accept the Book which confirms the Book that is with them. They are severely threatened that if they turn away from accepting the truth without any cause, then because of their evil deeds Allah will disfigure them, turning their faces around, and a curse will fall upon them just as it fell upon those who violated the Sabbath.
