(Verse 47–48)

The People of the Book are addressed by their attribute as People of the Book, because that attribute required them to be the first to accept the Islamic call and the first to become Muslims.

﴿O you who have been given the Book, believe in what We have sent down, confirming what is with you, before We obliterate faces and turn them back upon their backs, or curse them as We cursed the people of the Sabbath. And the command of Allah is always carried out.﴾ (4:47)

Since they had been given the Book, accepting guidance should not have been unusual for them. The same Allah who gave them the Book now calls them to faith, telling them to believe in this Book which confirms the Book they already possess. For them this should be no strange matter, since this Book also confirms their own scriptures.

Had faith depended on proofs or on apparent causes, the Jews would have been among the first believers. But the Jews fell victim to their particular interests and expediencies. Moreover, because of envy and enmity they could not believe. By their very temperament they were also rejecting people, with arrogance in their nature. The Torah itself described them with the words "a stiff-necked people." This is why they did not believe, and Allah's threat against them was severe and frightening.

﴿Before We obliterate faces and turn them back upon their backs, or curse them as We cursed the companions of the Sabbath.﴾ (4:47)

The meaning of "obliterating faces" is that the features by which a person is human are erased, and that faces are distorted and turned backward so that one walks backward. It is intended as a warning of a terrifying punishment, which includes compelling them to walk backward with their faces turned toward their backs. The curse that fell upon the companions of the Sabbath is also included in this punishment. (These were the people who tried to hunt on the Sabbath, though their law made that hunting forbidden to them.) For this crime, Allah in fact turned those people into apes and swine. It may also mean that Allah erases the traces of guidance and insight from their thoughts, hearts and minds, and returns them to disbelief and ignorance, that is, to the state in which they had no book of guidance, and that they then go from faith back into disbelief. Returning to disbelief after faith is in fact the distortion of faces, that is, going from guidance into error. And a person turning on his heels is worse than every kind of apostasy.

Whichever of these meanings is intended, it is in any case a terrifying threat and warning, and a fitting punishment for the harsh and arrogant temperament of the Jews. Likewise, it is a fitting punishment for their evil and corrupt deeds.

Out of fear of this threat, Ka'b al-Ahbar became a Muslim. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated a report through the chain: his father, Ibn Nufayl, Umar ibn Waqid, Yunus ibn Julays, Abu Idris, and Ā'idh al-Khawlani. He said that Abu Muslim al-Khawlani was the teacher of Ka'b, and he would rebuke him for delaying in meeting the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. They say Abu Muslim sent Ka'b to see the Messenger ﷺ, to see whether Muhammad ﷺ was indeed the one. Ka'b says: I mounted my mount and reached Madinah. Suddenly I heard a reciter reciting:

﴿O you who have been given the Book, believe in what We have sent down, confirming what is with you, before We obliterate faces and turn them back upon their backs.﴾ (4:47)

I fled, bathed in water, and passed my hand over my face to see whether my face had been distorted. After that I became a Muslim.

The final warning on this threat is: ﴿And the command of Allah is always carried out.﴾ (4:47) This is a repeated threat and warning, and it fits exactly the temperament of the Jews.

After this comes another threatening conclusion, concerning the Hereafter. Its purpose as a warning is that Allah never forgives the crime of associating partners with Him, while forgiveness is open for all other sins of every kind, provided Allah wills:

﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. And whoever associates others with Allah has certainly fabricated a tremendous sin.﴾ (4:48)

From the context it is implicitly established that the Jews too were afflicted with shirk, and so they too are invited to adopt pure monotheism and not to commit shirk. Here Allah does not mention any specific shirkiyah statement or act of theirs. However, other places in the Qur'an contain some details. The Qur'an mentions their belief that Uzair is the son of Allah, just as the Christians believed that the Messiah is the son of Allah. And it is clear that this is shirk. Likewise the Qur'an says that both groups, the Jews and Christians, "have taken their rabbis and monks as lords besides Allah." These people gave their rabbis and monks the right of legislation, and gave them the authority to make lawful and unlawful, although these rights are the exclusive rights of Allah and are the most specific domain of Allah's sovereignty. For this reason the Qur'an also regarded the People of the Book as polytheists. This viewpoint holds great importance in the Islamic conception of life, because it clarifies the definition of faith and its conditions, as the detailed discussion in this surah will show.

Furthermore, it should be kept in view that the Jews who lived in the Arabian Peninsula at the time of the Prophet ﷺ had polytheism entering their beliefs in many respects, and their practices were full of idolatry. These people had deviated from monotheism, so here they are sternly warned that Allah will never forgive shirk, although He forgives every kind of sin lesser than shirk. For a person who committed shirk in this world and died without repentance, there is no way to forgiveness.

Shirk is a great crime because it severs the link between Allah and the servant, and the polytheist has no hope that Allah will forgive him. If such people leave this world as polytheists with no connection to Allah, they cannot be forgiven. Whoever commits shirk and dies in that state of shirk, while the proofs of monotheism, the signs of the cosmos and the teachings of the Messengers are before him, will be among the people of Hell. Had there been even an atom's weight of good in him, he would never have done such a thing. The natural disposition that Allah gave him has been ruined by this crime, and that person has gone to the lowest rank and has, as it were, prepared himself for the fire of Hell.

As for crimes that are lesser than this clear, manifest, great, foul and open wrong, all sins, even if they are major sins, have the door of forgiveness open with Allah, provided Allah wills. These crimes fall within the bounds of forgiveness, whether the person repents and Allah forgives him, or without repentance they are forgiven on the Day of Resurrection, as some narrations state, provided the servant possesses within himself awareness of Allah's grace, hopes for His forgiveness, and is certain that Allah can forgive and that His forgiveness far exceeds his sins. This is the hope in Allah's mercy, which never ends and is never limited. It is a mercy whose doors are not closed, nor are there gatekeepers at those doors.

Imam al-Bukhari and Imam Muslim both narrated from Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him), through the chain: Qutaybah, Jarir ibn Abd al-Hamid, Abd al-Aziz ibn Rafi, Zayd ibn Wahb. He says: I went out one night and saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ walking alone, with no person accompanying him. I thought that perhaps the Messenger ﷺ did not like anyone to follow him. Still I kept walking in the shadow of the moon. He turned and saw me and said: "Who is that?" I said: "Abu Dharr, may Allah make me your ransom." He said: "Abu Dharr, come." I walked with him for a while. Then he said: "Sit here." He seated me in an open place surrounded by stones, and said: "Sit here until I return." Then he went ahead into the valley until he was out of my sight. He stayed away a long time, until the waiting grew long. Then I heard his voice coming back, and he was saying: "Even if he committed fornication and even if he stole." When the Messenger ﷺ returned, I could not help asking: "O Messenger of Allah, may Allah make me your ransom, with whom were you speaking in that valley? I heard someone speaking with you." He said: "That was Jibril. He met me at the valley's edge and said to me: 'Give your Ummah the glad tidings that whoever of them dies without associating anything with Allah will enter Paradise.' I said: 'O Jibril, even if he committed fornication and stole?' He said: 'Yes.' I said again: 'Even if he stole and committed fornication?' He said: 'Even if he stole, committed fornication and drank wine.'"

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated with his chain from Jabir ibn Abd Allah (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger ﷺ said: Whoever dies without associating anything with Allah, forgiveness for him becomes permissible: if Allah wills He will punish him, and if Allah wills He will forgive him. Allah never forgives that anything be associated with Him; apart from that, He forgives whom He wills.

Ibn Abi Hatim (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated with his chain from Ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with him). He said: "We, the companions of the Messenger ﷺ, had no doubt about those who take a soul unjustly, who consume the property of orphans, who accuse chaste women, or who give false testimony (that they are people of Hell), until this verse was revealed: 'Allah does not forgive that anything be associated with Him, and He forgives whom He wills other than that.' After that, the companions of the Messenger ﷺ stopped giving testimony."

Tabarani narrated with his chain from Ikrimah (may Allah be pleased with him), from Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah the Exalted has said: whoever knows that I am able to forgive sins, I will forgive his sins, and I do not care, so long as he does not associate anything with Me."

In this last hadith there is a thought-provoking lesson for us. The primary importance lies in the fact that within the heart, behind goodness, hope, fear and modesty, there must be a true awareness of Allah. When a person commits a sin, this awareness, and the good impulse based upon it, along with hope, fear and modesty, produce God-fearing consciousness in him, and he becomes worthy of forgiveness.

Now the Qur'an advances further and launches an attack on the Muslim community against the Jews. At the same time it brings forward another surprising aspect of these people: that these Jews still regard themselves as the chosen people of Allah, praise themselves, and recount tales of their own purity and chastity, while their condition is that they alter words from their real meaning and show disrespect toward Allah and His Messenger. Yet they themselves believe in jibt (every kind of superstition) and taghut, as will come forward, and by proclaiming their own purity and calling themselves beloved of Allah, even though they are evildoers, they fabricate lies against Allah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 4, verses 49–50:

(Verses) 49 to 50.

The Jews have an ancient claim that they are the chosen and favoured people of Allah. There was a time when Allah chose them to bear this trust and for the duties of prophethood and da'wah (the call to Islam). For their sake Allah destroyed Pharaoh and his companions, and He made the Children of Israel the inheritors of the holy land. But in the periods that followed, they completely abandoned the Islamic system. They began to commit great acts of disobedience and grave sins on this earth, and the earth itself began to tremble from these sins. Their ahbar (rabbis) and scholars declared lawful for them those things that Allah had made unlawful, and declared unlawful for them those things that Allah had made lawful. They began to follow these rabbis in these wrong practices, and the rabbis, who had claimed a kind of divinity, were not opposed by them, although the determination of what is lawful and unlawful belongs to Allah alone. The rabbis changed the Shari'ah of Allah in order to please kings and nobles, and they followed and flattered the inclinations and tendencies of the common masses. This is why they had, in effect, taken these people as their lords. Then they began to consume interest (riba). Their bond with their religion and with their Lord became weak. Despite these crimes and countless other crimes, they still remain persistently in the delusion that they are the favoured nation of Allah, and that the Fire will touch them only for a few days, and that only Jews are deserving of salvation in the sight of Allah. It is as if religion has become limited to kinship, or as if personal relationships and friendships operate even in religion, from which Allah is far exalted. This is because Allah has no kinship or relationship with any of His servants. The bond of Allah's servants can remain only through correct beliefs, through righteous deeds, and through steadfastness upon the Islamic system of life. Whoever disrupted this bond incurred the wrath of Allah. Allah's wrath becomes especially intense when He guides a misguided people, but that people then chooses the path of deviation against guidance. The circumstances of these Jews are not different from those of today's so-called Muslims, who think that they are among the ummah (community) of Muhammad, and that Allah will surely help them and expel the Jews from their land, while they themselves have completely departed from Islam, although Islam is their religion and system of life. But they have removed it from their lives, and they do not judge according to the Book of Allah, neither in their disputes, nor in their economic matters, nor in their collective affairs, nor in their manners and customs. Their Islam has remained limited to bearing names like those of Muslims, and to the fact that they were born in Muslim lands, in which they once lived and in which they once established the religion of Islam and made all decisions according to the Islamic system.

Allah expresses amazement before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that these Jews are strange, for they consider themselves an extremely pure people. But the condition of today's Muslims is even more astonishing than this amazing situation, because their moral state has fallen even lower than that of the Jews of that era.

It is not the task of people to pose like Miyan Mittu and proclaim their own chastity, and to give this testimony in their own favour, that they are righteous, close to Allah, and chosen. Rather, it is Allah's task to decide who is pure and favoured in His sight. This is because He knows hearts and deeds thoroughly, and He does not wrong people even to the extent of an atom's weight. If they turn sincerely to Allah, perform righteous deeds, and abandon these random arrows and guesses, and if they abandon their claims and act with extreme modesty and shame, without propaganda about their own purity and without pride and arrogance, then in Allah's sight none of their deeds will be lost, no deed will be dropped from the reckoning because of forgetfulness or error, and none of their rights will be usurped.

Allah Himself testifies against the Jews, that their claims to be a favoured people, and that Allah is definitely pleased with them, are a great fabrication against Allah. Allah condemns this false claim of theirs and thus dismisses it in the eyes of the people.

﴿انظر كيف يفترون على الله الكذب وكفى به إثما مبينا﴾ (4:50)

"See how they invent lies against Allah, and that alone is sufficient as a clear sin."

Let us think for a moment: we who claim to be Muslims, merely because our names are like those of Muslims, and because we live in lands where Muslims once lived, how great a lie this is. We do not implement Islam in any sphere of our lives, yet we claim to be Muslims. In our conduct and appearance we distort the image of Islam, and through our practical lives we bear witness against Islam. Yet even so we claim to be a favoured people and followers of the Prophet (ﷺ), although through our practical lives we have completely expelled Islam. I believe that our situation is not different from the situation toward which Allah turns the attention of Muhammad (ﷺ) with amazement, and about those who make such claims He says that they fabricate against Allah and commit a great sin, we seek refuge in Allah.

Remember that the religion of Allah is a system of life, and obedience to Allah means that the rule of this system is established throughout the whole of life. Nearness to Allah will be attained only when Allah is obeyed. Reflect for a moment on how far we are from Allah, from His religion, and from His system of life. Then also reflect that our condition and the condition of the Jews are exactly alike, and that Allah and His Messenger are amazed at their condition. Their baseless claim has been described as a fabrication against Allah. Therefore the rule that applies to the Jews will apply to us, and our condition will be the same as theirs. And remember that Allah has no kinship with anyone, and no friendship with anyone.

The discourse continues, as before, about those people who consider themselves favoured, although they believe in falsehood in opposition to truth, accept rulings that are not authentic according to the Shari'ah, and for these rulings there is no principle that can restrain them from oppression and transgression. This is belief in al-jibt wal-taghut (false deities and tyrannical powers). At the same time they also testify on behalf of polytheism and polytheists, that these people are more guided than the Muslims, although the people of faith believe in the Book of Allah, the Shari'ah of Allah, and His system of life. After mentioning their amazing condition and their misguidance, Allah severely criticizes these people and disgraces and humiliates them. The hidden corners of their character are unveiled, that they are extremely envious and miserly. The reasons are given for their deviation from the religion of Ibrahim and their adoption of their present stance, although they were extremely proud of the religion of Ibrahim, and they were also extremely proud of their genealogy traced to Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him). This criticism concludes with the definitive decision that the blazing Fire of Hell is sufficient for them.

It is not the task of people to pose like Miyan Mittu and proclaim their own chastity, and to give this testimony in their own favour, that they are righteous, close to Allah, and chosen. Rather, it is Allah's task to decide who is pure and favoured in His sight. This is because He knows hearts and deeds thoroughly, and He does not wrong people even to the extent of an atom's weight. If they turn sincerely to Allah, perform righteous deeds, and abandon these random arrows and guesses, and if they abandon their claims and act with extreme modesty and shame, without propaganda about their own purity and without pride and arrogance, then in Allah's sight none of their deeds will be lost, no deed will be dropped from the reckoning because of forgetfulness or error, and none of their rights will be usurped.

Allah Himself testifies against the Jews, that their claims to be a favoured people, and that Allah is definitely pleased with them, are a great fabrication against Allah. Allah condemns this false claim of theirs and thus dismisses it in the eyes of the people.

﴿انظر كيف يفترون على الله الكذب وكفى به إثما مبينا﴾ (4:50)

"See how they invent lies against Allah, and that alone is sufficient as a clear sin."

Let us think for a moment: we who claim to be Muslims, merely because our names are like those of Muslims, and because we live in lands where Muslims once lived, how great a lie this is. We do not implement Islam in any sphere of our lives, yet we claim to be Muslims. In our conduct and appearance we distort the image of Islam, and through our practical lives we bear witness against Islam. Yet even so we claim to be a favoured people and followers of the Prophet (ﷺ), although through our practical lives we have completely expelled Islam. I believe that our situation is not different from the situation toward which Allah turns the attention of Muhammad (ﷺ) with amazement, and about those who make such claims He says that they fabricate against Allah and commit a great sin, we seek refuge in Allah.

Remember that the religion of Allah is a system of life, and obedience to Allah means that the rule of this system is established throughout the whole of life. Nearness to Allah will be attained only when Allah is obeyed. Reflect for a moment on how far we are from Allah, from His religion, and from His system of life. Then also reflect that our condition and the condition of the Jews are exactly alike, and that Allah and His Messenger are amazed at their condition. Their baseless claim has been described as a fabrication against Allah. Therefore the rule that applies to the Jews will apply to us, and our condition will be the same as theirs. And remember that Allah has no kinship with anyone, and no friendship with anyone.

The discourse continues, as before, about those people who consider themselves favoured, although they believe in falsehood in opposition to truth, accept rulings that are not authentic according to the Shari'ah, and for these rulings there is no principle that can restrain them from oppression and transgression. This is belief in al-jibt wal-taghut (false deities and tyrannical powers). At the same time they also testify on behalf of polytheism and polytheists, that these people are more guided than the Muslims, although the people of faith believe in the Book of Allah, the Shari'ah of Allah, and His system of life. After mentioning their amazing condition and their misguidance, Allah severely criticizes these people and disgraces and humiliates them. The hidden corners of their character are unveiled, that they are extremely envious and miserly. The reasons are given for their deviation from the religion of Ibrahim and their adoption of their present stance, although they were extremely proud of the religion of Ibrahim, and they were also extremely proud of their genealogy traced to Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him). This criticism concludes with the definitive decision that the blazing Fire of Hell is sufficient for them.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 4, verse 51–55 (part 1 of 2):

Verses 51 to 55.

Those who were given the Book have more right that they should believe in this final Book, the Qur'an, and refrain from shirk, which is the practice of those who have received no Book of guidance from Allah. They should judge in their lives according to the Book of Allah, and not obey the taghut (taghut is every law that is not from Allah and every command for which there is no legitimate sanction behind it). But the Jews, who were constantly narrating tales of their purity and were proud that they were the beloved servants of Allah, alongside these claims were followers of falsehood and shirk. They obeyed soothsayers and obeyed their rabbis (ahbar), who made for them laws for which Allah had given no authority. They believed in the taghut (taghut is the system of government and legal system that is not based on the Shari'ah). It is called taghut because there is in it tyranny (taghyan) and overreaching. For example, a human being claims for himself those attributes which are the essential attributes of Allah's divinity and sovereignty, and this person removes himself from obedience to the code of the Shari'ah, according to which it was obligatory for him to act justly. This is an act of tyranny, and such a person is taghut, and those who obey this taghut and believe in him are mushrikun or kafirun. Allah expresses astonishment at such people, that they commit this abhorrent act despite having been given the Book before, yet they did not follow that Book.

Furthermore, in addition to believing in jibt (all kinds of superstitions) and taghut, they went and stood in the ranks of the disbelievers and polytheists, and lined up against the Muslims to whom Allah has given the Book.

﴿And they say to those who disbelieve: "These are better guided in the way than those who believe."﴾ (4:51)

Ibn Ishaq narrated, through Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, Ikrimah and Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them all), that among the people of Quraysh, Ghatafan and Banu Qurayzah who had gathered all the parties and confederates in the Battle of the Confederates were Huyayy ibn Akhtab, Sallam ibn al-Haqiq, Abu Rafi', Rabi' ibn al-Haqiq, Abu 'Amir, Wahwah ibn 'Amir and Hawdhah ibn Qays. When these people came to Quraysh they said: "These people are the rabbis and scholars of the Jews, and they are the scholars experts in the first Book. Ask them whatever you wish to ask, whether your religion is better or the religion of Muhammad (ﷺ)." Quraysh asked them, and they replied: "Your religion is better than the religion of Muhammad, and those who have followed Muhammad are more upon guidance than you." Upon this, Allah revealed this verse.

﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Book...﴾ up to ﴿and We gave them a great kingdom﴾ (4:54). This is a rebuke upon them and an announcement that neither in this world nor in the Hereafter will they have any helper or supporter. These people now seek help from the polytheists. They called the polytheists more guided so that they might incline them to aid them. Accordingly, the polytheists accepted their invitation, and on the Day of the Confederates these people came with their armies. In that battle, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his noble Companions (may Allah be pleased with them all) dug a trench around Madinah, and the averting of that great calamity from them was by Allah alone; and Allah returned those who disbelieved with their rage, and they did not obtain any good, and Allah sufficed the believers in fighting, and Allah is ever Strong and Mighty.

It was astonishing that the Jews should resort to saying that the religion of the polytheists is better than the religion of Muhammad (ﷺ) and his companions, and that the polytheists are more guided than those who believe in the Book of Allah and His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ). But this is no unusual thing from the Jews. Between truth and falsehood they have always preferred falsehood, and among the people of truth and the people of falsehood, they have always found the people of falsehood pleasing. They are so greedy that there is no limit to it. They have become so entangled in self-interest that it is impossible for moderation to come into their temperament. Their breasts are full of malice that can never be cleansed. They do not find in the people of truth the means to satisfy their desires, their greed and their avarice. If they receive anything, they always receive it from the people of falsehood. Therefore they are always accustomed to giving false testimony against the testimony of truth, and they bear witness for the people of falsehood against the people of truth.

These are their enduring conditions and habits. The causes behind these conditions still exist, because this act was their natural and logical act: that they should testify about the disbelievers that they are more upon guidance than the believing Muslims.

Today the Jews openly say that through their power, which is in their hands by means of the media, they can make fail every movement that succeeds on this earth, and in this regard they give full support to the people of falsehood so that they may defame and destroy the Islamic movement. And they adopt this secrecy because if they come out openly, then in the modern age the veil of their deception is torn, and their agents, who in reality work on their signals and day and night labour to uproot Islamic movements everywhere from root and branch, become disgraced among the masses.

Indeed, sometimes their cunning and cleverness reach such a point that they outwardly display enmity toward their agents and appear to fight with them, but in reality they are helpers of those who are engaged in eliminating Islamic movements and are erasing the truth. Sometimes they start a false fight with their agents who work only for speech and words, so that they may fulfil their far-reaching aims. They never abandon the work of distorting the image of Islam and the Muslims, because their real hatred is toward the Islamic way of life, and their real enmity is with every movement for the revival of Islam that is visible to them from afar and that they cannot deceive.

This is one and the same nature, one and the same plan, and one and the same aim. This is why an announcement is made from Allah that these people are rejected and cursed. They are declared to be cast out from the court of Allah, and a decision is made that for them there shall be no victory and no one shall help them.

﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has cursed, and whoever Allah curses, you will not find for him any helper.﴾ (4:52)

Today it appears horrifying to us that all Western countries are supporters and helpers of the Jews. Therefore the question arises: where then is Allah's promise that He cursed the Jews, and whom Allah has declared cursed will have no helper?

The truth is that the true helper is Allah alone. True helpers are not people, nor are governments, even if they possess atomic bombs, hydrogen bombs and missiles. The true helper is Allah, and He has control over all His servants, and the bombs and missiles are with people who are under Allah's complete control. Allah alone is the true helper of those who help Him. ﴿And Allah will surely support those who support Him﴾ (4:... ) Allah helps only those who believe in Him in the manner that belief is due, and who obey His system in the manner that obedience is due, and who, in submission and contentment, make all their decisions according to the Islamic method and the Islamic Shari'ah.

Through these verses Allah addressed a community which had truly come to believe in Allah. It was obedient to the Islamic system of life; it judged all its matters according to the Shari'ah. Allah had weakened the Jews, its enemies, in comparison with this believing community, and at that time the believers received help against the Jews and gained victory, because they had no supporter. Allah gave practical form to His promise to them, and Allah's promise takes practical form only through those who are truly believers.

We should not, at this time, be alarmed by the unanimous backing of the Jews by all atheists, polytheists and the people of the Cross, because they have been helpers of the Jews against Islam in every age. This is nothing new. But let us not be deceived by it. The promise of help is only for the believers. Whenever we become believers, victory will kiss our feet.

Let the Muslims undertake an experiment: let them become true Muslims, and then see whether any helper for the Jews remains in this world, and whether the support of these polytheists and the people of the Cross benefits the Jews at all.

After describing the conditions, positions and statements of the People of the Book, and expressing astonishment at them and declaring them humiliated and cursed, the passage now objects that their stance regarding Muhammad (ﷺ) and the Muslims is open to censure. Furthermore, they are enraged that Allah bestowed this favour upon the Messenger (ﷺ) and the Muslims, granting them religion, support and victory; and even when Allah poured out His bounty upon them, they were consumed with jealousy. Yet nothing good or benefit had been snatched from them to give to the People of Islam. This shows how harsh of temperament and how greedy these people were. They could not bear that anyone other than themselves should receive anything. Yet Allah had also bestowed His mercy upon them, showed favour to their forefathers, and had not forbidden them generosity and tolerance, nor taught them this malice and envy.

﴿Or do they have a share in the kingdom? Then they would not give the people even a speck.* Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty? We had already given the family of Ibrahim the Book and wisdom, and We gave them a great kingdom.﴾ (4:53–54)

It is most astonishing that these people cannot even bear that Allah should bestow His favours upon anyone else from His treasures. Are these people partners with Allah in His inexhaustible treasures? Are they partners with Allah in His sovereignty? It is Allah alone who gives, and it is He who withholds. If this were so, these people, because of their stinginess and harshness, would not give anyone even a speck. Naqir refers to the thin membrane that is on the back of a date stone. The stinginess and avarice of the Jews would not permit them to give anyone even that much, if they had any share in the kingdom of Allah. Thanks be to Allah that they have no share in His divinity. If it were so, even if all people were to perish of hunger, they would not give anyone even the husk of a date stone.

Perhaps they envy the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) because Allah bestowed upon him His bounty, giving him this religion through which those Arabs received a new birth, began to progress afresh, and turned those ignorant Arabs into a distinguished people and nation; He gave them light, certainty, tranquillity and confidence, and gave them purity, cleanliness and power in the world. Certainly this state of affairs is the cause of the Jews' envy. They were consumed with the thought that their literary, cultural and economic superiority over the ignorant, divided, mutually conflicting Arabs was about to end. This superiority had existed at a time when they possessed no religious message.

Why do they envy that Allah should grant prophethood and supreme authority on earth to a people, when upon them too this favour and grace had continued since the time of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), to whom Allah gave the Book and wisdom (prophethood)? Prophethood continued among his descendants, and they were also given rule and sovereignty; yet they did not value that favour. They did not preserve that blessing, nor did they keep the ancient covenant they had made with Allah; rather, many of them were not believers at all. For those upon whom such great favour was bestowed, it is not fitting that disbelievers and unbelievers should arise among them.

﴿For We had already given the family of Ibrahim the Book and wisdom, and We gave them a great kingdom. Among them were some who believed in it, and among them were some who turned away from it. And sufficient is Hell as a blazing fire.﴾ (4:54–55)

Upon whom does the pain of envy fall? If a destitute person envies a wealthy possessor of blessings, this envy too is a wicked act. But if a wealthy possessor of blessings begins to envy someone, this is a depravity more profound than baseness, and this kind of evil and corruption is the portion of the Jews alone. This is why they have been threatened with the fire of Hell, which is a most fitting recompense for this baseness.

﴿And sufficient is Hell as a blazing fire.﴾ (4:55)

When the discussion reached the point that among the family of Ibrahim some people became believers while others barred people from the way of Allah, it became necessary that the end of the believers be stated, and that the end of those who bar people from the path of faith also be stated. This recompense and punishment has always remained the same in every religion, and in the Holy Quran Allah Almighty describes it in the form of the Day of Resurrection with extremely severe and terrifying scenes.

Prophethood continued among his descendants, and they were also given rule and sovereignty; yet they did not value that favour. They did not preserve that blessing, nor did they keep the ancient covenant they had made with Allah; rather, many of them were not believers at all. For those upon whom such great favour was bestowed, it is not fitting that disbelievers and unbelievers should arise among them.

﴿For We had already given the family of Ibrahim the Book and wisdom, and We gave them a great kingdom. Among them were some who believed in it, and among them were some who turned away from it. And sufficient is Hell as a blazing fire.﴾ (4:54–55)

Upon whom does the pain of envy fall? If a destitute person envies a wealthy possessor of blessings, this envy too is a wicked act. But if a wealthy possessor of blessings begins to envy someone, this is a depravity more profound than baseness, and this kind of evil and corruption is the portion of the Jews alone. This is why they have been threatened with the fire of Hell, which is a most fitting recompense for this baseness.

﴿And sufficient is Hell as a blazing fire.﴾ (4:55)

When the discussion reached the point that among the family of Ibrahim some people became believers while others barred people from the way of Allah, it became necessary that the end of the believers be stated, and that the end of those who bar people from the path of faith also be stated. This recompense and punishment has always remained the same in every religion, and in the Holy Quran Allah Almighty describes it in the form of the Day of Resurrection with extremely severe and terrifying scenes.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 4, verses 56–57 (part 1 of 2):

(Verse) "Numbers 56 to 57."
(Verse) "Whenever their skins are roasted through, We shall replace them with other skins." (4:56)

This is a scene that unfolds continuously: a scene that stands before the eyes and is repeated again and again, so that the gaze becomes fixed upon it, and thought does not stray from it. It is certainly a terrifying scene, and its terror draws the mind and the sight towards it. A single word brings this continuous and frightening scene onto the screen: the word (kullama, "whenever"). And this scene becomes terrifying and dreadful through just one part of the sentence: "Whenever their skins are roasted through." Then, in the second part of the sentence, this process is made an extraordinary and astonishing act: "We shall replace them with other skins." All these dreadful scenes, this terrifying process and this strange and miraculous picture, are completed within a single conditional sentence, in one clause.

Now consider the reward of the believers in contrast to this blazing, terrifying Hell: in contrast to these burning skins, these skins that are roasted, which when they are consumed are changed so that they burn anew and the torment begins again. (Verse) "As for those who believe and do righteous deeds," and "those who accepted Our signs and did good works," they will be in gardens of lush greenery. Lesson 35 at a glance:

This lesson deals with a most important subject, and this subject is fundamental to the life of the Muslim community. It explains the conditions of faith and the definition of faith, that faith which manifests itself as the foundational system of this community. The importance of this subject lies partly in its own content, and partly in the manner of its connection and integration with the foundational system.

The Qur'an brought this community into existence and trained it. This community was brought out from concealment, or brought from non-existence into existence, and the Qur'an used a most comprehensive expression for it: (Verse) "You were the best community brought forth for mankind" (3:110). "You were the best nation, raised up for the people."

In short, the Qur'an gave this community existence, because it did not exist before the Qur'an. Then it trained it so that it would become an unparalleled community in the history of humanity, a best community, and "brought forth for mankind." Before proceeding, it is necessary that we clarify this reality: how the Qur'an created this community and how it trained it. It is a fact that the bringing into being of this community and its subsequent training was a new birth for it. Indeed, it was a new birth for the whole of humanity. After the coming of this community, humanity appeared in an entirely new form. This community was not a stage in the course of progress, nor one step among the stages of evolution. Nor was it a "long jump" in the process of development. Rather, this community was in fact a new birth for the Arab nation, and then for all humanity.

When we look at the poetry of the pre-Islamic age and study the scattered remnants of the Jahiliyyah period, which are in reality the diwan (collection) of the Arabs, we see that they record the Arabs' view of life, their view of the universe, their view of morality and their social conduct. These are their enduring and fundamental concepts. In these verses are the traces of their life, their national sentiments, and the entire stock of their ideas. The summary of their civilisation and culture is also recorded within them. In short, the complete personality of the Arabs exists in this Jahili poetry and the other scattered remnants.

In this diwan of the Arabs we see the collection of their ideas and their knowledge and culture, and we examine their values present in this diwan in the light of the Qur'an. Then we look at their view concerning existence, life, the universe and man, and their concepts regarding their social order and the purposes of human existence, and their practical organisation based on those concepts. Then we examine the practical condition of the Arabs before and after Islam, and make this comparative study in the light of the concepts found in their diwan. Then we compare it with the circumstances that arose in Arab society under Qur'anic concepts, and we come to know with complete certainty that, under Qur'anic concepts, this new society was a new birth for the Arabs. It was not progress, nor a stage of progress, nor a rapid advance; rather, this nation emerged through the craftsmanship of God and was given birth through God's perfect power. The Qur'an uses the word (akhrajat, "brought forth") most accurately for this. This new rebirth was most astonishing and wondrous, because it was the first and last appearance of this nation, and it is the unique example in the world of a nation being born between the two covers of a single book, a community coming into being and receiving life through the words of one book. But this is no cause for wonder, because these words are the commands of God.

If anyone disputes this point with us, let him tell us: at the turn of history when God, through His word, raised up this community, where was this community before? When the Qur'an created it and it was brought forth, where was it?

We know that it was in the Arabian Peninsula, but did it have any human existence? What was its record in the register of human civilisation? How many pages did it occupy in world history? Where was its place at the global table of humanity? And what gift did it offer on that table, so that history would remember it and it would be recognised: "This is the gift of the Arabs."

The truth is that this community was nurtured only through this religion, and it was trained under the shelter of the Islamic system of life. It led its own self and its own being, and then the whole of humanity, through the book that was in its hand, and its life was stamped by the system of life of that book. It came into existence through the Qur'an alone and nothing else. History bears witness to this. And God fulfilled His promise: (Verse) "Indeed, We have sent down to you a Book in which is your mention... will you not then use your reason?" (21:10).

In short, the Arab nation's mention on this earth came about only because of this Book, and it played a significant role in history. First it established its own human existence, and after that it brought into being a universal civilisation and culture. But now some fools wish to deny this bounty of God upon the Arab nation, and to be ungrateful for the fact that God sent down His final word in the Arabic language to the people of this world and made the Arabs its first addressees. Through this word He gave them a human existence, and granted them fame, history and civilisation. These fools in fact wish to strip off the robe that God bestowed upon the Arab nation, and they wish to tear the banner through which they gained honour and renown, indeed through which they were given existence when God raised them up as a community.

We say that when Islam was creating this community and training it, drawing the new features of Islam within the congregation of Muslims and firming them up, it was lifting it out of the deep pit of ignorance and erasing from its existence all the features of jahiliyyah; it was purifying its life, its souls and its society, organising it, raising it up anew and giving it a new birth, sending this new congregation into a battle-field, and erasing from its souls and its ways of conduct the lingering traces of the former jahiliyyah. And at the very time when the Qur'an was eliminating from within the congregation and from its environment the jahiliyyah present in Medina in the form of hypocrites, polytheists and Jews, these battles against jahiliyyah continued day and night, in every time and every place. In doing all this, the Qur'an first gave this community a correct conception of life. It laid down the conditions and limits of faith for it. Then, in accordance with this conception, Islam prescribed for it a constitutional system, by which a dividing line was drawn between its existence and the existence of jahiliyyah around it. The distinctive characteristics and purposes for which it was established were determined for it, so that it might convey them to people and call them to God and to God's divine system.

This lesson sets out this foundational system. This system springs from this foundational conception of life and rests upon it, and it is in accordance with these conditions of faith and limits of Islam.

Then this lesson contains the renewal of covenant from which this community takes its system of life. It also indicates the method by which it will derive its system, and the system by which it will comprehend what it is deriving, or return to that system in the problems and difficulties of life, in matters concerning which there is no explicit and clear text and in which difference of opinion is possible. Then it is also shown which authority is to be obeyed, what the source of that authority's strength is, and all these matters are the conditions and definitions of faith.

Here the constitutional system of this community becomes bound to its conception of life. This union is not dissolved again, nor are its constituent elements separated from one another.

This is the important subject to which this lesson does justice; complete guidance is given on it and all questions relating to it are answered. From the study of this lesson it also becomes clear that the matter is so clear and self-evident that it is hard to understand how any Muslim could dispute about it. This lesson clearly tells the community that messengers were sent only so that they might be obeyed, and that this obedience is by God's command, and that messengers were not sent merely to convey the message or to satisfy people by setting out convincing arguments, but rather: (Verse) "And We did not send any messenger except to be obeyed by the leave of God" (4:64).

This lesson makes clear that people are not believers if they do not make their judgements according to the system of law that God has revealed. This method is found in the practical life of the Messenger of God ﷺ and in his commands, and it remains until the Day of Resurrection in the form of the Qur'an and the Sunnah. And it is not enough merely that they have their judgements made according to this law; it is also necessary that they accept those judgements with willing contentment of heart.

(Verse) "But no, by your Lord, they will not truly believe until they make you judge in what they dispute among themselves, then find within themselves no resistance to what you have decided, and submit with full submission" (4:65).

"No, O Muhammad ﷺ, by your Lord, they can never be believers until they make you the judge in their mutual disputes, and then find no discomfort in their hearts at what you decide, but submit completely."

This lesson also tells that those who take their judgements to the taghut (false authority), that is, who have their disputes decided by any law other than the Shariah of God, will not be accepted in their claim that they believe in the word of God and the commands of the Messenger of God ﷺ, or that they believe in the earlier scriptures. Their claim is false, and the proof of it is their act of taking their judgements to the taghut.

(Verse) "Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you, yet desire to seek judgement from the taghut, though they were commanded to reject it? And Satan wishes to lead them far astray" (4:60).

"O Prophet, have you not seen those who claim that they have believed in the Book revealed to you and in the Books revealed before you, yet they wish to refer their disputes for judgement to the taghut, although they were commanded to disbelieve in it? Satan wishes to lead you far astray from the right path."

And this lesson also tells that a sign of hypocrisy is to prevent people from judging according to the law that God has revealed and that is found in the Sunnah of the Messenger ﷺ.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 4, verses 56–57 (part 2 of 2):

﴿And when it is said to them, "Come to what Allah has sent down and to the Messenger," you see the hypocrites turning away from you with aversion.﴾ (4:61)

This lesson states that the method of faith and its foundational constitution is this: you should follow the Book that Allah has sent down, follow the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and obey those believers who are ulul-amr (those in authority).

﴿O you who believe, obey Allah, obey the Messenger, and those of you who are in authority.﴾ (4:59)

All of this shows that where viewpoints differ, where issues are entirely new and there are no explicit injunctions concerning them, then you should turn to Allah and His Messenger and seek their solution in the light of the Quran and Sunnah. ﴿If you dispute over anything, refer it to Allah and the Messenger.﴾ (4:59) Through this method, the Islamic system of life discovers solutions to problems and circumstances that appear for the very first time... By this principle, Islam perpetually devises means for solving newly arising problems. Since the constitutional principle of Islam is that no one can be a believer until he resolves his affairs according to the Islamic system, therefore, along with the expansion of the Islamic system of life, it establishes this method of resolution and commands that matters be referred to Allah and His Messenger, because obedience here is a condition of faith. Faith is clearly conditional: ﴿If you truly believe in Allah and the Last Day.﴾ (4:59)

We must not forget this divine decree stated earlier: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with others, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills.﴾ (4:48) The Jews were declared to be polytheists merely because they regarded their rabbis as lords besides Allah. This was not because they worshipped and served their lords, but because they had granted their lords the authority to declare things lawful and unlawful. They conferred upon the rabbis both the right of sovereignty and the right of legislation, and they did this on their own initiative. Therefore they made them partners with Allah, which is an unforgivable crime, while all other sins may be forgiven. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Even if he committed fornication, even if he stole, even if he drank wine." Hence Allah Almighty has restricted the matter of belief to this: that there is no partner with Allah in sovereignty. He is unique in this, for it is the most specific of the attributes of divinity. Only within this can a believer remain a believer and a Muslim remain a Muslim, and only then may he hope that his sins be forgiven, whether small or great. Stepping outside of it is shirk, which Allah never forgives, because this is the condition of faith and the definition of Islam (Definition). ﴿If you believe in Allah and the Last Day.﴾ (4:59)

This is the important theme discussed in this lesson. Along with this, it also explains the obligations of the Muslim ummah on this earth, such as that they must establish justice and equity according to the correct system of life of Allah.

﴿Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to their owners, and when you judge between people, to judge with justice. Excellent is that which Allah instructs you. Indeed, Allah is ever Hearing and Seeing.﴾ (4:58)

This is the general outline of this lesson. Now, let us look at a detailed discussion of the texts.
