This is a truth which awakens every inner feeling in the heart, provided there is some particle of goodness present in a heart, provided there is some seed of righteousness present, provided there is in it some impulse toward an honourable station, entry into the shade of Allah's mercy, and the search for the generosity of Allah's grace. This gathering is for precisely such people as are high-minded and seekers of lofty ranks. This is the grace of Allah, and no one can reach the station of this grace and bounty merely through his obedience and his deeds. Rather, it is only the wide, profound and abundant grace and bounty of Allah, whose general outpouring covers whoever is destined for it.

Here it is fitting that we spend a few moments in the gathering of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ. These people were eager for the gathering of the Messenger ﷺ, both in this world and in the Hereafter. Some of these gentlemen would become distressed merely at the thought of being separated from him, even though he was then present among them. Therefore these verses were revealed, by which their love was refreshed and their pure sentiment was stirred, and their pure and transparent love became purer still.

Ibn Jarir narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: a man from the Ansar came who was very distressed. The Messenger ﷺ said, "O so-and-so, why are you distressed?" He replied, "O Messenger of Allah, I was thinking about a matter." He asked, "What was it?" He said, "It is that we come to you morning and evening, we look upon your face and sit in your assembly. Tomorrow you will go to the prophets, and we will not be able to meet you." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave no answer to this man's question. In the meantime, Jibril (peace be upon him) came with this verse:

﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger – those are with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour from among the prophets...﴾ (4:69). The Prophet ﷺ sent a message to that man and gave him glad tidings.

Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh also narrated this report from Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her): a man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger, you are dearer to me than my own soul, you are dearer to me than my family, and you are dearer to me than my daughters. When I am at home I remember you, and I rise and come and see you, and I cannot be patient. When I think of my death and your death, I realise that you will enter Paradise and join the company of the prophets, and even if I enter Paradise I may not be able to see you." The Prophet ﷺ gave no answer to this man's concerns until this verse was revealed:

﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger – those are with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour from among the prophets and the truthful and the martyrs and the righteous; and excellent are those as companions.﴾ (4:69)

Sahih Muslim has the hadith of Rabi'ah, who said: I was with the Prophet ﷺ one night. I provided him water for ablution and his other needs. The Messenger ﷺ said, "Ask whatever you wish." I said, "O Messenger of Allah, I seek your companionship in Paradise." He said, "Is there anything else?" He said, "No, just that." The Messenger ﷺ said, "Then help me against your own soul by increasing your prostrations."

In Sahih al-Bukhari this report has come through several chains: a man loves a group but does not meet them, so what will his condition be? The Prophet ﷺ said, "A man will be with those whom he loves." This was the very matter in which their hearts and minds were always occupied: love for the Messenger and companionship with the Messenger in the Hereafter. They had already tasted the company of the Messenger in this world too. Today only that heart can taste this which contains love for the Messenger, and for us, in this last hadith, there appears a ray of light, a means of tranquillity, and a lamp of hope.

Lesson 36 at a glance:

I am inclined to think that the collection of verses in this lesson was revealed in the early period at Madinah, after the Battle of Uhud and before the Battle of the Trench, because the picture it draws of Islamic society shows that it had not yet reached a stage of maturity. Within this society there were various kinds of groups, some of whom were immature, and there were also people who had not truly believed but were merely practising hypocrisy. These verses show that the Islamic society still needed its education and training further, and that in this regard great effort and deep attention were required. It needed to be prepared for that great goal and made capable of bearing the burden which Islam had placed upon its shoulders, and it was also necessary to raise this society to the level of people needed for an Islamic revolution, whether this training and reform was in the field of beliefs and concepts or in the field of confronting opposing camps.

And when we say that some were immature, this does not mean that there was a shortage of people of the very highest standard in that society. Here we are taking the Islamic society of that time as a whole. Various elements existed in this society, but they were not all alike. Therefore there was a need to strive to bring all the elements of this society to a high level so that complete harmony might arise among its members. This is clearly expressed through these verses and guidance.

Through a deep study of these guidances revealed by Allah, we get the opportunity to assess the Muslim society of that time, and the features of the Muslim community emerge in which this society appears as a human society. We often overlook this aspect. In this society we see both high-standard training and strength, and we also see some weaknesses. It is also seen how the Qur'an deals with human weaknesses, the remaining traces of jahiliyyah, and the opposing camp of Islam, and how all this happens at the same time. When we study the Qur'an's method of training, the Qur'an appears to deal with living human beings in the real world, and it is also seen how, through successful effort in the field of training, the Qur'an created a society which was taken from the jahili society, which had people of various ranks and classes and people of various characteristics, and the Qur'an made them so harmonious, so lofty, and so united, the complete image of which is clearly visible in the final period of the Prophet ﷺ, and this was a society so elevated, complete and perfect that it is not possible for human beings to go beyond it.

From the study of any human society we learn what capacities lie within the human soul, and in what form they manifest within the best community and society in the world. That community whose training was itself given by the Messenger ﷺ, and this training was indeed in accordance with the Qur'anic method.

From this we also learn what the Qur'an's method of training was, and how the Qur'an dealt with human souls. How gentle its attitude toward them was, and how it bound together and united people of different levels within the community. We see the Qur'an's method of training, and we see this training system functioning in the real world in accordance with human nature.

One further benefit we gain is that we compare our own circumstances and those of other human societies with that human community which Allah established. Then we study the actual condition of those societies from a human perspective, so that, seeing our own shortcomings, we do not despair of reforming our condition in the modern age and do not abandon the effort to reform ourselves. And lest this first Islamic society become in our imagination merely an imaginary society, and we abandon the endeavour to walk in the footsteps of that community, and in the modern age raise these modern societies from their present decline to a lofty station.

This is a great storehouse of lessons. And when we take this storehouse, living within the shade of Fi Zilal al-Quran, it will be a great means of good for us.

From the verses given in this lesson it is known that the following kinds of people existed in the Islamic ranks at that time:

(A) There were also people who kept themselves back from jihad. Through them, laziness also arose among others, and if they did not go out for jihad and remained safe and sound in their homes, they considered it a success for themselves, while the Muslims who took part in jihad faced difficulties and hardships in it. Similarly, if these people did not go for jihad and the Muslims obtained spoils of war, such people would feel that they had suffered a loss because they did not receive a share of the spoils. In this way these people were trading the world for the Hereafter.

(B) Among these people were some emigrants who, while they were in Makkah and were subjected to persecution, out of a spirit of defence and bravery would say that they wished they were permitted to fight and wage war, but there the permission to fight had been entirely withheld from them. Now, when the command for jihad came in Madinah and it was said that they should begin fighting the disbelievers, these people began to wish that they had been given more time and that the command to fight had not come.

(C) Among them were people who, when some good fortune reached them, would say, "This is from Allah's grace," and when a calamity came, would say, "This calamity is because of the Prophet ﷺ." They did not say this because they had firm faith in and reliance upon Allah, but rather they said these things while criticising the Islamic leadership.

(D) There were also some who, in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ, would show themselves as most obedient, but when they left his presence they would plot against the Muslims and speak something else with their companions.

(E) There were some who lent their ears to rumours and spread them within the Islamic ranks. In this way they created unrest in the Islamic front, whereas they should have taken the matter to proof or referred it themselves to the Islamic leadership.

(F) There were some who doubted whether the source and origin of these guidances was the Divine Being, or not; they thought that the Prophet ﷺ spoke some matters on his own initiative.

(G) There were some who used to defend the hypocrites, as the examples at the beginning of the next lesson show. Their aim was that the community of Muslims should be divided into two groups concerning the hypocrites. From this it was apparent that within their Islamic conception and organisation complete harmony did not yet exist, and these people did not fully understand the duties of leadership and the need for connection with the leadership in such matters.

All these elements that existed in the Islamic ranks were groups of hypocrites. It may be that they all belonged to one group; it is also possible that in Madinah's society these people belonged to several groups of hypocrites, or that among these people there were also weak-faith Muslims whose state of faith had not yet matured. Some of these people may also have been emigrants. In any case, several such groups existed within the Islamic community, and this community at that time was surrounded by the Jews of Madinah, while in Makkah it was in the grip of the polytheists, and throughout the Arabian Peninsula this community was encircled by those waiting to see which way the camel of this movement would sit. This community was continually creating unrest within the ranks of the Muslims. Therefore there was a need for training and purification within the inner ranks, and a need to rouse people to jihad.

From these verses it is known in what manner the Qur'an carried out this inner jihad and training. The Qur'an removed despair from the ranks of the Muslims and reassured every individual of the community. (Verses 71–74)

This is an admonition to the believers. It contains guidance from the Exalted Realm, in which is laid down for them a method of action and a path for the future. When a person studies the Qur'an, he is amazed to see that this Book also prepares the general scheme for the struggle of jihad. The strategy of war is likewise recorded in the Qur'an. In another verse it says:

﴿O you who believe, fight those of the disbelievers who are near to you, and let them find in you harshness.﴾ This is the general plan for the Islamic movement. In this verse the believers are addressed:

﴿O you who believe, take your precaution, then go forth in separate groups or go forth all together.﴾ (4:71)

"O you who believe, be always ready to confront the enemy, then go forth in separate units as the occasion demands, or go forth together." This is a part of the scheme of practical action, which is called tactics (ٹیکٹکس). And in Surah al-Anfal too, some such instructions are given that concern the battlefield:

﴿So if you overtake them in war, then inflict such punishment upon them that those who are behind them may be dispersed, that perhaps they will take heed.﴾

This is the Qur'an. In it Muslims are taught not only acts of worship and the rites of servitude, nor only personal Islamic manners and morals, as some people hold such a mendicant view of this religion. Rather, this Qur'an takes the life of people as a whole (As A Whole). It passes judgement on every single practical event of life, and gives complete guidance for the whole of life. This Book demands from a Muslim individual and a Muslim society nothing less than that their entire lives be lived in accordance with this Book, under its governance, and in conformity with its guidance. In particular, this Book does not permit a Muslim individual or society to adopt multiple systems for their life whose principles differ. It should not be that they take the personal system, worship, and the system of morals and manners from the Book of God, while they take guidance in economic, social, political and international affairs from some other book or from concepts given by a human being. According to this Book, the task of a human being is to derive his thought and concepts from this Book and its method, and to take the detailed rulings for his life from this Book and apply them to the events of life. This is because constantly new problems and circumstances arise in life, and he should derive these rulings in the same manner as the Book itself has given their details in the lesson preceding this one. The Book has left open no other path than this, otherwise there would be neither faith nor Islam. Indeed, there would be no Islam and no faith at all, because those who do not accept this demand of the Book do not enter into faith and Islam, and have, as it were, not acknowledged the pillars of Islam. The first of these pillars is the testimony of faith (لاالہ الا اللہ), the meaning of which is that there is no ruler but Allah and there is no legislator but Allah.

This is the Qur'an which, in this struggle, lays out for Muslims the battlefield plan which accompanied their position at that time, and which was necessary for their existence, because on every side around them there were countless opponents, among whom they were surrounded. Within the Islamic state, Jews and hypocrites were plotting deep conspiracies against the Muslims. First of all, Allah Most High warns the believers.

﴿O you who believe, take your precaution, then go forth in separate groups or go forth all together.﴾ (4:71)

"O you who believe, be always ready to confront the enemy, then go forth in separate units as the occasion demands, or go forth together."

Thubat is the plural of thubah, meaning a group. The ruling is that it is not permissible to go out for jihad alone. For jihad, either go out in small units or go out in a large army and force, according to the kind of encounter that confronts you, because the enemy can easily capture individuals, and at that time the enemy was spread everywhere. This ruling was especially applicable at that time, because in that era the enemy was spread throughout the centre of Islam, and was roaming openly in Madinah in the form of Jews and hypocrites.

﴿And indeed among you is he who will surely lag behind. So if a calamity befalls you, he says, "Allah has already blessed me, since I was not present with them as a witness." But if bounty comes to you from Allah, he will surely say, as if there had never been any affection between you and him, "Oh, I wish I had been with them, so I would have achieved a great achievement."﴾ (4:72–73)

"Yes, among you there is someone who holds back from fighting. If a calamity befalls you, he says, 'Allah has blessed me that I did not go with those people.' And if bounty from Allah comes to you, he says ... and says in such a way as if there had been no bond of love between you and him ... that 'Would that I had been with them, so my affair would have succeeded greatly.'"

Go forth in organised units or go forth all together; let it not be that some among you go forth while others are slack, as some are being slack now, and remain always ready. Be ready not only against the external enemy, but also against these internal enemies, against those who shirk, who hold back from fighting and who are defeatist. These people prevent themselves from jihad and are slack, and they also prevent others from war; this is generally the habit of people with a defeatist mentality.

The word (لیبطئن) used here carries a kind of heaviness and slipperiness. In the pronunciation of its letters and in its vocal movement there is a kind of slipperiness too. And when the tongue utters its final doubled letter, there is also a tension in it. With a single word has been expressed the entire psychological struggle that was in the minds of such people, and the very word used to convey this meaning contains the whole struggle. Just as the meaning is heavy, so the word used is heavy, and this is a style of expression of the highest perfection, which is unique to the Qur'an. (See al-Tasvir al-Fanni fi'l-Qur'an, chapter Tanasuq.) After this word, the whole sentence (وان منکم لمن لیبطئن) [4:72] shows that they are fully engaged in sluggishness; these people are few in number, and they insist fully on this holding back. They are strenuously striving at it, and this is shown by the emphatic particles used in this sentence, which show that this group is persisting in its conduct and that it is having an effect on the Islamic front, and a very bad effect.

This is why the Qur'an gives detailed explanations about them. It reveals the hidden secrets in their hearts, and it portrays vividly their detestable reality. This is a wonderful miraculous style of the Qur'an.

Behold, these people are before you, with all their intentions, with their complete temperament and with their words and deeds, standing completely exposed before your eyes, as if they have been placed under a microscope. And this inner microscope is revealing the secrets of their hearts, and all their aims and purposes are becoming clear from it.

Look, these are the people who are seen in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and after his time this type will remain in the same way in every time and place. What are they? Weak, hypocrites, and ever-changing, whose aims are extremely petty, extremely commonplace, who cannot even think of any benefit higher than their personal interest and individual gain. They do not even raise their eyes towards a horizon higher than their own selves. These people revolve the whole world around a single axis, and that axis is their own self and personal interests; they never forget it.

These people are slack and limp, and are not ones who advance so as to stand at their true station, and their concept of gain and loss is fit only for base hypocrites.

These people are those who stay behind from the struggle of jihad. If calamities befall the mujahideen and they become beset with difficulties, as often happens, these backward people become very pleased, and they think that their flight from jihad and their escape from hardships is beneficial for them.

﴿And indeed among you is he who will surely lag behind. So if a calamity befalls you, he says, "Allah has already blessed me, since I was not present with them as a witness."﴾ (4:72)

Such people are not ashamed that they regard this life of cowardice as a blessing of Allah, and then call it the bounty of that Allah in whose command they have disobeyed by sitting back. In such circumstances, even if someone escapes, he can never attain the blessing of God, because the blessing of Allah is not obtained by violating the command of Allah, even though outwardly such a person may appear to be among the saved.

That would indeed be a blessing, but only in the view of those who do not deal with Allah Most High. It is salvation in the view of those who do not understand what their purpose of creation is, and who do not serve Allah by obedience and jihad so that they establish the Islamic system of life in the world. It is a blessing in the view of those whose gaze cannot fall upon the lofty horizon beyond the ground in front of their feet. These are people like ants. This salvation is a blessing in the view of those who have no sense that bearing the hardships of jihad in the path of Allah is for the establishment of the Islamic system and for the exaltation of the word of Allah. This is the bounty of Allah, and it is His special selection, by which He chooses whom He wills from among His servants, so that they may overcome human weaknesses in this worldly life. In this way He frees them from the bondage of the world. They attain an exalted life; they become masters of life, and life does not become their master, so that this freedom and this exaltedness may carry them to those heights which are reserved for the martyrs in the Hereafter. Indeed all people die, but only those who give their lives in the path of Allah are martyrs, and this is the great bounty of Allah.

If the situation turns out differently, and the mujahideen succeed, those who went out prepared, so that whatever befalls them in the path of Allah may come, and they may receive the bounty of Allah in the form of victory and spoils, then these backward people become deeply remorseful that they did not take part in that profitable struggle. In their view the standard for this gain is extremely base: a purely worldly standard.

﴿And if bounty comes to you from Allah, he will surely say, as if there had never been any affection between you and him, "Oh, I wish I had been with them, so I would have achieved a great achievement."﴾ (4:73)

"And if bounty from Allah comes to you, he says ... and says in such a way as if there had been no bond of affection between you and him ... 'Would that I had been with them, so my affair would have succeeded greatly.'"

This is an extremely base desire, merely a desire for spoils, and this person calls it a great success. The believer does not regard returning with spoils as wrong; rather, it is expected that he too would ask Allah for such success. And from the believer it is not expected that he seek hardships; rather, what is desired is that he pray for well-being. The overall concept of the believer is entirely different from the concept of these laggards, and therefore the Qur'an presents the concept of these people in a most repugnant form, which is detestable.

The truth is that the believer does not wish for hardships and calamities either, but seeks well-being; yet when he is called to jihad, he does not advance with heavy steps. When he goes forth, he seeks one of two good outcomes: either victory and triumph, or martyrdom in the path of Allah, and both of these are from the bounty of Allah, and both are a great success. If the believers' lot is martyrdom, they are content with the decree, and they join the company that attained the station of martyrdom.
