(Ayah 100)

In this verse the Qur'an addresses the various doubts that arise within the human soul. At that time, the difficulties of migration appeared before people, and such doubts constantly surface whenever a person sets out for the sake of Allah and falls into hardship.

The Qur'an trains such souls with clarity. It is told plainly, and nothing is concealed. It is not the case that the dangers faced by one who takes a step are hidden; rather, everything is explained, including the dangers of death and of sacrificing one's life. Yet the Qur'an also reassures the believers through certain other realities, the guarantee of which Allah Himself gives.

Here it is said that this migration is for the sake of Allah and for no other purpose, and that in Islam only this migration is considered valid. It is not for wealth, nor is it to flee from difficulties, nor is it to attain pleasures and desires. In short, it is not for any worldly aim. And whoever migrates in the way of Allah, and in the way of Allah alone, will find in this world great abundance; the earth will not be constricted for him. In the provision of sustenance too, his means and resources will not be limited, and faith and salvation in the Hereafter will certainly be attained.

﴿And whoever migrates in the way of Allah will find in the earth many a refuge and abundance.﴾ (4:100)

(Whoever migrates in the way of Allah will find in the earth ample room to take refuge and a great scope for earning his livelihood.)

It is merely the weakness of the human soul, its greed and miserliness, that creates in the mind the whisper that the sources of livelihood in the world are confined to one particular place and to certain conditions. If someone leaves those conditions and circumstances, his sustenance will be cut off.

In truth, this is a most false notion regarding livelihood and the means of life. It is this very thinking that causes a person to accept humiliation, subjugation, and the trial of religion and faith, and then his end is that evil end mentioned in these verses: that the angels take the lives of such people while they are wronging themselves. Accordingly, Allah assures a good end to those who migrate in His way: such people will be granted freedom, and they will find great expansiveness in Allah's world. They will surely see that wherever they go, Allah will keep them alive, provide for them, and grant them salvation in the Hereafter.

However, it also happens that some people respond to the summons of death during the migration itself. Death is a binding reality, and it is not connected with apparent causes. When the appointed time arrives, death certainly comes, whether a person stays put or migrates. It neither comes earlier nor later.

Yes, it is another matter that human thinking remains within apparent circumstances. In its view, death has apparent causes, and the Islamic system speaks taking these into account as well. Accordingly, it is said that the moment one leaves home in the way of Allah, the reward becomes incumbent upon Allah, and such a person will receive complete reward.

﴿And whoever leaves his home as a migrant to Allah and His Messenger, and then death overtakes him, his reward has indeed fallen upon Allah.﴾ (4:100)

(And whoever leaves his house migrating toward Allah and His Messenger, then death overtakes him, his reward has become binding upon Allah.)

Such a person will receive his full wage: the reward of the migration, the reward of the journey, and the reward of reaching the abode of Islam and of all the hardships that existed there, all of this he will receive. Allah is the guarantor of this reward. Yet along with this guarantee of reward, it is also indicated that his sins may be forgiven as a pension and allowance, and further bounties may be granted. All these privileges are in addition to the principal wage.

﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (4:100)

Indeed, this is an extremely profitable bargain. In it, a migrant in the way of Allah receives the full price. The moment he steps forward and sets out in the way of Allah, he receives his reward. Death is death; when its time comes, there is no advancing or delaying of it. It has no connection with whether one migrates or remains settled in one place. If a person stays settled in one place, death will still come, and in the bargain he will suffer loss. He will receive no reward or forgiveness; rather, the angels will take his soul, regarding him as a wrongdoer. ...... How great is the difference between these two states and these two bargains, and how different is their end.

What conclusions emerge from this entire lesson? Various results are derived from it. Before the discussion of the other topics of this lesson proceeds, it is good to complete a reflection on these results.

(1) From this we learn that Islam regards abstaining from participation in jihad in the way of Allah as a very grave matter. Moreover, Islam does not look favourably upon separating from and remaining distant from the Islamic community, unless there is an excuse, and the excuse is that one is not able to undertake the journey of migration or has no way to do so.

(2) From this lesson it is known that jihad in the way of Allah holds very great importance within the Islamic worldview. The Islamic system also has the duty to keep the practice of jihad continuing. The Shia school of thought counts jihad as one of the pillars of religion, since there are strong Qur'anic proofs in its favour, which serve to clarify and interpret their position. If there were not the hadith whose content is that Islam is founded upon five things, their position would be correct, and there would be no evidence against it. But great emphasis has been placed upon jihad in Islam. Its importance at times of danger to Islamic life is established. In every age and every place its need arises, and this need is a most natural demand of Islam, not merely due to temporary circumstances, because all the proofs and evidences indicate that in Islam jihad is a foundational and fundamental obligation.

(3) From this lesson it is also known that a human being remains a human being. Sometimes a multitude of difficulties crowds in upon the human soul. At times a person is frightened by dangers; at other times, seeing difficulties, he becomes lethargic, and these weaknesses have appeared even among the most righteous societies and the best of generations. Therefore, in addressing weaknesses we should never fall into despair; rather, in this matter continuous striving must go on. People should be encouraged, and they should be shown the prospects of success in the end. Admonition and guidance should continue at all times, and this work should be carried out in accordance with the wise style of the Qur'an.

(4) Finally, from this lesson we learn how the Qur'an was striving for the reform of this life, what real difficulties it faced, and how it led the Islamic society amid those difficulties. The battle the Qur'an faced was continuing on every front. The first front was the human soul: its nature, its temperament, and the weaknesses of the age of ignorance present within it. ... We should also reflect on the style with which we study the Qur'an, and how we should convey the call to Allah when addressing the human soul and the real circumstances and difficulties of life.

After this comes the statement regarding the permission to shorten prayer for migrants and other travellers. Whether journeys are for jihad or for commercial activities, and also in a state of fear, shortening is permitted; that is, in such circumstances the enemy might attack and capture them, and thus they might fall into trial. This shortening is separate from the shortening that is due merely to travel. This is a specific shortening and relates to a state of fear.

(Verse) 101.

A traveler needs a constant connection with his Lord, so that Allah makes things easy for him in the difficulties of his journey. He receives help in his preparations, his travel provisions are supplied, and Allah makes the hardships of the road easy for him. Prayer is the most effective means of connecting with Allah. Allah has guided the Muslims to seek help through prayer in difficulties and hardships. When there is a place of fear, and when they face the trials of life, the command is: seek help through prayer. ﴿And seek help through patience and prayer﴾ (The Prayer and patience are the means by which one seeks Allah's help.)

This is why Allah mentioned prayer immediately after the subject of travel and jihad. In such circumstances, prayer is an essential weapon for a believer. If someone faces fear and danger on the road, he finds peace only in the remembrance of Allah. For one who leaves his homeland, reaching the court of Allah is itself a cause of tranquility. Yes, it is also true that, with complete prayer and full bowing and prostration, an enemy hiding somewhere nearby may attack a believer, may recognize him, and may seize him during his long bowing and prostration. Therefore, it is permissible for those who go out for jihad to shorten (qasr) the prayer in a time of fear.

Here, regarding the meaning and interpretation of qasr (shortening), we prefer the view adopted by al-Jassas, that this qasr does not mean shortening the number of rak'ahs. That is permissible for any traveler, whether or not there is fear. Rather, in travel, shortening is obligatory, as the Prophet (ﷺ) shortened the prayer and did so on every journey, since according to the preferred opinions, it is not even permissible to pray the full number of rak'ahs while traveling.

Therefore, the qasr here, in a state of fear, means something entirely different, and this qasr differs from the qasr of the traveler. This qasr concerns the manner of performing the prayer itself. For example, in standing, bowing and prostration, the pillars are performed very briefly and with less than full calm. Thus, in a state of fear, a traveler may pray while walking, while riding, and even by gesture alone, and in this way he remains connected with his Lord. Even in a state of fear and trial, he is armed with this essential weapon, and he is also in need of it against the enemy, because ﴿Indeed, the disbelievers are to you a clear enemy﴾ (4:101).

After the command of shortening the prayer for the traveler and the fighter in a state of fear, and in this connection, the ruling of Salat al-Khawf (the prayer performed in a state of danger) is now given here in the context of battle. Even within this purely jurisprudential ruling, there is an abundant store of psychological and educational indications that are present and available.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 4, verses 102–103:

(Verse) Nos. 102 to 103.

One who reflects on the secrets and subtleties of the Qur'an, and who contemplates the divine method of training, especially in this lesson, discovers wondrous secrets. Within this lesson there are moments of reflection and feeling whose impact reaches down into the depths of the human soul. Let us first glimpse the battlefield:

This verse of the Qur'an does not merely state a jurisprudential and legal rule, that the prayer of fear shall be performed in this manner. Within it there is an abundance of education and training, through which a revolutionary community is morally trained and, at the same time, made aware of revolutionary action.

The first thing that becomes clear from the verse is that in Islam prayer has such importance that it is not abandoned even within the field of battle. From the standpoint of faith it is entirely evident that prayer is an excellent weapon in the field of combat, indeed more important than all weapons, and that it is very necessary to benefit from this weapon in every battle. Prayer has a deep connection with the temper and atmosphere of that battle.

The Islamic troops of the early period, who were trained according to the divine and Qur'anic method, confronted their enemy with the weapon in which they were superior to the enemy. They held this superiority over their enemies: they acknowledged only the One God, without partner. They had come to know their Lord well, and they fully felt that this God of theirs was fully a partner in their struggle. They were also superior to the enemy in terms of purpose. Their goal was lofty, and they regarded it as the highest aim. Their conception of the universe, their conception of life, and their conception of the ultimate purpose of human existence were all loftier than those of every enemy. In the organization that came into being under this superior system of life, too, they were superior to the enemy. In the battlefield, prayer was a sign of all these superiorities, and at every moment it reminded them of this lesson and this awareness, that they were superior. This is why, in the battlefield, prayer was for them the supreme weapon; indeed, their reliance was upon this very weapon.

The second thing seen in the context of these verses is that the believers are spiritually prepared and vigilant, and stand against the enemy. The enemy too sits in ambush, awaiting a brief moment of the believers' heedlessness, so that when they are unaware, the enemy may seize their weapons and equipment and attack suddenly. Along with this warning, this admonition, and this instruction to steadfastness and composure, it is stated that for those with whom you contend, Allah has prepared a humiliating punishment. On one side there is a stern command to remain alert and ready; on the other side there is the assurance: be at peace. On one side there is guidance to be extremely attentive and watchful; on the other side there is complete tranquility. This is the method by which Allah trains the believers, because the enemy is extremely cunning and may adopt base stratagems.

Scholars differ regarding the manner of the prayer of fear. These rulings they have derived from this very verse. We shall mention only the general manner and will not enter into the detailed jurisprudential particulars.

(Verse) "And when you are among them and lead them in prayer, let one party of them stand with you, and let them take their arms. Then, when they have prostrated, let them go behind you, and let another party who have not yet prayed come and pray with you, and let them also remain on guard and keep their arms with them." (4:102)

The meaning is that when you are present and leading them in prayer, one group of them should pray the first rak'ah behind you, while the other group takes up arms and stands guard. When the first group has completed the rak'ah, they should withdraw and take up guard duty with their arms, and the other group should come and pray one rak'ah behind you. In this way your prayer is completed, and you give the salam.

After this, the first group comes and completes the one rak'ah that remains for them, and departs. That rak'ah is performed alone. Then this group withdraws and stands on guard, while the other group comes and completes the one rak'ah that remained for them, while the first group keeps watch.

In this way both groups will have prayed with the Imam: in the leadership of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the same ruling applies to the caliphs and commanders who come after him.

(Verse) "The disbelievers wish that you would be heedless of your weapons and your baggage, so that they might attack you in one sudden assault." (4:102)

This is the wish that the disbelievers have always harbored in their hearts against the believers. Months and years pass, centuries have elapsed, and even today the desire of the disbelievers is the same. This is the reality that Allah instilled in the hearts of the first community of believers, and today too it is being emphasized. It is true that Allah used to prepare a military plan for those people at that time; but in the prayer of fear, as we have understood, there is a military plan for us as well.

This caution, this psychological preparedness, and this constant readiness with arms is not required at every moment, nor is it appropriate to command the Muslims with a perpetual order merely to put them to hardship; but they should do so as far as they are able.

(Verse) "There is no blame upon you if you lay down your arms because of rain that troubles you, or if you are ill." (4:102)

In such circumstances bearing arms is difficult, and it is also not beneficial; mere caution suffices, along with complete reliance on Allah's help.

(Verse) "But take your precaution. Indeed, Allah has prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment." (4:102)

It is possible that this very caution, this very vigilance, and this very watchfulness become the means of the punishment that Allah has prepared for the people of disbelief, which is deeply humiliating; thus the believers become the instrument of Allah's power, and Allah's will is fulfilled through them. Alongside the aforementioned caution, this is a glad tiding of tranquility for the believers, because the believers had complete certainty that Allah was their helper against the enemies of Islam, and that a humiliating punishment was destined for the enemies of Islam. And it may be that they themselves are the hand of that power.

(Verse) "And when you have finished the prayer, remember Allah standing, sitting, and on your sides; and when you are secure, establish the prayer. Indeed, the prayer has been enjoined upon the believers at fixed times." (4:103)

It is commanded that in every state you keep your hearts connected with Allah, both within the prayer and outside it, because connection with Allah is the greatest military preparation, and it is the weapon that never rusts.

At times of security and peace, the command is that you perform the prayer in full, with all its pillars and with tranquility, and not shorten it as was said, because the permission to shorten was under certain circumstances. Prayer is an obligation that must be performed at its appointed time, and when the state of fear is absent, it is performed in the same manner in which it is ordinarily performed.

With the words "Indeed, the prayer has been enjoined upon the believers as an obligation bound to fixed times," the Zahiris have argued that if a prayer is missed, it cannot later be performed. In their view, performing a missed prayer does not discharge the obligation. They say that an obligatory prayer does not exist after its appointed time has passed; if the time has gone, there is no need to pray or perform it. However, the opinion of the majority of scholars is that it is discharged. Yes, the making up of a missed prayer should be done very promptly, and it is not appropriate to delay it without cause. Beyond this, we do not enter into further differences of subsidiary rulings.

Now the conclusion of this lesson is near. It is commanded that you continue the work of jihad, even though you may face pain and grief, and even though it may be a cause of hardship and fatigue for you. A sharp awakening is given, and so forceful a jolt is administered, that this awareness reaches into the hearts, and this awareness, descending into the depths of the hearts, illuminates the human conscience, and in that light aims, inclinations, and objectives are determined.

(Verse) "Number 104."

These few words draw clear and decisive lines, showing how long and arduous the path of a believer is. The believers are always caught between two millstones. Certainly in this perpetual conflict they suffer pain and grief and deep wounds, but let them consider: have these hardships fallen upon them alone, or do their enemies also face the same kind of hardships? The enemies too suffer pain and grief; they too receive wounds. But the difference between you two is that the people of faith fight in the way of Allah and hope for a magnificent reward from Allah, whereas their enemies are fighting a purposeless and fruitless war; they have nothing to take before Allah, and they have no hope from Allah in this world nor any expectation in the Hereafter... So if the disbelievers are determined upon this struggle, then it is fitting for the Muslims to be even more determined. If the disbelievers bear deep wounds in this struggle, then the people of Islam should endure more wounds than them and be patient. And they should pursue those disbelievers, continue jihad and qital, and bring them to a state where their strength is broken and they no longer remain a source of fitnah (trial) for any Muslim's religion, life and property.

In every struggle the worldview that is superior prevails. There are also moments when calamities exceed the endurance of a human being; the pain becomes unbearable. In such circumstances the believer needs a special provision of strength, which flows from the fountainhead of faith and ideology, and this is the remembrance of Allah, which is the best balm for every wound.

These instructions were being given at a time when the battle was balanced and equal. Both sides were engaged in combat, both suffered pain and grief, and both were armed... But there may come a time for the believers when the battle is not balanced and open warfare is not taking place; even in such circumstances the same principle applies. Falsehood never tolerates the people of Islam, even when falsehood is dominant and the Islamic creed is subdued, because there is a contradiction within falsehood. Due to this internal contradiction it is restless. It itself suffers from the struggle within its own being, and then it is also at war with human nature and the nature of things.

The path of the community of believers in such circumstances is likewise: to endure and not lose courage. It should keep in view the reality that although it is afflicted with hardships, its enemy is afflicted with the disease of internal contradiction. Diseases also have kinds: heart-wounds are deeper than wounds of the body, and the enemy receives wounds that are not apparent outwardly. ﴿And you hope from Allah for what they do not hope﴾ (4:104), and this is the balm that is not available to the enemy. This is the point where the paths of the two sides diverge, and Allah knows this well. ﴿And Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾ (4:104). Allah knows what the remedy for hearts and emotions is, how to deal with them, what the cure for wounds of the heart is, and what the balm of the soul is, from which the people of disbelief are unaware and deprived.

Lesson 39 at a glance:

The verses point to a story for which there is no parallel on this earth, and none similar to it in the whole history of humanity. This too is a witness that this religion is from Allah and must be from Allah. For however lofty human notions of justice and equity may be, however pure the human soul may become, and however firmly human temperament may stand upon the Straight Path, they cannot raise themselves to that lofty station to which these verses point. This can be achieved only through divine revelation. The graph drawn on the horizon of human history is so high that humanity has reached that station only under the shade of the Islamic system of life, and in future too this exaltation can be attained only under the Islamic system.

This event occurred when the Jews of Madinah were employing every poisoned arrow and weapon in their quiver against Islam and the Muslims, the details of which have already been explained in this surah, in Surah al-Baqarah and in Surah Ali 'Imran. The circumstances were such that the Jews were spreading every kind of false propaganda against Islam. They were forming a front of the polytheists against Islam, encouraging the polytheists, paving the way for them, spreading false news in their propaganda, and corrupting people's minds. They insulted the leadership of the Messenger ﷺ and created doubts about revelation and prophethood. They also tried to create internal disorder within the Islamic society, and day and night they were busy gathering the enemies of Islam to attack the Muslims. The Islamic movement was entirely new in Madinah, and traces of jahiliyyah were still present in human souls. Some Muslims still had kinship and other ties with Jews and polytheists, and all these matters were a source of danger to the ranks.

In such difficult, dangerous and emergent circumstances these verses were revealed, and these strict instructions were given to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Muslims. The purpose was that justice should be done to a Jewish accused: the charge of theft against him was false, and those who had leveled the false accusation were obliged to make amends for it. He belonged to a household of the Ansar of Madinah. The Ansar were the treasure of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who in the face of all these Jewish conspiracies were his supporters and helpers, and aides to his prophethood and religion.

How lofty is this standard of magnanimity, exaltation, justice and equity! No words can be found to praise and describe it. All statements, all comments and all explanations fall short of this standard and level. Human powers cannot by their own effort reach this level and standard; human beings alone cannot perform this miracle. It is the leadership and guidance of the Islamic methodology that can raise a human being to that lofty station.

The story that was narrated in connection with the background of these verses, and which several sources have transmitted, is worth hearing from the Ansar. Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man and his paternal uncle Rifa'ah both fought alongside the Messenger ﷺ in some expeditions. Once one of them lost his coat of mail (Rifa'ah's). It was commonly suspected that a man from the Ansar family of Banu Ubayriq had stolen this coat of mail. The owner lodged a report with the Messenger ﷺ that Tu'mah ibn Ubayriq had stolen his coat of mail. Some narrations mention the name Bashir ibn Ubayriq. It was also well known about him that he would write verses satirizing the companions and spread them around, claiming that they belonged to a certain Arab poet. When the thief learned that a report had been lodged against him, he quickly threw the coat of mail into the house of a Jew named Zayd ibn Samin, and told some people of his family that he had made the coat of mail disappear and thrown it into the house of so-and-so, and that it would soon be found in his house. "Go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and say that our brother is innocent, that so-and-so is the thief, and that we have gathered information about this matter. Ask him to publicly acquit our man and clear him, for if he is not honourably acquitted by Allah through you, his honour will be ruined."

When the Messenger ﷺ learned that the coat of mail had indeed been found in the Jew's house, he announced in the assembly that Ibn Ubayriq was innocent. For his family had requested of the Messenger ﷺ that Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man and his uncle had come to a Muslim family of theirs and made it a suspect of theft, and they had done this without any proof or evidence. Qatadah says: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and spoke with him, and he said: "You deliberately leveled a charge of theft against a family whose Islam and goodness are well known, and without proof." I returned, but my condition was such that I kept saying that if all my wealth had gone and I had not spoken to the Messenger ﷺ, it would have been better. Then my uncle Rifa'ah came and said to me: "Nephew, what have you done?" So I told him what the Messenger ﷺ had said, and Rifa'ah said: "Allah is the helper." Not long after this, these verses were revealed.

﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book with the truth, that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you. After this assault on the treacherous and the persistently sinful, and after condemning their supporters, argumentators and advocates, the commentary now makes a principled statement about this evil act and its consequences: what their reckoning and accounting will be in the Hereafter, what their general punishment should be, how Allah treats such criminals, and then that you too should deal with criminals and with one another in the same way as Allah has described, and adopt the morals Allah has taught, especially in matters of justice and fairness.

Lesson 39 at a glance:

The verses point to a story for which there is no parallel on this earth, and none similar to it in the whole history of humanity. This too is a witness that this religion is from Allah and must be from Allah. For however lofty human notions of justice and equity may be, however pure the human soul may become, and however firmly human temperament may stand upon the Straight Path, they cannot raise themselves to that lofty station to which these verses point. This can be achieved only through divine revelation. The graph drawn on the horizon of human history is so high that humanity has reached that station only under the shade of the Islamic system of life, and in future too this exaltation can be attained only under the Islamic system.

This event occurred when the Jews of Madinah were employing every poisoned arrow and weapon in their quiver against Islam and the Muslims, the details of which have already been explained in this surah, in Surah al-Baqarah and in Surah Ali 'Imran. The circumstances were such that the Jews were spreading every kind of false propaganda against Islam. They were forming a front of the polytheists against Islam, encouraging the polytheists, paving the way for them, spreading false news in their propaganda, and corrupting people's minds. They insulted the leadership of the Messenger ﷺ and created doubts about revelation and prophethood. They also tried to create internal disorder within the Islamic society, and day and night they were busy gathering the enemies of Islam to attack the Muslims. The Islamic movement was entirely new in Madinah, and traces of jahiliyyah were still present in human souls. Some Muslims still had kinship and other ties with Jews and polytheists, and all these matters were a source of danger to the ranks.

In such difficult, dangerous and emergent circumstances these verses were revealed, and these strict instructions were given to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Muslims. The purpose was that justice should be done to a Jewish accused: the charge of theft against him was false, and those who had leveled the false accusation were obliged to make amends for it. He belonged to a household of the Ansar of Madinah. The Ansar were the treasure of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who in the face of all these Jewish conspiracies were his supporters and helpers, and aides to his prophethood and religion.

How lofty is this standard of magnanimity, exaltation, justice and equity! No words can be found to praise and describe it. All statements, all comments and all explanations fall short of this standard and level. Human powers cannot by their own effort reach this level and standard; human beings alone cannot perform this miracle. It is the leadership and guidance of the Islamic methodology that can raise a human being to that lofty station.

The story that was narrated in connection with the background of these verses, and which several sources have transmitted, is worth hearing from the Ansar. Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man and his paternal uncle Rifa'ah both fought alongside the Messenger ﷺ in some expeditions. Once one of them lost his coat of mail (Rifa'ah's). It was commonly suspected that a man from the Ansar family of Banu Ubayriq had stolen this coat of mail. The owner lodged a report with the Messenger ﷺ that Tu'mah ibn Ubayriq had stolen his coat of mail. Some narrations mention the name Bashir ibn Ubayriq. It was also well known about him that he would write verses satirizing the companions and spread them around, claiming that they belonged to a certain Arab poet. When the thief learned that a report had been lodged against him, he quickly threw the coat of mail into the house of a Jew named Zayd ibn Samin, and told some people of his family that he had made the coat of mail disappear and thrown it into the house of so-and-so, and that it would soon be found in his house. "Go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and say that our brother is innocent, that so-and-so is the thief, and that we have gathered information about this matter. Ask him to publicly acquit our man and clear him, for if he is not honourably acquitted by Allah through you, his honour will be ruined."

When the Messenger ﷺ learned that the coat of mail had indeed been found in the Jew's house, he announced in the assembly that Ibn Ubayriq was innocent. For his family had requested of the Messenger ﷺ that Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man and his uncle had come to a Muslim family of theirs and made it a suspect of theft, and they had done this without any proof or evidence. Qatadah says: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and spoke with him, and he said: "You deliberately leveled a charge of theft against a family whose Islam and goodness are well known, and without proof." I returned, but my condition was such that I kept saying that if all my wealth had gone and I had not spoken to the Messenger ﷺ, it would have been better. Then my uncle Rifa'ah came and said to me: "Nephew, what have you done?" So I told him what the Messenger ﷺ had said, and Rifa'ah said: "Allah is the helper." Not long after this, these verses were revealed.

﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book with the truth, that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you. And do not be an advocate for the treacherous.﴾ (4:105) That is: do not be an advocate defending the Banu Ubayriq. "Khasim" means an advocate, one who defends, and one who argues and disputes on someone's behalf. Seek forgiveness of Allah for what you said to Qatadah; indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. Furthermore, the verses from "Wa la tujadil" to "rahima" ... and "If they seek forgiveness, Allah would forgive them" ... likewise from "Wa man yaksib" to "ithman mubina" and from "Wa lawla fadl Allah" to "ajran 'azima" ... When these verses were revealed, the Messenger ﷺ brought the coat of mail and gave it to Rifa'ah. Qatadah says: when the coat of mail reached my uncle, he was old and his sight had been lost in the days of jahiliyyah. I used to think that he had become Muslim under compulsion. When I gave him the coat of mail, he said it was in the way of Allah. From this point I became certain that he had been a true Muslim. When these verses were revealed, Bashir (the thief) joined the polytheists. Then further verses were revealed.

﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him, and follows other than the way of the believers, We will leave him in what he has turned to and burn him in Hell, and evil it is as a destination. Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He should be associated with, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. And whoever associates others with Allah has certainly gone far astray.﴾ (4:115–116)

Issue: It was not merely that an innocent man was acquitted who had been accused through a conspiracy, although the acquittal of an innocent person before Allah is itself a great matter; the matter was even greater and more important than that. Namely, the scales of justice were to be kept perfectly balanced, so that they would not incline to either side: neither toward carnal desires nor because of partisanship, neither through friendship nor enmity; in the balance of justice there should be no tilt in any way. In short, whatever the circumstances, justice must be done and must be impartial.

The issue was that this new society had to be purified of all impurities, and the remaining traces of jahiliyyah and partisanship had to be erased from within it, whatever form they took, especially when they touched the question of justice for the common people. After this, the foundation of a society was to be laid that would be entirely unique and without parallel in the whole history of humanity. This foundation was to be laid upon utterly pure and firm principles, in which prejudice, personal inclination, momentary expediency and personal desires would have no influence.

In this case there were countless reasons that could have justified leniency toward the wrongdoers, or at least that these verses would not have been revealed about them and they would not have been criticized, nor would they have been publicly disgraced or exposed in this way.

The first reason could have been that the first accused in this case was a Jew, and the Jews were people every arrow of whose quiver was used against Islam. The Jews were people who at that time inflicted the bitterest torments upon the Muslims, and as it happens, in every age they keep stinging the Muslims. Moreover, the Jewish outlook was that they recognized no one's right and did not deal justly with anyone. Their condition was that they had no moral value among them, and in dealing with Muslims they did not subscribe to any moral principle at all.

Another reason was that the real accused were Ansar, and the Ansar were those who gave refuge to the Messenger and supported him. Moreover, enmities from jahiliyyah had persisted between some Ansar households, and since the accusation and investigation had turned toward the Jews, the investigation could have been dropped here so that discord within the ranks of the Muslims could be avoided.

A third justification was that in this way a new weapon would come into the hands of the Jews to mislead the Ansar: that the Ansar and Muslims also steal from one another and then blame the Jews. The Jews could have used this incident too against Islam.

But this matter was of far greater importance than those trivial considerations; compared with all these concerns and calculations, this matter was very significant and lofty. These considerations had no importance from the Islamic point of view. Islam's aim was that this community be trained to such an extent that it would become ready for the system of earthly vicegerency and the office of human leadership. This community could not become ready for the leadership of all humanity and for vicegerency over the whole earth until it was trained upon extremely firm and superior principles; until the principles of the Islamic system of life became a part of its life; until its very existence was thoroughly washed and wrung out and purified, and it was cleansed of every kind of human weakness that had been part of its personality since the age of jahiliyyah; and furthermore, until a firm system of justice was established within this community itself, so that it might do justice among all people in accordance with it, and that its justice and its judgment would be free of all human weaknesses, and able to disregard all apparent expediencies.

In such circumstances, and at this most difficult stage, Allah placed the Muslim community upon the path of justice through the case of a Jew. This happened at a time when Muslims were the target of countless intrigues by the Jews, who were also busy forming a front against Muslims throughout the Arab world. They were also helpers and supporters of the hypocrites of Madinah, and they were using every arrow of their quiver against the religion of Islam and plotting against it at every turn. For the Muslims of Madinah the circumstances there were extremely dangerous, where they were surrounded by enmities and conspiracies, and all these plots came from the Jews. In these circumstances Allah chose a Jew to guide His servants and to set the signpost of the path.

The selection of a Jew in these circumstances was made so that Allah could make the community understand what the standard of justice is, and teach this community what Allah wished to teach it. Therefore in this matter there was no politics in Allah's policy, no so-called intellectual manoeuvring, and no verbal trickery. Nor was use made of cover-ups or the skill of concealing facts, and the matter was stated plainly.

In the judgment of this case, all expediencies were set aside and all circumstances and conditions were disregarded.

The matter was extremely realistic and serious. There was no veneer or whitewashing in it. Realism is one of the most important characteristics of the Islamic system of life, and it is an important attribute of this community. It is among the aims of this community that it spread justice among people and raise justice to the standard that humanity had never reached before, and that this community reached it only through revelation and guidance from Allah alone.

When a human being reached that lofty station, he saw that in every era and age of history, humanity lay in the deep pit of its lowliness. He saw that on the path to reaching that lofty station there were very deep ravines. Along this path, at every point, there are countless obstacles of cunning, outward show, politics, deceit, eloquence, skill, the expediency of government, the expediency of the country, and the expediency of the party, and so on, which under various names and titles stand blocking the way of justice. And if from that height a person looks at all systems of life with a discerning eye, he will see nothing but filth in the world.

When a person casts his gaze from that height, he sees that the Muslim community stands alone in this field, having risen above these filths of life and reached that pure station; and the landmarks of the Muslim community alone are seen at various points along the highway of history, and only the Muslim community has laid down the paths to reach that lofty peak of justice and equity, and it is unique in this field.

As for the filth and stench that jahiliyyah of old and jahiliyyah of modern times call justice, it is proper that we leave that filth buried, for its stench would pollute this pure atmosphere and foul odour would spread everywhere.

It is appropriate now that we discuss the verses in somewhat more detail.

Lesson 39: Explanation of the verses 105 to 113

(A) The matter is being stated with great severity. It appears as though anger and wrath are being employed on behalf of truth, and strong zeal is being shown for establishing justice, and feelings are apparent from the atmosphere and tone of the speech.

The commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah an-Nisa 4:105–109 (part 2 of 2):

This is also made clear by the fact that the Messenger (ﷺ) is addressed and told that We have sent down this Book with truth so that you may judge among people by what Allah has shown you. He was strictly forbidden to become a partisan of the treacherous and not to defend them, and he was told to seek forgiveness from Allah for the dispute he had raised on behalf of those treacherous people.

(Verse) "Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between people by what Allah has shown you, and do not be a advocate for the treacherous. And seek forgiveness from Allah; indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful." (4:105–106)

(O Prophet (ﷺ), We have sent down to you this Book with truth, so that you may judge among people according to the right guidance Allah has shown you. Do not become a pleader on behalf of the dishonest. And ask Allah for forgiveness; indeed He is most forgiving and merciful.) [A]

After this, the prohibition is repeated and it is said that those on whose behalf you argued are wronging themselves, and the reason is that, since they are treacherous, and Allah does not love those who betray.

(Verse) "And do not dispute on behalf of those who betray themselves. Indeed, Allah does not love one who is treacherous and sinful." (4:107)

(Do not defend those who wrong themselves; Allah does not like anyone who is a betrayer and persistently sinful.)

Apparently they had betrayed other people, but in reality they were betraying themselves. They betrayed their own community and their own system, they betrayed their own principles and their distinguished standing, they betrayed the ummah of which they themselves were members... Moreover, from another aspect too, they were betraying their own souls. They were involving their souls in a crime whose punishment was very severe, where Allah would compel them and seize them and punish them. Clearly this too is a betrayal of one's own soul. A third form is that they were involving their consciences in betrayal by calling the truth a lie and committing crime.

(Verse) "Indeed, Allah does not love one who is treacherous and sinful." (4:107) Allah's disapproval is the greatest of all punishments. There is also another indication within this: that those whom Allah does not love, no one should support them, and no one should advocate for them, because by committing crime Allah has disliked them. After calling these people treacherous and persistently sinful, their portrait is now drawn in this way and their veil is torn away:

(Verse) "They hide themselves from people, but they cannot hide from Allah, and He is with them when they conspire at night with words He does not approve..." (4:108)

(They may conceal their deeds from people, but they cannot conceal them from Allah, for He is with them when they plot by night in speech that does not please Him.)

This portrait is extremely repulsive, and a person involuntarily laughs at it. In it their weakness and their scheming are plainly visible. They gather at night, plot to conceal their crime, and commit betrayal. They can conceal their crime from people, but not from Allah. Hiding from people has no meaning, for people cannot protect them from benefit or harm, and they cannot hide from the One who holds the power of benefit and harm. He is with them when they plot. He knows their outward and inward states. They practice deception and speak against the pleasure of Allah. How feeble is their position: from the One from whom they hide, they cannot hide. Why? Because:

(Verse) "And Allah is ever encompassing of what they do." (4:108) (Allah encompasses all their deeds.) If Allah encompasses all deeds absolutely, then what benefit will their secret plots at night bring them? Allah is present in that gathering with them; everything is within His sight and under His control. And this forceful attack is still ongoing, and it applies to all those who argue on behalf of treacherous and criminal people.

(Verse) "Here you are, you argued on their behalf in this worldly life, but who will argue with Allah on their behalf on the Day of Resurrection, or who will be their guardian then?" (4:109) (Yes, you argued on behalf of these criminals in the life of this world, but on the Day of Resurrection who will dispute with Allah on their behalf? Who will be their advocate there? They will certainly not escape that heavy day.)

After this assault on the treacherous and the persistently sinful, and after condemning their supporters, argumentators and advocates, the commentary now makes a principled statement about this evil act and its consequences: what their reckoning and accounting will be in the Hereafter, what their general punishment should be, how Allah treats such criminals, and then that you too should deal with criminals and with one another in the same way as Allah has described, and adopt the morals Allah has taught, especially in matters of justice and fairness.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 4, verses 110–112:

(Verses) 110 to 113.

These three verses lay down general principles according to which Allah deals with His servants with justice, and according to which people too, if they wish, can build a good society and, by acting upon these same principles, save themselves in their dealings with Allah.

In the first verse, the door of forgiveness has been kept wide open. If people repent, they will find the door of Allah's forgiveness open. Every sinner who repents has been given hope of forgiveness.

(Verse) "And whoever does evil or wrongs himself, then seeks forgiveness of Allah, will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful." (4:110)

(If anyone commits an evil deed or wrongs his own soul, and then asks Allah for forgiveness, he will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful.)

Allah exists, and His forgiveness and mercy exist, provided there is someone who asks for forgiveness, someone who seeks mercy, someone who turns back. A person who does evil sometimes wrongs others and sometimes wrongs himself (wronging oneself occurs when the evil does not extend to another, and its effect is confined only to his own self). In any case, the door of forgiveness is open for wrongdoers. If they seek forgiveness, if they return repentant, He not only forgives them but also shows mercy upon them. His door is open, there is no gatekeeper upon it, and His proclamation is a general proclamation, unrestricted and unconditional. Whenever they return repentant, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.

In the second verse, the principle is established that responsibility is individual. In punishment, it is a fundamental principle of the Islamic system of life that each person is himself responsible for what he does, and this principle creates both fear and tranquillity in the heart of every person. Fear, because he will set right his deeds and his actions; and tranquillity, because he will not be responsible for the affairs and misdeeds of others.

(Verse) "And whoever earns a sin, earns it only against himself. Allah is ever Knowing and Wise." (4:111)

(Verse) "And whoever commits a fault or a sin and then throws it upon an innocent person has certainly borne a slander and a manifest sin." (4:112)

According to this principle, the law of inheritance does not apply to crimes. Just as the People of the Church speak of inherited sin, in Islam there is no concept that another will bear the punishment for a crime or give its expiation. In Islam, every person is himself responsible for his deeds. According to this concept, every person will be cautious about his deeds, and will be content that he will not be seized for the crimes of others. This is a wonderfully balanced law, and a most balanced conception of life. It is an important element among the fundamental elements of the Islamic conception of life (see Khasa'is al-Tasawwur al-Islami). Human nature is content with this conception. The unrestricted justice of Allah is enforced, and man should adopt this principle of Allah concerning crime and punishment in the world.

The third verse speaks about the matter that committing a crime oneself and then imposing it upon another human being is a very great crime, and in the case under discussion, a crime was committed.

(Verse) "And whoever commits a fault or a sin and then throws it upon an innocent person, he has certainly borne a slander and a manifest sin." (4:112)

Slander means that a chaste person is accused, and sin is what a person commits and then places upon the shoulders of one who is free of blame. It is as though this person has taken up both upon his own head. As if it were a burden which this person is carrying. This is the style of the Holy Qur'an, that it presents truths and meanings in embodied form, and this is the miraculous style of expression of the Qur'an (see al-Tasvir al-Fanni fi'l-Qur'an).

Islam establishes its system of justice upon these three principles and punishes criminals according to them. It does not pardon any criminal if someone other than the offender falls within the scope of that crime. But at the same time, Islam also leaves open the door of forgiveness and repentance, and establishes that the door be kept open at all times for those who seek forgiveness and those who repent. Whenever they wish, they may knock upon it. Indeed, if they enter the court of Allah without permission and take refuge, forgiveness and mercy will cover them.

After this, Allah expresses His favour to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that had Allah not protected him, he would have fallen victim to the conspiracy of the conspirators and made some wrong decision. But Allah exposed the plot that they wished to hide from the people. They could not conceal it from Allah, for even at the time of night, when they uttered displeasing words, Allah was with them. Then Allah, by way of favour, reminds him that Allah bestowed upon him a favour by sending down to him wisdom and teaching him what he did not know, and this favour was for all of humanity, and this favour Allah embodied in his noble person, since his person was always in close nearness to Allah.

But the grace and kindness of Allah always remained with him, and Allah protected him, while those who plotted were themselves caught in their own plot and went astray by their own hands. And in the Seerah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) there are countless incidents of this kind: schemers plotted, Allah frustrated their plot, and their efforts came to nothing. Here Allah Almighty assures the Prophet (ﷺ) that His grace and mercy will remain with the Messenger of Allah, and that they will not be able to cause him any harm.

In connection with the fact that Allah protected you from the plot of those who schemed, and you were spared from the situation where, because of your judgment, the guilty would escape and the innocent would be punished, Allah Almighty reminds him of one of His great favours. It is that Allah placed upon you the crown of prophethood.

﴿And Allah has sent down to you the Book and wisdom, and has taught you what you did not know; and the grace of Allah upon you has been immense.﴾ (4:113)

This favour is in fact upon the whole of mankind, for Allah sent His final message for the guidance of humanity. It was no ordinary favour but a new birth for humanity, and through it humanity received a life in the way a person receives humanity and spirit for the first time. This favour, through which humankind was raised from the depths of jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance) and, through the Islamic system of life, was given honour and progress in the world and brought to a most exalted station, Allah described as a great grace.

Only the person who has undertaken a comparative study of Islam and jahiliyyah, who has observed the past and the present, and who has tasted jahiliyyah as well as Islam, can truly estimate the kindness and goodness of the Islamic way of life.

This favour was first mentioned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was the first to attain Islam, the first to taste it, and the first to know it, and he was the one most knowledgeable of Islam and the one who tasted it most fully.

﴿And He taught you what you did not know, and the grace of Allah upon you has been very great.﴾ (4:113)

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 4, verse 114:

Lesson No. 40: At a Glance

This lesson is connected with the previous lesson, and there are many links between the two. Some of its verses are an echo of the incident of the previous lesson. After that incident and the revelation of the divine word, Bashir ibn Ubayriq, who was involved in the theft, apostatised, became hostile to the Messenger of Allah, and returned to jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance) after Islam. Accordingly, this lesson speaks of jahiliyyah: jahili ideas, concepts, and the mischief of Satan in that system. It is explained that the boundary between Islam and jahiliyyah is shirk-laden belief. In the system of Allah there is no forgiveness for shirk.

Everything else is forgivable... In this lesson, secret plotting at night is also forbidden, and most of the things that are done in secret are not good. For example, in the theft incident of the previous lesson there was a secret conference (najwa). After the prohibition of najwa, goodness, recommended counsel and schemes for reform among people were excepted from it, because these are deeds of merit. Then, at the end, it is explained that reward with Allah is according to His own principles, and no personal desire has any role in it. The desire of neither the Muslims nor the People of the Book will enter into it. All matters will be according to Allah's unrestricted justice, and in accordance with the truth; and if the truth were to follow people's desires, the entire system of the heavens and the earth would be corrupted.

In short, this lesson, in its subject and its direction, is fully connected with the previous one. Besides this, it is a new link in the training of the Muslim community, whose preparation for the leadership of all humanity was the aim in view: such that it excels in organisation, and is aware of where the weaknesses lie in its ranks and where traces of jahiliyyah still remain, so that it may reform them. This is the purpose that has been kept in view throughout this surah. Several topics related to it have come under discussion, and it is also one of the important themes among the aims of the entire Holy Qur'an.

Lesson 40: Explanation of the Verses

Verses 114 to 126

(Verse) No. 114.

In the Holy Qur'an, najwa (secret consultation) is prohibited again and again. Najwa is when a group thinks about and gathers together over a matter separate from the Islamic community and separate from Islamic leadership. The method of Islamic training was that people would bring all their difficulties and problems to the Islamic leadership; if the matter was personal, they would present it in private, so that it would not spread among the common people; and if the nature of the matter was general, they would ask about it openly, that is, if the matter did not specifically concern the one asking.

The wisdom in this policy was that, because of it, no bloc or faction could form within the Muslim community, nor could it happen that parts of the community would separate on account of their own notions and difficulties, or go their own way according to their inclinations and opinions. Nor should it be the case that some members of the community would consult at night, decide on a matter, and present it during the day within the community as a decided matter. Although in the time of the Messenger ﷺ no matter could remain hidden: whatever they consulted about, Allah was with them, and when necessary He informed the Messenger ﷺ.

The mosque of the Prophet was the parliament of the Muslim community. People met there with one another, prayed there, and all the affairs of life were settled there. Furthermore, Islamic society was an open society (Open Society), in which all matters that were not related to the military secrets of the community, or to issues concerning people's personal lives and families which they would not wish to become known, were brought forward. Since Islamic society was an open society, it was a free and pure society, and in this society separate, secluded consultations at night were held only by those who plotted against it, or who gathered against one of its principles; and these people were generally hypocrites. That is why, whenever najwa took place, hypocrites took part in it.

This is a reality which is very beneficial for us. Islamic society must be purified of this. Whoever has any doubt about anything in it should present it before the general leadership. Or, if any difficulty arises, or any proposal is before them, or any tendency is seen, in such matters one should turn to the leadership.

Here the Holy Qur'an has permitted one form of najwa. In reality it is not najwa at all, although it has the form of najwa.

(Verse) "Except for one who enjoins charity, or what is right, or reconciliation between people" (4:114). (That is: if someone privately urges charity, or says something for a good deed, or for reforming people's affairs, then this is indeed a good thing.)

For example, two good and righteous men gather and consult one another: whether money should be spent to help a certain person, or on a certain task, because that person is in need and I know of his need; or that money should be spent on a certain work, come, let us do this. Or that differences have arisen between so-and-so and so-and-so, come, let us reconcile them. A society or association of such people can also be formed, which, through consultation, can cooperate with one another in a good work, provided that these works are not najwa, nor a plot against the Islamic system. Although in outward form it will also be najwa, the Qur'an has described it with the word "amr" (command/matter), because such a limited society sometimes settles its affairs at night in seclusion, and its aim is a righteous and good work.

However, for this kind of society too, it is necessary that its formation and activity be for the seeking of Allah's pleasure.

(Verse) "And whoever does that seeking the pleasure of Allah, We shall give him a great reward" (4:114).

That is: the purpose of giving charity to a person, and of reconciling so-and-so with so-and-so, must not be that the people doing these things become known in such a way that people say, "By God, these are very good people, who urge people to charity and work for reconciliation among people." In short, in this work their sole aim should be the attainment of Allah's pleasure. This is the distinction that exists between a deed done purely for Allah's pleasure and the reward of the Hereafter, and a deed done for some other purpose. Although outwardly both deeds look alike, one is registered in the register of good deeds, and the other is registered in the register of evil deeds.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 4, verse 115–116:

(Verse) "115 to 116."

Regarding the occasion of the revelation of these verses, it has been said that Bashir ibn Ubayriq apostatised and went and joined the polytheists of Makkah, although the truth had become clear to him. Previously he had been in the ranks of the Muslims, but he abandoned the way of the believers and adopted another way. However, this verse is general in its content and application. It applies to every situation in which opposition is being offered to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), in which disbelief, polytheism and apostasy are adopted in opposition to him, and it applies to all such events, ancient and modern.

The meaning of (al-mushaqqah) is that one person takes one piece and another takes the opposing piece in confrontation with him. And whoever opposes the Messenger of Allah in schism adopts the opposing side, the opposing camp, and the opposing party against the Messenger, and opposes the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in whatever is without party, front or organisation. This means that he brings a system of life opposed to the system of life enforced by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), a system which includes beliefs and ideas, which includes acts of worship, which includes a system of law and a system of government, and which covers all spheres of life. And all these matters are limbs of the collective body of the Islamic system. And the principle is that if these limbs are cut into pieces, the system cannot remain; its soul will depart. Whoever opposes the Messenger in schism is the one who either completely rejects the Islamic system of life, or accepts some parts and denies others. That is, he takes one part and leaves another.

It is the demand of Allah's mercy that the proof should not be left incomplete against them, and that they should not become deserving of the evil abode of Hell; therefore Allah sent Messengers to them. The Messengers presented the truth before the people; they made the path of guidance completely clear to the people. Then, if they reject it, they will choose misguidance. This was Allah's vast mercy, that He made this arrangement for this weak creation to walk upon the straight path. Then, when the truth has become clear to someone, the Messenger is present, and yet he chooses another way in opposition to the way of the Messenger, does not believe in him, does not obey him, and is not content with the Islamic system and the system of the Chosen One (ﷺ), then the proof is complete against him, Allah writes misguidance on his account, and then turns him towards the direction he has turned. Then Allah hands him over to the disbelievers; he becomes a companion of the polytheists, and now upon him that punishment becomes binding which Allah has proclaimed.

(Verse) "And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him, and follows a way other than the way of the believers, We shall turn him over to what he has turned to, and burn him in Hell, and evil is it as a destination." (4:115)

Translation: "But whoever opposes the Messenger, after the right path has become clear to him, and follows a path other than the path of the believers, We shall let him go in the direction he has turned, and cast him into Hell, which is the worst place of return."

The reason given for this evil end is that Allah's forgiveness can embrace every sin, but shirk is such a sin for which there is absolutely no forgiveness.

(Verse) "Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. And whoever associates partners with Allah has certainly gone far astray." (4:116)

"With Allah there is only no forgiveness for shirk. Everything else may be forgiven for whom He wishes. Whoever associates someone with Allah has gone far astray in misguidance."

As we have said earlier in the commentary of the verse on this same theme, the meaning of shirk is to associate other deities with Allah, as the Arabs did in the age of ignorance, and as other ancient ignorant peoples besides the Arabs did. Likewise, associating anyone else with the attributes of Divinity of Allah, especially the attribute of sovereignty, also constitutes the commission of shirk. For example, considering a human being to be a legislator. Just as the Qur'an has said regarding the shirk of the Jews and Christians that they have taken their rabbis and monks as lords besides Allah.

These people did not worship their rabbis and monks in the way they worshipped Allah, but they gave them the right of legislation. They also set the bounds of lawful and unlawful for them, and the Jews and Christians obeyed them in this matter. In this way they gave them a share of the attributes of Divinity, and therefore they were deemed polytheists. It was also said regarding them that they violated Allah's guidance in the matter of tawhid, although the command given to them by Allah was only that they should worship the One God alone, perform acts of worship to Allah alone, and take the command of Allah as the source of law along with commands and prohibitions.

According to Allah's explicit commands and declarations, there is no forgiveness for the sin of shirk, provided someone dies in the state of shirk. Other than shirk, all sins may be forgiven if Allah is pleased. The question is: why has shirk been declared such a grave crime that it is unforgivable? The real truth is that whoever commits shirk is excluded from the very sphere of goodness and benefit, and his nature itself becomes corrupted, and there remains no hope of his reform.

(Verse) "And whoever associates partners with Allah has certainly gone far astray" (4:116) ... If even one thread of the nature of such a person remained, it would keep him tied to the Oneness of Allah; but he has severed all ties. If someone repents of shirk, and repents a few minutes before death, he will still attain salvation. However, if the death throes have set in and he is a polytheist, then his end will be that (Verse) "We shall cast him into Hell, and evil is it as a destination." (4:115)

After this, Allah mentions some of the superstitions and myths of the age of ignorance. Among the shirkish superstitions prevailing in Arab ignorance was that they called the angels the daughters of Allah. These people also worshipped Satan, just as they had made idols of the angels. Furthermore, there were customs among them such that they would cut or slit the ears of the animals they dedicated as vows. These were offered to their deities, and in this way they altered the creation and making of Allah. And in this way they committed shirk, although the meaning of committing shirk is that a person corrupts his nature.

The Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 4, verses 117–120:

(Verses) 117 to 120,

In the age of ignorance (Jahiliyyah), the Arabs believed that the angels were the daughters of Allah. Then they would make idols of the angels and name them after women: al-Lat, al-Uzza, Manat and others. Then they worshipped these idols, and they worshipped them on the basis that these were the idols of Allah's daughters. In this way they made them a means of nearness to the divine presence. In the beginning, this was how they had started shirk. After this, they forgot the reality of that story and began to worship these idols in themselves. Then, when they went further, they began to worship stones in general. In the fourth part (juz') we have given some details of this.

Some of them, in their own right, were also worshippers of Satan. This verse is explicit on this matter. Al-Kalbi says that the branch of Khuza'ah, Banu Mulayh, used to worship jinn. But the meaning of this verse is very broad, in that they would call upon Satan in their shirk and seek help from him. The story of Satan with their forefather Adam was well known, and Allah had declared him accursed. This was because he had announced his enmity towards man. When Allah expelled him from His presence, he became very angry with man and became his bitter enemy. He asked Allah for a respite, so that He would give him an opportunity to mislead those who do not take refuge in the secure fortress of Allah.

﴿Those who invoke besides Him none but females, and they invoke none but a rebellious Satan. Allah cursed him, and he said: "I will surely take from among Your servants an appointed portion. I will mislead them, I will arouse in them desires, I will command them and they will slit the ears of cattle, and I will command them and they will alter the creation of Allah."﴾ (4:117–119)

They call upon Satan, who is their ancient enemy. They take guidance from him and seek his help in this error, although this Satan is the one upon whom Allah has cast His curse. Allah has made clear that his intention is to mislead a large part of the children of Adam and to make them captives of false hopes and false desires. They will remain lost in false pleasures, illusory successes and pleasing hopes of the Hereafter. Moreover, that Satan who openly declared his intention, will cause these humans to commit most vile and foolish acts. They will hold extremely feeble notions and will decide religion on the basis of mere stories and tales. For example, by slitting the ears of certain animals they will say that riding on it is now forbidden, or that eating its flesh is forbidden, although Allah has issued no such command. Also, they will make unwarranted changes in human nature and the creation of Allah, for example by cutting parts of the body, and altering the forms of humans and animals, for example by castrating slaves and making marks on their skin. In short, these and all other unnatural acts and conduct, which neither sound human nature nor Islam permits.

The awareness that the ancient enemy of man, Satan, is the one who propagates shirk and shirkish ideas, and is the one who incites people towards idol worship, frees man at least from needing their whispers, which come from the enemy. Islam has declared this struggle of life to be a battle between man and Satan, and has directed the full strength of man towards struggling against Satan in this battlefield and against all the mischief he creates on this earth. They should gather under the banner of Allah and the party of Allah, because this battle between man and Satan is a continuous war. When it has been declared to be an eternal war, one does not tire of it in this war. The believer also does not become heedless of it, nor can the believer step out of this war, because he knows that in this war he will either be a follower of Allah or a friend of Satan. There is no third position between them at all. The technique of Satan is that he instils lust, pleasure and luxury in the hearts of people. Then he carries out his work in the guise of polytheists, mischief-makers and debauchees. A Muslim confronts him with himself and his companions, and throughout life this long and unending war continues.

Whoever takes Allah as his helper succeeds, and whoever becomes a companion and helper of Satan, and Satan assists him, is destroyed.

﴿And whoever takes Satan as a guardian instead of Allah has certainly suffered a manifest loss.﴾ (4:119)

The Qur'an also portrays the role that Satan plays through his companions. Observe what his method of deception is in misleading:

﴿He promises them and arouses desires in them, but Satan promises them nothing except delusion.﴾ (4:120)

Satan's method of misguidance is that he makes the evil deeds of man appear very attractive in his eyes. He does this with great deceit. He convinces them that their benefit and their worldly and otherworldly success lie in the path of disobedience. In this way man enters into companionship with Satan. He convinces them that through these deeds they will attain salvation, and thus man happily advances towards destruction. Yet ﴿Satan promises them nothing but delusion﴾ (4:120).

Despite this very clear depiction of Satan's method of operation, this eternal enemy spreads his snares and lays his nets, and gradually drives his prey towards them. It is only those whose nature has changed and in whose souls all traces of righteousness have been erased who fall into his net and trap. Such people are heedless and asleep, and they do not consider the path on which they are being led or the deception into which they are being drawn.

While the message being given to awaken the people of guidance was doing its work, and the thoughtful mind was still contemplating the nature of this battle, suddenly the end of those whom Satan had ensnared is revealed, those in whom he had established firm assurance of his plan and upon whom his announced sorcery had taken effect. Alongside this, the end of those who escaped Satan's snare also appears on the screen, because they had truly believed in Allah. Those whose faith is firm are protected from Satan's snare, because Allah has cursed Satan, and because when Allah granted him the opportunity to lead people astray and mislead them, He said that you will not be able to harm My sincere servants. Accordingly, he has always been weak against the sincere servants of Allah, so long as they held firmly to the rope of Allah. Reflect carefully!

﴿Whoever takes Satan as a guardian instead of Allah has certainly suffered a manifest loss.﴾ (4:119) ﴿He promises them and arouses desires in them, but Satan promises them nothing except delusion.﴾ (4:119–120)
