Lesson No. 24: An Overview

This lesson too is an example of the training of the Muslim ummah by the hand of divine power, concerning which Allah Himself has said that this is a good community, brought forth for mankind. This lesson is also an important link in the Islamic system of life, which is an extremely firm system, whose aims and objectives are fixed, and which has been sent down for the betterment of the human self. Through it, the human self is treated in such a way that the same hand of power which created the human being is also treating its weaknesses. This treatment is successful because Allah is aware of this distinguished creation of His and of every detail of its workmanship. He knows its reality and essence well, is acquainted with its inclinations and tendencies, and has knowledge of its needs and of its most hidden abilities and weaknesses.

In this lesson, the principles of the Islamic system of life are described as extremely firm, immutable principles, which are permanent, for every age, every place and every era, so that they may raise humanity from the depths of jahiliyyah (ignorance) to the highest heights, and carry it further beyond whatever heights humanity has already reached. Alongside these principles, this lesson also describes some features of the first community of Muslims, which was the first audience of this Qur'an. In the mirror of these verses, the first Islamic movement appears very beautifully as a human community. Human weaknesses are visible in it, and so is the standard of lofty purity. In this community, the remnants of the period of jahiliyyah and natural weaknesses are also visible. The Qur'an, while training this community, takes up each weakness one by one and treats it, then strengthens the community and makes it an exemplary community. It is enjoined that they should hold firmly to truth, strive in the path of the Truth, and make sacrifices.

The lesson begins with a call addressed to the Muslim community: you are the best community, and in this world you have a defined role. Gird yourselves to fulfil it, and establish in the world a standard of justice which is the highest standard in human history and an exemplary justice. In establishing justice, your aim and objective should be the attainment of the pleasure of the Divine Being, and in this matter do not keep in view any other impulse, any other desire or any other interest. In this matter, do not keep in view even the interests of your own community, your own government or your own nation. Your only motive should be the fear of God and the pleasure of Allah. The ummah actually did this, and the Qur'an itself recorded an example of it in the form of the incident of the false accusation against a Jew, and in this regard Allah directed and emphasized to His Prophet, through revelation, to do justice, the account of which we have given in detail earlier.

The lesson begins with the command: do justice, absolute and pure justice. How difficult absolute and pure justice is, only the Lord of the worlds knows, who created man. The Lord knows what difficulties arise on this path. Allah knows what aspects of human weakness exist. He knows how human emotions are, toward one's own self, toward relatives, toward the weak and the powerful, especially parents and close relatives, toward the poor and the rich, toward friends and enemies. Besides these, there are countless other emotions, and any one of them, or all of them together, can influence justice, and to disregard them is an extremely difficult task. This task is as difficult as a man climbing an extremely steep ascent while keeping in view only the pleasure of Allah and the rope of Allah. How difficult this task is!

The second call in this lesson is to complete faith: believe in Allah, His books, His angels, His messengers and the Last Day. This is complete faith. Each of its parts has great importance in its own place. These parts together complete faith, and from these parts the overall Islamic conception of life comes into being, which holds greater excellence than all other conceptions that have prevailed in human societies at any time, before Islam and after it. This worldview, in itself, is stronger and superior to every other worldview, and from it all other values come into being, whether they are moral, social or organizational. These were practically demonstrated in the life of the first Islamic community, and in later periods too, whichever community truly affirmed faith in this system and fulfilled its requirements, the same supremacy and superiority came into being in its life. This principle will remain established until the Day of Resurrection, and on the Day of Resurrection the word of Allah alone will prove true and supreme. This is the meaning of this verse: ﴿And Allah will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers﴾ (4:141).

After these two calls, Allah now begins a critical attack on the hypocrites. Some of them are those who still conceal their hypocrisy, and some are those who, after remaining hypocrites, have openly declared disbelief again. In this critical account, the temperament of the hypocrites, their detestable state, the details of the situation of their activities within the Islamic ranks, their fluctuating position—that if the Muslims are victorious they flatter them, and if the people of disbelief gain victory, they sit with them and everywhere claim themselves to be the cause of victory—are described. They go to prayer with extremely heavy steps, and pray only for show. Their attitude is extremely wavering: neither with these nor with those.

In the midst of this critical attack, guidance is also given throughout to the believers, from which it becomes clear how the hypocrites had infiltrated the Islamic ranks at that time and what mischief they were carrying out, and how much influence the hypocrites had within the Islamic ranks. In these circumstances, the need for such a critical attack arose so that, keeping in view the existing conditions of that time, the Islamic movement might be advanced step by step, and the believers be encouraged to gradually distance themselves from the hypocrites and avoid keeping relations with them, not sitting in their gatherings, where they often speak blasphemous words and mock the signs of Allah. However, in this period the Qur'an did not, in any case, command a boycott of the hypocrites, from which it is known that at the time these verses were being revealed, the band of hypocrites was very strong and so active that a complete boycott of them was simply not possible for the people of Islam.

While warning and admonishing the Muslims, it was also explained what the signs of hypocrisy are and how hypocrisy begins, so that they themselves might strive to protect themselves from the signs of hypocrisy. The very first guidance given is: do not at all make friendship with the hypocrites, and do not be greedy to increase your honour and respect in the eyes of the hypocrites, because honour belongs only to Allah. Allah does not at all like that He should give the disbelievers superiority over the people of Islam, and the hypocrites will be disgraced in this world and the Hereafter. Behold this is their picture; and then in the Hereafter they will be lying at the very bottom of Hell.

In this manner, these guidances and warnings show how the Islamic system of life corrects the human self and the habits deeply rooted within it, and how Islam begins the process of reform within an existing practical situation. Islam brings about change with great gradualness, and ultimately, by completely transforming some existing situation, brings in its place an entirely new state of affairs. Furthermore, it also shows what the conditions of the Muslims were in that period, how the fronts of disbelief and hypocrisy supported one another, and how they were colluding against the Muslim community and the religion of Islam.

Upon reflecting on all these commentaries, it becomes clear what a great battle it was into which the Qur'an had thrown the Muslim community, and according to which system and methodology the Qur'an was leading and guiding the Muslim community and the human self while placing them in that battle. This battle is the same battle that has continued between Islam and jahiliyyah in every time and place, and never comes to an end. The means may change and the faces may change, but the nature of the war between Islam and jahiliyyah today is the same as it was in the first century. Furthermore, these verses also show how great is the importance of the leadership and guidance of the Qur'an in the activities of the Muslim ummah. The Qur'an gives this leadership just as it did in the time of the Prophet ﷺ, and it gives the same guidance and leadership today. The Qur'an did not come merely for the guidance of one age or one generation; it is the constitution of this ummah, its guide and its mentor, and it is for every age and every generation.

And at the end of this lesson, a point for reflection: what concern does Allah have that He should punish people needlessly? His only demand is that you believe and render due thanks to Allah. If people do not believe and do not become grateful servants, He cares nothing for it; He is free of need from both their faith and their gratitude. The guidances that Allah is giving are for their reform, to bring them gentleness, so that they become deserving of rewards in Paradise. If they violate these guidances and turn back on their heels, they themselves will become deserving of the punishment of Hell. In this there is only their own personal loss, and the hypocrites will be in the most dangerous "lowest depth" (darak asfal) of that Hell, the lowest of all levels.

Lesson No. 42: Explanation of the Verses 135 to 147

Verse 135:

This is a special address to the believers. In this address, a new title and a new attribute are employed for them, and in this title and attribute they are entirely unique. The spirit of "Those who believe" has changed; their conceptions have become entirely new; their principles and objectives have changed and become new. They have become the leaders of this new revolutionary mission, and great responsibilities have been placed upon their shoulders; now they are guardians and custodians for all of humanity. They are now the ones who judge among people. Therefore, the words "O you who believe" here are of extreme importance. That is, because of this very attribute of faith, the responsibility of world leadership has been placed upon them, and leading the whole world is, as it were, a requirement of faith, and as a requirement of the attribute of faith itself, Muslims were at that time preparing to take charge of this position of leadership.

This is a very effective glimpse of Islamic methods of training. And this glimpse was shown before entrusting the Muslim ummah with a very heavy responsibility, and that heavy responsibility is this:

﴿O you who believe! Be steadfast in upholding justice, bearing witness for Allah, even though it be against yourselves or your parents and close relatives. Whether he be rich or poor, Allah is more concerned with both of them﴾ (4:135).

This trust and responsibility was that you must establish justice, and this justice will be absolute, of which you must become the standard-bearers. In every condition and in every field you must act justly. Such justice that through it oppression and transgression are automatically negated, and that nowhere on the whole face of the earth oppression remains, and this justice is such that every person with a right receives his right. In this giving of rights, believer and non-believer are equal, as has been clearly stated in the story of the Jew. In it, relatives and non-relatives are all equal... friends and enemies are all equal. The rich and the poor have one and the same status.

﴿Be steadfast in upholding justice, bearing witness for Allah﴾ (Be standard-bearers of justice and witnesses for Allah)

This justice and testimony should be solely for Allah, and its relationship should be with Allah alone; testimony should be given neither for the sake of those in whose favour it is being given, nor because of those against whom it is being given. This testimony should not be for the interests of any individual or any group, nor should testimony be affected by the circumstances prevailing at the time or by factors influencing the case under discussion. It should be given purely for Allah and purely dealing with Allah, solely for His pleasure, and in such circumstances that no inclination, no tendency, no interest and no desire affects it, and no one is being favoured.

﴿Even though it be against yourselves or your parents and close relatives﴾ (4:135)

Here, the Islamic system is arming the human soul against itself: against its own feelings, against its own self, against its parents and against its relatives. It is an extremely difficult stage for a person to render a judgment against himself. Mere verbal talk is easy, but in practice doing so is extremely hard. A person can think mentally that it ought to be so, but acting on it is difficult, and the real difficulties of this matter are felt only when a person actually does this work. Despite the fact that it is a difficult task, the Islamic system, through taqwa (God-consciousness), is arming the believing soul against its own self, so that it plunges into this dangerous experiment, because the standard of justice in the world should be this: that a person judges even against himself if truth and justice demand it. And some people do make this judgment in practice and show it.

After this, the human soul is also armed against its natural and collective consciousness, namely when the person in whose favour or against whom testimony is being given is poor. If he is poor, the difficulty is that a compassionate person does not like to give testimony against him out of compassion, and prefers to give testimony in his favour because of his weakness. Or, due to some collective rank and status, or due to the class hatred of a society, someone may hate a weaker person, or, if the opponent is rich, may respect his standing and not give testimony against him. All the systems of jahiliyyah have always been like this. It may also happen that a witness harbours hatred for a wealthy person, and his wealth and superiority are not pleasing to him, and because of this he does not give the testimony of truth but gives testimony against the rich man. These are all natural inclinations, and when a person actually faces them, at the time of justice and testimony they exert their weight upon him. This is why the Qur'an took up all these matters, saying: whether it is the self, or relatives, or the poor or the rich, you must give the testimony of truth.

﴿Whether he be rich or poor, Allah is more worthy of both of them﴾ (4:135). This is an extremely difficult and heavy task. Islam placed the believers into practical life and raised them to such a height that the whole of humanity saw it, so that Islam showed on this earth, within the world of humanity, a great miracle. It was a miracle that could occur only under the shadow of the Islamic system.

﴿So do not follow your desires, lest you deviate from justice﴾ (4:135). The desires of the self come in many kinds, some of which we have mentioned above. Love of oneself, love of family, love of relatives, compassion toward a poor man, (at the time of testimony) favour toward a rich man and regard for his standing, hatred toward a rich or poor man, and so on, are all desires of the self. Partiality toward clan, tribe, nation, homeland and government (at the time of testimony), and hatred toward an enemy even if they are enemies of the religion, are all such desires. In short, desires have countless kinds and hues. Allah does not like the believers to be influenced by all these desires, and He forbids them, under such influence, from refraining from justice and the testimony of truth. Finally, it is warned: do not distort testimony at all, and do not turn away from giving testimony either.

﴿And if you distort or turn away, then indeed Allah is ever Acquainted with what you do﴾ (4:135). In this matter, only this reminder is given: whatever you do, Allah is aware of it, so that the impression becomes firm in the believers that if they do not do so, its consequence will be very bad, so that their hearts tremble, because the addressees of these verses of the Qur'an are none other than the believers.

It is related in the narrations that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Abdullah ibn Rawahah ؓ to collect the revenues of Khaybar (it should be remembered that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had agreed with them on half of the revenues), and he went there after the conquest of Khaybar, the Jews offered him a bribe so that he would be lenient with them. He said to the Jews: "By Allah, I am the representative of One who is more beloved to me than this whole world. By Allah, I regard you as worse than monkeys and pigs, but the love of the Messenger ﷺ and your hatred cannot move me to do anything other than justice between you." The Jews then said: "It is because of such people that the system of the heavens and the earth is established."

Abdullah ibn Rawahah ؓ was a student of the school of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and his education and training had been on the divine methodology. He was a human being, and with full human feelings he sat on the seat of a court and succeeded. And there were no lesser others, apart from him, who under the shadow of the Islamic system displayed the miracle to the world.

Years upon years passed, centuries elapsed, and this era has gone very far away, and libraries have filled with books of jurisprudence and law. Legal codes and rules and regulations of justice have multiplied, and departments and ministries of law and justice have been established. And minds have turned upon hearing the name of justice again and again. The longest speeches and articles about doing justice in the world have been read. Several theories have arisen regarding justice, and several organizations have come into existence, and conferences have been held, but where is that true justice? No one has tasted its flavour. This justice has remained rare in people's consciences and in their lives. And despite these arrangements, this justice has not reached that high standard which was the distinguishing mark of the best generations. Its true existence, if it was anywhere, was only in the era of the Islamic system. In that brief era, the graph of justice rose to such a height, and after the Prophethood and the Rightly Guided Caliphate, if it was found anywhere, it was found only within the Islamic society, and only in those hearts in which Islam was embedded, and in those individuals and those societies whose training had already taken place under the shadow of the Islamic system. This was certainly a unique and exemplary just system.

Those who today construct the most modern judicial systems, who employ the most modern means for justice and set out extremely complex procedures for the judiciary, should keep in view the matters we have mentioned above. These people think that this procedure is complicated and that these highly organized judicial structures will be more beneficial than those simple and very primitive arrangements adopted in the Islamic era. These modern people, in whose hands the administration of the judiciary lies, may think that they are very successful, but in reality this is not so.

This is an illusion, and this illusion arises because people seek to learn the reality by looking at outward bulk, whereas the reality of things is not known from their outward bulk. It is the Islamic system alone that reached such a high standard within those simple conditions, and even today it is Islam alone that can bring the standard of justice to that level, provided it is adopted.

But this does not mean that we should not benefit from the modern arrangements of judicial systems and the civil and criminal codes in this modern, advanced age, or that we should abolish the modern organization and advanced forms of the department of justice and replace them with the simple form of the Rightly Guided Caliphate. Our meaning is that the real aim is not the form and organization, but the true objective is the spirit that operates within the outward form, whatever its outward shape and size may be, and whatever the systems, ideas and time and place may be.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 4, verse 136:

(Verse) "136.

This is a second call, addressed only to those who have already believed, and here they are addressed with this attribute and title, which distinguishes them from the jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic ignorance) spreading around them. This attribute determines their obligations and duties, and connects them with the source and fountainhead which is the real origin of their strength and superiority, the source from which they derive all their powers and resolve.

(Verse) "O you who believe, believe in Allah and His Messenger, and in the Book which He has sent down upon His Messenger, and in the Book which He sent down before." (4:136) (O you who have believed, have faith in Allah, in His Messenger, and in the Book which He has revealed to His Messenger and the Book which He revealed before.)

Here the constituent elements of faith are described. These are the matters whose presence in the faith and belief of every person is necessary. This is, as it were, the foundation upon which the doctrinal concepts of faith are established. Belief in Allah and belief in the Messengers connects a person with the Being who created him, and Allah then sent the Messenger so that he might guide mankind. Included in belief in prophethood is the matter that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) conveyed correctly the message that he gave from Allah.

The necessary consequence of belief in Allah and belief in prophethood is sincerity of faith. The Book which Allah sent through His Messenger is entirely true. In this Book Allah has described to mankind all the ways of conducting life, and this Book is a common bond among all the believers, and mankind must take this entire Book as guidance. It is not permissible that some matters be taken from it and enforced, while other parts of it are abandoned.

Among the fundamental elements of faith is also belief in all the previous scriptures. This is because the earlier prophets were also Messengers of Allah, those scriptures too were books of Allah, and the system of life prescribed in all of them was Islam itself. The teaching of all of them was that Allah alone is God, and that none shares with Him in any of the attributes of divinity; and the teaching of all of them was that obedience to and implementation of this system of life is obligatory. It is also a requirement of the belief in the oneness of Allah that all these books, before their distortion, were all from Allah. In them one and the same system was recorded, and concerning mankind, the will of Allah alone was recorded in all of them. There was one path, which was the straight path (sirat al-mustaqim), and all other paths around it were deficient and crooked.

The purpose of believing in all the books is that in reality all the books are one Book, which is al-Kitab. And this unity of thought is a distinguishing feature of the Muslim ummah alone. Its concept is that all heavenly scriptures are one Book, all heavenly religions are one religion; the guidance contained in them is one system, and their method is also one. This very concept fits truly with the reality of divinity, and it is also correct for humanity. This concept establishes that truth is one, and multiplicity in truth is not possible. Whatever lies beyond it is misguidance. (Verse) "So what is there after the truth but error?" (10:32) After commanding belief, a stern warning follows: that the denial of any of these elements of faith is absolutely intolerable, and within the negative statement the full detail of the elements of faith has been given.

(Verse) "And whoever disbelieves in Allah and His angels and His Books and His Messengers and the Last Day has certainly strayed far astray." (4:136) (Whoever denies Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers and the Last Day, and has wandered far off into error and gone very far away.)

In the first verse, belief in Allah, belief in the Books and belief in the Messengers were mentioned, and the angels were not mentioned. Clearly, the angels and the Last Day are included within Allah's Books. And the necessary requirement of believing in the Books is that one believe in the angels and the Day of Judgment; but in this second verse they have been explicitly mentioned, because after disbelief comes threat and warning, and one is frightened with punishment. Their explicit statement and clarification was necessary, so that tomorrow no one could say that the Resurrection and the angels were not specifically mentioned. In this verse the expression "far error" (dalal ba'id) is used, the meaning of which is that these people have gone so far along the path of misguidance that it is no longer possible for them to return to the path of guidance, nor can any hope be held of them in this regard.

The question is: the one who denies Allah, although every person believes in the Being of God personally and naturally, indeed the nature of every person believes in Him, and after denying God he then denies the angels, the Books and the Last Day, in reality he is carrying forward the denial of the Divine Being itself. The original nature of such a person has fallen victim to corruption, paralysis and deterioration. This is why the expression "far error" was used for such disbelief.

After addressing the Muslims with the attribute of faith and calling them twice, now an attack on the hypocrites begins, and this attack starts with mention of their real conditions at that time. Their stance is such that it closely resembles the hypocrites of today."

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 4, verse 137:

(Verse) "No. 137."

Disbelief that precedes faith: faith wipes away its traces entirely. A person who has never seen the light, and who remains in darkness, is excused. But to adopt disbelief after faith, and to do so repeatedly, is a grave sin, so grave that Allah will by no means forgive it, and no excuse can be offered for such an act. Disbelief is indeed a veil; when the veil is lifted, the innate nature (fitrah) becomes connected again with its Creator, and the one who had strayed rejoins the path. The plant returns to its nursery, and the soul tastes the sweetness of faith. Therefore those who repeatedly apostatise after faith are, as it were, fleeing from their fitrah, fleeing from knowledge, and deliberately falling into ignorance; and they deliberately set out upon the road of misguidance and loss. And then they go so far along that road that the way back is cut off from them.

This is why Allah has ordained that He will not forgive them, and that He will not return them to the path of guidance again, because they deliberately abandoned the path of truth, having previously walked upon it and attained its goal. They deliberately chose blindness and evil, whereas previously they were people of insight and travellers upon the Straight Path.

As long as the human self is not purified for the sake of Allah, it cannot be free from the pressure of customs, values, expediencies and interests. Nor can it be purified from greed and avarice, nor from considerations and hopes. And such a self can never be filled with dignity, loftiness, resolve and freedom in the way that the self filled with the love of Allah is. When a heart is filled with the love of Allah, it stands superior to worldly values, worldly ways, the events of the world, the people of the world, all the powers existing in the world, governments, and their adherents and allies.

From here the plant of hypocrisy sprouts. And you know what the reality of hypocrisy is? Hypocrisy is simply this: a person appears to be firm upon the truth outwardly, but is weak in fighting for it and in confronting falsehood. This weakness arises because fear and greed enter the human heart, and both these fear and greed are directed not toward Allah but toward other than Allah. The person then becomes a prisoner of earthly circumstances and earthly personalities, and drifts away from the Islamic system.

Therefore, in this lesson there is talk of faith, talk of standing firm as witnesses and of justice, and talk of hypocrisy, and there is a deep connection among the three. The general relevance is that these are indeed the principal themes of this surah: the training of the Muslim community within the Islamic system of life, and the removal of the traces of jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance) from its collective life; the preparation of the souls of the community's members against natural human weaknesses; and then bringing them into the struggle against the polytheists and hypocrites surrounding them. This is the central theme of this entire surah, around which it revolves from beginning to end.

For this reason, in the remaining part of this lesson the discussion is confined to the hypocrites, and this section of the juz' concludes with it. Earlier there was mention of a particular group of hypocrites who repeatedly declare Islam and then disbelieve. Now from here criticism of the hypocrites begins, about whom the Qur'an has explained the details and has studied their disease in various ways, so that the temperament of the Islamic system becomes clearly visible, is acted upon in accordance with fitrah, and appears clearly in hearts and in conduct.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 4, verse 138–143 (part 1 of 2):

(Verses) 138 to 143.

This critical sentence about the hypocrites begins with a note of mockery. Here, instead of apostasy, criticism of them begins with the word "bashir" (give good news). They are being given the good news of the punishment that awaits them. Afterward, the cause of the punishment is also stated: these people, instead of making friends with the believers, are making friends with the disbelievers. A second reason is that they have bad opinions of Allah. A third is that they do not know who gives honor and who gives humiliation.

﴿Give the hypocrites the good news that there is a painful punishment for them. Those who take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Do they seek honor from them? Surely all honor belongs to Allah.﴾ (4:138–139)

According to the preferred narrations, the disbelievers mentioned here are the Jews. The hypocrites would take refuge with them, hide in their homes at night, consult with them against the Muslims, and plot all kinds of conspiracies against the Muslims.

Allah asks in an interrogative manner: these people claim faith and yet make friends with the disbelievers. Why do they place themselves in such a position? Do these people seek honor from the disbelievers? Yet honor is with Allah, and honor is given only to the one who is a friend of Allah, who seeks honor from Allah's court, and who takes refuge with Allah.

Thus, in these verses, a glimpse of the hypocrites is shown. This is their first characteristic: they do not keep friendship with the believers and are friends of the disbelievers. They seek honor and power among the disbelievers, though the source of honor and power is Allah. Therefore, it is necessary that the search for honor and the search for power be made from Allah. If they seek it elsewhere, the search will be in vain, because this commodity is not available anywhere else.

Note this: in this universe, the human soul has only one support from which it can gain honor. When this soul bows before that support, it will become exalted over others. This one servitude and one prostration frees a person from all other prostrations. If the human soul does not begin to bow before Allah, it will have to serve many gods and many persons. It will have to observe many considerations, attend to various directions, and face various dangers, and all these considerations, observances, and servitude to different people will not be able to save it. This is because either there is servitude to Allah here, and then the person becomes exalted and honorable, or there is servitude to human beings, which is slavery and humiliation, and in which there is imprisonment instead of freedom. Now it is up to the human being to choose which of these to adopt: slavery or freedom.

No one who is a believer can seek honor from anything other than Allah. If he does so, he cannot be a believer. Likewise, if a believer seeks honor, support, and power from the enemies of Allah, he is not a believer. Today, those who claim Islam, bear Muslim names, and seek help in this universe from the enemies of Islam, more than anyone else need to reflect upon these guidances of the Quran, provided that they have a desire to be true Muslims. If they have no inclination toward this at all, then Allah is free from all the worlds.

Apart from other matters, it is also tantamount to seeking honor from the disbelievers when a person takes pride in those ancestors who died in disbelief, and considers that there is a bond of kinship between them and the Muslims. Just as some people take pride in the Pharaohs, some take pride in the Assyrians, some in the Phoenicians, some in the Babylonians, and the Arabs observe their pre-Islamic Arab ignorance and the community of ignorance.

Imam Ahmad narrated from Abu Rayhana, who said: the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever ascribes himself to nine disbelieving ancestors, intending by that to take pride in them, will be the tenth, who will be his companion in Hell."

The reason is that in Islam, unity is based solely on the ideology of life. In Islam, the ummah is based solely on the foundation of Islam and faith, and this has been so since the beginning of Islam. From the beginning of Islam until today, in every land, every place, and every lineage, this has been Islam's stance. The meaning of ummah is not that people of one lineage reside in one place at one time and thereby become one ummah.

Among the degrees of hypocrisy, the highest is that a believer sits in a gathering in which the verses of Allah are being denied, mocked, and he remains silent and turns a blind eye. Then he calls it tolerance, or wisdom, or breadth of heart, or freedom of opinion, though this stance is in reality an inner defeat that has seeped into his veins and sinews. He gives it this name so that people will not taunt him as weak and of weak faith. The truth is that such people hide their weakness behind these words.

Zeal for Allah, zeal for the religion of Allah, and zeal for the verses of Allah are in reality a great sign of faith. When this zeal ends, the dam breaks and all veils are removed. All barriers are removed, and when great pressure is applied, even the weak thread snaps. At first, Islamic zeal is suppressed, just as a spark is buried under ashes, and then it cools and goes out.

Whoever is in a gathering where his religion is mocked should either defend the religion or get up and leave the gathering. But if he turns a blind eye and remains silent, this is his first defeat. It is a state in which a person stands exactly in the middle of the bridge of hypocrisy, between faith and disbelief.

In Medina, there were some Muslims who sat in the gatherings of the great hypocrites, and these hypocrites were highly influential. Even after the Prophet's ﷺ migration, they still had influence and standing in society. Therefore, the Holy Quran warned the Muslims that going to such gatherings, and then listening silently as conversations against Islam proceed in those gatherings, is the first stage of defeat. So it was ordered that Muslims should abstain from such gatherings. But the circumstances were not such that the Quran would prohibit sitting in such gatherings absolutely, so here it was only ordered that when the verses of Allah are being denied and mocked, the Muslims should boycott them. If a Muslim takes part even in this situation, he is a hypocrite.

﴿And it has already been revealed to you in the Book that when you hear the verses of Allah being denied and mocked, do not sit with them until they engage in some other talk. Otherwise, you will be like them. Indeed, Allah will gather the hypocrites and the disbelievers together in Hell, all of them.﴾ (4:140)

Here, the reference given to "the Book" is this verse of Surah al-An'am: "And when you see those who engage in vain talk about Our verses, turn away from them until they engage in some other talk." The harsh statement here is: "Otherwise, you will be like them" and the severe warning that follows cuts through the matter: "Indeed, Allah will gather the hypocrites and the disbelievers together in Hell, all of them" (4:140).

However, only those gatherings are prohibited in which the verses of Allah are denied and mocked. And in the circumstances through which the Muslim community was passing at that time, Allah did not order a complete boycott. Such circumstances may occur in other societies and in future generations, and the method of the Islamic system of life is also that when it launches a movement, it takes it with great wisdom and gradualness. It takes into account the conditions existing in society, the actual situation, and people's thoughts and ideas, but the goal is always that this actual situation will be changed and that it will move continuously forward in that direction.

After this, some features of the hypocrites are described. Here a very unflattering picture of the hypocrites is painted, that when they stand with the Muslims their facial features are one way, and in that same scene, when they are seen standing with the hypocrites, their facial features are entirely different. They have made a strange state for themselves. They shift sides like insects and snakes. They are neither of this side nor of that side.

﴿Those who wait and watch over you. If there is a victory for you from Allah, they say, "Were we not with you?" And if the disbelievers get a share, they say, "Did we not gain control over you and protect you from the believers?" So Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection, and Allah will never grant the disbelievers a way over the believers.﴾ (4:141)

This is a strange picture and scene. It shows how deep a plot the hypocrites are weaving against the Muslims and how evil their intentions are. They are always waiting for the moment when some calamity befalls the People of Islam. But outwardly they express their love for the Muslims: if the Muslims achieve victory and win spoils, they will say at that time, "Were we not with you?" (4:141). By this they mean that we were with you at the time of battle, because the hypocrites sometimes went into the ranks of the Muslims and continued their intrigues. Or it means that they would say, "We too were your supporters and helpers, and if we did not go to battle, we were your helpers behind you."

﴿And if the disbelievers get a share, they say, "Did we not gain control over you and protect you from the believers?"﴾ (4:141) Their meaning is that they cooperated with the disbelievers, assisted them, and supported them, and did not speak the truth to the Muslims, and created unrest and chaos within the ranks of the Muslims.

Thus these people shifted sides like insects and snakes, and poison against Islam was filled in their hearts. Their mouths held sweet and smooth words, but they were people of weak character. From this picture it appears that they are extremely wretched and ugly, and that the People of Faith are disregarding them. This is the first glimpse of the Islamic system of life for the spirit of the believers. Under the watch and guidance of Allah, the policy of the Prophet ﷺ toward the hypocrites was to adopt a stance of turning a blind eye and gentleness toward them, and to alert and warn the Muslims against them, to make them aware of their true intentions, and thus to give them a sweet cup of poison. That is why, for their punishment, it is said: do not hasten in punishing them; Allah will judge them in the Hereafter. ﴿So Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection﴾ (4:141), where no plot will succeed, where no cunning and deceit will avail, and where no one will be able to hide what is in his heart.

At this point, the People of Faith are also reassured by a definite promise that these people will gain nothing from their deceit and cunning, that there will be no change in Allah's way through this, and that their plot with the disbelievers will not benefit them. The way of Allah is that He has never decreed that the disbelievers and hypocrites should prevail over the People of Faith.

﴿And Allah will never grant the disbelievers a way over the believers.﴾ (4:141)

Some narrations state that the domination of the disbelievers in this verse refers to domination on the Day of Resurrection, when Allah will judge between the People of Faith and the hypocrites and disbelievers, and the outcome for the believers will be good. But another narration also states that it means Allah will not grant the disbelievers such domination over the Muslims that they uproot them completely, although in some battles and some regions they may gain the upper hand. Even if this verse is taken to apply to both this world and the Hereafter, there is no harm, since there is no restriction or specification regarding the Hereafter in it.

If it is taken to refer to success in the Hereafter, then there is certainly no doubt about it. However, if worldly dominance is intended, then difficulties may sometimes arise and misunderstandings may also occur, which require explanation.

This is a firm and comprehensive promise of Allah, and a general rule of His. When the reality of faith settles in the hearts of the believers, and that reality becomes manifest in the true circumstances of their lives, and then this reality becomes their system of life and a system of government is established upon it, and every movement and every thought of theirs becomes for Allah, and they become servants of Allah in matters both small and great, then there is no way in the Sunnah of Allah for the disbelievers to overcome the Muslims. This is such a reality that not a single instance can be cited from Islamic history as an example to the contrary.

I say with great certainty that there can be no doubt about this promise of Allah. The true believers can never suffer defeat, and in history they have never been struck by any such defeat. And whenever it has happened, it has happened only at the time when their faith has weakened. Either their faith has weakened consciously, or a weakness has been found in their creed, or else some weakness has remained in their practice. Let it be remembered. It is the demand of faith that the believers remain ready for jihad at all times, and that this jihad be purely for the sake of Allah, with no other aim in view. And if there is any loophole in it, then defeat keeps occurring in accordance with that weakness. But as soon as the believers remove this weakness through faith and action, victory and triumph once again kiss their feet.

See, at Uhud the weakness was that the archers disobeyed the command of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) instead of obeying him, and the reason for this was only the greed for spoils of war. And at the Battle of Hunayn the weakness was that the Muslims became proud of their numbers and could not keep before them the true source of their strength. If we analyse every incident in our whole history in which we suffered defeat, we will find that there was some shortcoming of this kind present there. If we do not see any shortcoming anywhere, then this will be the fault of our understanding. As for the promise of Allah, it is true both in this world and in the Hereafter.

It should also be kept in view that sometimes a trial occurs purely because of the wisdom of Allah. The wisdom in it is that the Muslims should well realise their shortcomings in the obligatory deeds imposed by the requirements of their faith. As happened at Uhud, and on which Allah made a lengthy commentary. And when, because of that trial, the reality of faith, the obligatory deeds and the preparations became correct, then the help of Allah arrived and victory appeared before them, clearly manifest victory.

As for defeat, it is the defeat that is not in a single battle or skirmish; it is not a defeat. Its meaning is also very broad. It means spiritual defeat, the breaking of resolve. Defeat in a battle is acknowledged only when, under its influence, the defeated group's courage breaks and it sits down exhausted and disheartened. But if it generates fresh courage within itself, rekindles the torch anew, identifies its points of weakness, and comes to know the nature of that battle, the nature of this way of life, and what difficulties lie on this path, then that defeat will be a prelude to victory and triumph, even though the road becomes long.

When this verse says that Allah has not provided any way for the disbelievers to dominate, its meaning is that a believer is spiritually dominant, and victory comes only when the spirit and faith are dominant. Victory is in fact the victory of believing thought. That is why Allah calls upon the Muslims to be complete and perfect believers in their consciousness and conception, to be superior and perfect in their practical lives, that their conduct and character be superior, and that their confidence not rest merely on the title. Because help is not given to a name and title alone, but victory is granted to the reality behind the name and title.

For our victory and defeat there is only one condition, and that condition is that we complete the reality of faith, and after that bring about in our practical lives the changes that the demands of that reality of faith require. The reality of faith is that we prepare fully, and are equipped with the means of war and the experience of war. Among the completion of the reality of faith is also this: that we never bow before our enemies, and that we seek honour from Allah alone.

This emphatic promise of Allah accompanies the reality of faith fully, and in the same way there is this promise with the reality of disbelief as well. The reality of faith is that a person's connection is made with that great power which neither weakens nor becomes feeble. The meaning of disbelief is that someone cuts off his connection from that great power. It can never happen that a limited, broken-down, lonely power overcomes a power that is unlimited, one that is connected to its source of power, and which is the power of this whole universe.

But it should be kept in mind that there is a great difference between the reality of faith and mere outward appearance of faith. The reality of faith is that power which is solid, and is as firm and unalterable as the natural laws of this universe are solid and unalterable. And that reality of faith holds complete control over the personality of man and influences each of his movements. It is a great reality, and it guarantees that when it confronts the power of disbelief, which is lonely, cut off from its true source of power, and limited, this reality of faith overcomes the reality of disbelief. But if faith is not a reality but merely a form, then disbelief can overcome that form, provided disbelief is active within its reality and sincere in its reality of disbelief, not merely a form; for the reality of anything weighs heavier than a mere form, even if on one side there is a form of faith and on the other a form of disbelief.

The principle of Allah regarding the overcoming of falsehood is that truth and honesty rise up against it, and when truth exists in its reality, the contest between truth and falsehood is decided at that very moment, even though falsehood may appear very great and vast and dazzling to the eyes.

(Verse) "Rather, We hurl the truth against falsehood, and it crushes its head, and behold, it vanishes." (Sadaqa Allah al-'Azim) (And Allah has not provided for the disbelievers any way over the believers.)

After this definitive and decisive promise that the disbelievers cannot dominate or be superior over the believers, Allah presents another picture of the hypocrites, those who take the disbelievers as friends and seek honour with the disbelievers, and along with this picture comes their humiliation and chastisement.

(Verses) "Indeed, the hypocrites deceive Allah, but He is deceiving them. And when they stand up for prayer, they stand lazily, showing off to the people, and remember Allah only a little. Wavering between that, belonging neither to these nor to those. And whomever Allah leaves astray, you will not find for him a way." (4:142–143) (These hypocrites are practising deceit against Allah, whereas in reality it is Allah who has put them into deception. When they stand up for prayer, they stand up lazily, merely to show off to people, and they remember Allah only a little. Wavering between disbelief and faith, neither fully on this side nor fully on that side. And for one whom Allah has led astray, you cannot find any path.)

This is another glimpse of the Islamic system that is being shown to the hearts of the believers: that Allah does not deceive anyone, because Allah knows even the secrets of the heart, and whoever dares to deceive Allah will certainly be a fool, an ignorant person and one of most wicked nature. That is why such people are here declared to be extremely contemptible, detestable and base.

After this glimpse and touch, it is decided that Allah too is deceiving these people: He is granting them respite, and has left them in a state of misguidance. He is not bringing upon them any calamity by which they would be warned and return to the right path, nor is He afflicting them with any pang by which the eyes of these people would be opened. Allah is giving them a free rein to continue on that path which has pitfalls, so that these people fall into them. This is the deception which is practised upon them by Allah. Calamities and hardships sometimes come as mercy from Allah. When trials come upon some servants, they turn back from the path of error, and the secrets that they previously had no knowledge or awareness of become known to them. And sometimes ease and well-being is a respite from Allah for a person, and sinners advance further on the evil path, because these people have progressed so far in the way of sin and misguidance that Allah grants them well-being and lets them go further, until they reach an evil end.

Now the matter moves a little further, and in this picture of theirs, some other blemishes become visible.

(Verse) "And when they stand up for prayer, they stand lazily, showing off to the people, and remember Allah only a little." (4:142) (When they stand up for prayer, they stand up lazily, merely to show off to people, and they remember Allah only a little.) They do not stand up for prayer because they have a longing to meet Allah; they wish to stand before Allah with folded hands, to be joined with Allah and to seek help from Allah. They pray only to show off to people. That is why these people rise towards prayer with extremely heavy steps, as if someone were rising for some burdensome task, or were being summoned to some forced labour; and the condition of these people is that they remember Allah very little. They do not remember Allah, but remember people. They do not turn towards Allah, but turn towards people.

Surely, in the eyes of the believers, this is their extremely repulsive appearance. It has created in their eyes feelings of contempt and disapproval, and the natural result of these feelings and this outlook is that a distance arises between the people of faith and the people of hypocrisy. Personal and self-interested relationships weaken, and this is one of the stages of complete boycott between the people of faith and the people of hypocrisy, and the Islamic method of training is moving the Muslim community towards it.

Look at a few more features and blemishes:

(Verse) "Wavering between that, belonging neither to these nor to those. And whomever Allah leaves astray, you will not find for him a way." (4:143) (Wavering between disbelief and faith, neither fully on this side nor fully on that side. And for one whom Allah has led astray, you cannot find any path.)

Their stance is wavering and vacillating. They do not stand firmly in any one row: they are neither among the ranks of the believers nor among the ranks of the disbelievers. This is a stance which produces in believing hearts no feeling except contempt and loathing. It also reveals the personal weakness of the hypocrites. That is why they do not adopt any clear and decisive stance, nor can they openly express any creed or opinion: neither to this side nor to that side.

Now the conclusion of this ugly picture and this abject stance is that the decision of Allah has been made final regarding these people, and Allah has decided not to assist them in attaining the path of guidance. That is why no one can bring them onto the path of guidance, nor can anyone find a path of guidance for them. (Verse) "Whomever Allah leaves astray, you will not find for him a way." (4:143)

Up to this point, the Holy Qur'an, by creating feelings of aversion and contempt towards the hypocrites in the hearts of the believers, has made them understand that these are very weak people. Having fully achieved this purpose, the address now turns to the believers, and they are commanded that they should not themselves tread the path of the hypocrites, and the method of the hypocrites was that they made friendships with the disbelievers while not making any friendship with the Muslims. Allah warns the believers of His own grip, and thus Allah warns them by showing a glimpse of the otherworldly end of the hypocrites. This glimpse is extremely frightening and extremely humiliating.

This critical sentence about the hypocrites begins with a note of mockery. Here, instead of apostasy, criticism of them begins with the word "bashir" (give good news). They are being given the good news of the punishment that awaits them. Afterward, the cause of the punishment is also stated: these people, instead of making friends with the believers, are making friends with the disbelievers. A second reason is that they have bad opinions of Allah. A third is that they do not know who gives honor and who gives humiliation.

According to the preferred narrations, the disbelievers mentioned here are the Jews. The hypocrites would take refuge with them, hide in their homes at night, consult with them against the Muslims, and plot all kinds of conspiracies against the Muslims.

Allah asks in an interrogative manner: these people claim faith and yet make friends with the disbelievers. Why do they place themselves in such a position? Do these people seek honor from the disbelievers? Yet honor is with Allah, and honor is given only to the one who is a friend of Allah, who seeks honor from Allah's court, and who takes refuge with Allah.

Thus, in these verses, a glimpse of the hypocrites is shown. This is their first characteristic: they do not keep friendship with the believers and are friends of the disbelievers. They seek honor and power among the disbelievers, though the source of honor and power is Allah. Therefore, it is necessary that the search for honor and the search for power be made from Allah. If they seek it elsewhere, the search will be in vain, because this commodity is not available anywhere else.

Note this: in this universe, the human soul has only one support from which it can gain honor. When this soul bows before that support, it will become exalted over others. This one servitude and one prostration frees a person from all other prostrations. If the human soul does not begin to bow before Allah, it will have to serve many gods and many persons. It will have to observe many considerations, attend to various directions, and face various dangers, and all these considerations, observances, and servitude to different people will not be able to save it. This is because either there is servitude to Allah here, and then the person becomes exalted and honorable, or there is servitude to human beings, which is slavery and humiliation, and in which there is imprisonment instead of freedom. Now it is up to the human being to choose which of these to adopt: slavery or freedom.

No one who is a believer can seek honor from anything other than Allah. If he does so, he cannot be a believer. Likewise, if a believer seeks honor, support, and power from the enemies of Allah, he is not a believer. Today, those who claim Islam, bear Muslim names, and seek help in this universe from the enemies of Islam, more than anyone else need to reflect upon these guidances of the Quran, provided that they have a desire to be true Muslims. If they have no inclination toward this at all, then Allah is free from all the worlds.

Apart from other matters, it is also tantamount to seeking honor from the disbelievers when a person takes pride in those ancestors who died in disbelief, and considers that there is a bond of kinship between them and the Muslims. Just as some people take pride in the Pharaohs, some take pride in the Assyrians, some in the Phoenicians, some in the Babylonians, and the Arabs observe their pre-Islamic Arab ignorance and the community of ignorance.

Imam Ahmad narrated from Abu Rayhana, who said: the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever ascribes himself to nine disbelieving ancestors, intending by that to take pride in them, will be the tenth, who will be his companion in Hell."

In Islam, the ummah is based solely on the foundation of Islam and faith, and this has been so since the beginning of Islam. From the beginning of Islam until today, in every land, every place, and every lineage, this has been Islam's stance. The meaning of ummah is not that people of one lineage reside in one place at one time and thereby become one ummah.

Among the degrees of hypocrisy, the highest is that a believer sits in a gathering in which the verses of Allah are being denied, mocked, and he remains silent and turns a blind eye. Then he calls it tolerance, or wisdom, or breadth of heart, or freedom of opinion, though this stance is in reality an inner defeat that has seeped into his veins and sinews. He gives it this name so that people will not taunt him as weak and of weak faith. The truth is that such people hide their weakness behind these words.

Zeal for Allah, zeal for the religion of Allah, and zeal for the verses of Allah are in reality a great sign of faith. When this zeal ends, the dam breaks and all veils are removed. All barriers are removed, and when great pressure is applied, even the weak thread snaps. At first, Islamic zeal is suppressed, just as a spark is buried under ashes, and then it cools and goes out.

Whoever is in a gathering where his religion is mocked should either defend the religion or get up and leave the gathering. But if he turns a blind eye and remains silent, this is his first defeat. It is a state in which a person stands exactly in the middle of the bridge of hypocrisy, between faith and disbelief.

Even after the Prophet's ﷺ migration, they still had influence and standing in society. So it was ordered that Muslims should abstain from such gatherings. If a Muslim takes part even in this situation, he is a hypocrite.
