Part 6 at a Glance:

Part six is divided into two sections. The first section contains the remainder of Surah An-Nisa'. The beginning of Surah An-Nisa' occurred at the end of Part four, the whole of Part five is also devoted to it, and some of it has come in Part six as well. The second section of this part, which is about three-quarters of it, consists of Surah Al-Ma'idah.

Here we will limit our discussion only to the first section of this part. The second section, namely Surah Al-Ma'idah, will be discussed at the place of Surah Al-Ma'idah, where we will discuss the importance of Surah Al-Ma'idah and its themes in the same way as we have discussed the earlier surahs, if Allah's help remains with us.

While commenting on Surah An-Nisa', we said something about the method of discussion of this surah, and the same method continues in this section too. It is appropriate here to remind readers of it in very brief words, twice.

This surah deals with the Islamic concept of life, and it seeks to instill it in the nascent Islamic community, which it raised from the deep and narrow valleys of jahiliyyah and gradually brought to the heights of glory, to the utmost peaks. It extracted the conscience of this community from beneath the heaps of jahiliyyah ideas, and sorted out those ideas which had dimmed the features of its conscience. Along with this purification, as we said above, the features of jahiliyyah were erased from Islamic thought and consciousness and Islamic colours were filled in their place.

After this, in the light of this new concept of life, this surah takes the conscience, morals and collective habits of the Muslim ummah, and sorts them out one by one from jahili morals and habits, exactly in the same way as its thoughts and concepts were purified. Moreover, besides intellectual and moral purification, this surah established the collective life of the ummah and its family ties on the firm foundation of the solid divine system of life of Islam.

During this training and purification, this surah has also taken up deviant and wrong beliefs. Criticism has been directed at those holding wrong beliefs and concepts, and an effort at reform has been made, whether these people are from among the mushrikin or the Jews and Christians, that is, the People of the Book. Their beliefs have been corrected and reformed. Truth and reality, which these deviations had corrupted, have been brought out in clear relief, which these people had introduced into their scriptures and beliefs.

After this, the themes of the surah enter the struggle that was continuously taking place between the People of the Book and the Muslim community, especially with the Jews. Because from the time the Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived in Madinah with his community, they began to oppose the Islamic call with great intensity. When the centre of the Islamic movement shifted to Madinah, the Jews feared that their former distinguished position could no longer be maintained in Madinah's society; their national existence was threatened, and even their claim that they were the only distinguished people enjoying Allah's nearness, and that they were a nation chosen by Allah, was ending. For these reasons, they rose up against the Islamic movement with every kind of weapon. Thus this surah described in detail their mentality, their means of warfare, and their historical attitude towards their own prophets, so that it would be known that they had always treated every call to truth in this manner, whoever presented it, even if the one presenting it was their own prophet, their own leader and their own saviour.

After this, this surah tells the Muslim ummah itself what the responsibilities are of the burden placed upon its shoulders, what great role it has to play on this earth, and what strategy it must follow to be purified from all the defilements of jahiliyyah, to have its conscience purified, and its whole life purified. For this purpose, how much vigilance is needed and how great sacrifices are required, such as continuous struggle against the desires of one's own self, and continuous struggle and continuous sacrifices against the entire surrounding environment.

This entire surah continues steadily along this path. The themes of the previous section are also here, and this section too consists of the ups and downs of the same path, with the same style as in the previous part.

The beginning of this part itself is about the purification of the self and the purification of society. Efforts have been made so that an atmosphere of complete mutual trust remains among the members of the community, that people are not affected by the accusations of the Jews, and that Muslims have the right to take revenge, but forgiveness, magnanimity and generosity hold a position higher even than the scales of justice. It is explained that Allah dislikes backbiting and slander. If in this new society one brother oppresses another and the oppressed brother forgives, this act is very pleasing to Allah. Allah Himself also forgives, although He has the power to take revenge.

After this it is explained that the Islamic concept of life is that it regards the religion of Allah as a system of life, and gives the idea that in human history the caravan of messengers carried only this one religion. According to Islamic belief, to make distinctions between these messengers, and between the religions they brought, is clear disbelief. This statement comes so that the Jewish view among the People of the Book, that after their prophet no other prophet would come, may be refuted, and that this view was adopted by them merely out of religious and national prejudice and malice.

In this section a round with the Jews begins, in which it is explained what disobedience and ill-treatment they committed against their prophet, their leader and their saviour, Moses (peace be upon him). The purpose of these events is to make clear that the Jews are, by their nature, evil people. Their attitude towards truth and the Islamic call has always been this, even if a prophet was the one giving this call, even though he be their great prophet Moses (peace be upon him). Also, the false words they used regarding Jesus (peace be upon him) and his mother have been refuted, which Allah dislikes very much. By relating these events, their attitude and hostility towards the Last Prophet ﷺ become understandable, and people come to know what the real causes of that attitude are. In connection with the false claims and accusations of the Jews regarding Jesus (peace be upon him), and especially their claim that they had killed Jesus (peace be upon him), the Qur'an makes the reality manifest. Their claim of having killed the Messiah (peace be upon him) is plainly refuted, and it is explained that Allah inflicted various punishments upon the Jews because of their oppression, their obstructing of the path of truth, and their usury (although they had been forbidden from these acts). Also, because of their consumption of unlawful wealth and their economic exploitation of people, Allah, as a punishment, declared certain things unlawful for them which were lawful for the whole world. And that besides this worldly punishment, they will be given the painful punishment which awaits them in the Hereafter. However, excepted from this punishment are those who are firm in knowledge and who have believed in the Messenger ﷺ, who have recognised the truth and have begun to follow it.

Refuting the position the Jews were insisting upon, that they rejected the prophethood of the Last Prophet ﷺ, it was said that this prophethood is a normal matter. It is not something strange or wonderful that one of their own has been raised as a messenger. It is not an unusual matter that a human being has come as a messenger for the guidance of people. This is the Sunnah of Allah. From Noah (peace be upon him) until today, messengers have continued to come. Abraham (peace be upon him), Ishmael (peace be upon him), Isaac (peace be upon him), Jacob (peace be upon him), Jesus (peace be upon him), Job (peace be upon him), Aaron (peace be upon him), Solomon (peace be upon him) and David (peace be upon him) were sent according to this Sunnah of Allah. Also, all the other prophets whose prophethood the Jews acknowledge, and those whose prophethood they reject out of mere envy and jealousy. This is because it is the Sunnah and plan of Allah that messengers come for the guidance of people, who are warners and bearers of good news: ﴿So that mankind will have no argument against Allah after the messengers﴾ (4:165). This is not only a logical matter but also a necessary one.

In opposition to the Jews' rejection of truth, Allah Himself bears witness to the truth of Islam; the testimony of the angels is recorded, and Allah is sufficient as a witness in every matter. Therefore, because of their rejection of truth and their blocking of the path of truth, Allah gives a severe warning to these wrongdoers and disbelievers: that Allah will never forgive them, will never guide them to the straight path, and if He does guide them, it will be to the path of Hell, where they will abide forever. After this, all people are called: O people! This Messenger has come to you with the truth from your Lord. Believe in him; and if you cannot do so, then everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah. The Master of the heavens and the earth has testified to the messengership of this Prophet, and He Himself is calling you to faith. Therefore, the path which they are determining for themselves is a path opposed to the Master of the heavens and the earth.

This round with the People of the Book concludes. In it, their temperament, their means of operation, and the evil habits they have had since ancient times are exposed. By this exposure, all their deceptions are rendered ineffective, and it is decided that the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ is true, because testimony has already been given to it by Allah. The entire chain of messengers and the line of those who called to the truth also bear witness to it. Thus, the proof of Allah is established upon the people, and this reality comes to light: that the salvation of people depends upon firm belief in the messengership of the messengers. If they wish to be saved from the punishment of Hell, or if they, by the requirement of logic, deem themselves deserving of it, that is their choice, but it is clear that this is a most dangerous end.

With the conclusion of this round with the Jews, after doing justice to them in opposition to them, and refuting their false claims about Jesus (peace be upon him) and his blessed mother, a round now begins with the Christians themselves, who call themselves followers of Jesus (peace be upon him). They are instructed: do not exaggerate regarding Jesus (peace be upon him). The true reality concerning Jesus (peace be upon him) is recorded thus: he is a servant of Allah, and he himself does not hesitate to acknowledge that he is a servant of Allah. Likewise, the angels are also servants of Allah, so do not regard the Holy Spirit as God; the doctrine of the Trinity is false, and the relationship of father and son between Jesus (peace be upon him) and Allah is a most erroneous concept.

Amid the correction of Christian beliefs, the correct Islamic belief is also stated, and it is made clear that sovereignty belongs to Allah alone, and servitude to His servants, and whatever exists besides Allah, whoever it may be, is a servant and slave of Allah. This is the foundational belief of the Islamic concept of life. For this reason, the believers are given glad tidings here, and the disbelievers are warned in harsh words. And here too, as at the end of the discussion with the Jews, a general proclamation is made to all people, and it is explained that a clear proof has come to them from Allah, so that those who have missed its acceptance will have no argument left, will be unable to present any doubts, and their excuses will not be accepted.

The surah concludes with an explanation of a form of kalalah from the laws of inheritance, which was not explained in the earlier rulings. Some forms of kalalah have been mentioned earlier in this surah; this is the remainder of those. It was placed here because it is the remaining part of the economic reorganisation of the Muslim community, upon which Islam sought to establish this new Islamic society. It sought to transform it into a society with its own economic system and its own distinctive characteristics, which are permanent, so that this new society and this new community could perform, for all of humanity, the great role for which Allah has raised it up: the role of leadership, revolution, and organisation and reform.

Thus, from the study of this entire surah, and especially from the study of the section under discussion, it becomes clear that in Islam, alongside collective organization, economic reform and political regulation, there also continues the reform of morals, culture, the outlook on life, and the correction of beliefs. Together with this moral and ideological training, the community of Muslims also continues to engage in battle on the battlefield with its enemies, despite the great burden of responsibility placed upon its shoulders and the great role assigned to it to play on this earth. It has also been decided that the Qur'an is the constitution of this community; it is the source of its call. It is the duty of this community to move forward, fulfilling all these responsibilities together, with great depth, balance and in a general manner. These guidelines and matters are stated in such a way that whoever or whatever group takes up the task of the modern reconstruction of this ummah, this methodology is binding and definitive for them, so that they may fulfil their duties. Let them make this Qur'an the methodology of their call. The methodology of their movement should be derived from this Qur'an. Every step of the revival of Islam, its rebirth and modern reconstruction should be in accordance with this methodology. If one thinks along these lines, this Qur'an is still ready to play exactly the role it played before. This Qur'an is Allah's address to all of humanity, and it is a guide for all its affairs until the Day of Resurrection. Its wonders will never come to an end, and its being read again and again does not make it old, as the Prophet ﷺ said about it. He (ﷺ) is the one who, through this Qur'an, waged jihad against the disbelievers and hypocrites, and along with it waged jihad against the deviated and misguided People of the Book, and through it laid the foundation of a great ummah like the Muslim ummah in human history, raised it up and gave it elevation.

Lesson No. 43, Explanation of the Verses:
148 ... to ... 170.

The aim the Qur'an had before it was to produce a completely new ummah on this earth. Accordingly, the Qur'an formed this ummah from those people who were wandering in the dark valleys of jahiliyyah (ignorance). Among them, those who had already answered the call of the Qur'an—the Qur'an took these believers by the hand and, in an instant, raised them up to a vertical height and brought them to the peaks of civilization and culture, the highest peaks. Why? So that after their formation and training, the leadership of all humanity could be entrusted to them, and their great role in the leadership of this world could be determined. History bears witness that this happened.

One of the important aims in the formation and building of this community was the purification of its conscience, the purification of the environment surrounding this community, and the raising of the moral and intellectual level on which this community stood at that time.

And when this community reached that desired level and standard, it became high in its individual morals, became exemplary in its collective morals, and to the same extent that it became superior to other people in its beliefs and concepts, then Allah, through it, brought about on this earth the revolution that was in Allah's plan. After this, Allah appointed this ummah as the guardian and watchman of His religion and His system of life. Its duty became to bring this entire humanity out of misguidance and darkness into light, and to remain continuously the trustee of the leadership of this entire humanity and to guide it; and in fact this is what happened.

When a community attains superiority over all the people of this earth in these qualities, its leadership of humanity becomes a completely natural and inherent matter, and this matter stands on its correct foundations. As a result of this situation, such a community then also becomes superior to other nations in knowledge, culture, civilization, economics and politics, and this second superiority it attains as a result of the first superiority, that is, as a result of moral and ideological superiority. And this is the Sunnah of Allah both for all individuals of this earth and for all communities and societies. One aspect of this psychological and collective purification has been addressed in the following two verses.

(Verses) No. 148 to 149.

Society is always extremely sensitive, so it needs certain collective etiquettes that suit this sensitivity. Sometimes a person says a casual thing but cannot gauge the effects it has on society. And sometimes it is a common matter, but the speaker intends it for only one person; yet the effects of such words are extremely harmful to the psychology of society, its morals and its customs. Not only that one individual is affected by this matter, but the entire community is affected by it.

When someone wishes to speak ill of another, whatever form it takes, if there is no fear of God in his heart and his conscience is not cautious, then such ill-speaking is very easy for a person. But the effects of this ill-speaking and foul-tongue create very bad results in society. Sometimes its effect is that people's trust is lost from society. People come to think that evil has now gained dominance in society. Sometimes it happens that those people in whom the capacity for evil lies hidden, but who did not commit evil because of social pressure, begin to commit it. Now it is commonly practised, so they do not hesitate about it, nor do they feel any social fear. They think that they alone are not doing it and that others too are doing the same. Sometimes it happens that, seeing an evil being committed again and again, the revulsion for that evil diminishes in a person's heart. A person initially feels an evil very intensely, but when it is repeatedly committed or repeatedly mentioned, its ugliness decreases in his eyes and his aversion to it lessens. It becomes easy for people to hear of such an evil, and then they do not promptly rise to eliminate it.

In ill-speaking, a person first makes individual accusations; it becomes individual abuse. After this, collective harm and disorder arise. Moral lawlessness spreads. In it, some people's assessments of one another change; some people no longer have trust in others; some communities no longer have trust in other communities. Accusations follow upon accusations, and tongues lick them up without any hesitation.

For this reason, Allah has made ill-speaking of one another forbidden for the community of Muslims. Only the one who has been wronged may speak ill, and he may use only such harsh words as express the real wrong of the oppressor, within the limits within which the wrong was done.

(Verse) "Allah does not like the public utterance of evil speech, except by one who has been wronged." (4:148) (Allah does not like that a person should open his tongue in ill-speaking, except where someone has been wronged.)

In circumstances of injustice, through ill-speaking the enemy is repaid, and in the same way defence is made against oppression. This ill-speaking includes those matters which in legal terminology are called sabb wa shatm (abuse and vilification). Through this ill-speaking, an individual rejects the individual mistreatment that has actually occurred. Thus this oppressed person carries out propaganda against the oppression and the oppressor, to which he has a right, so that society may do justice to this oppressed person, be able to stop the oppressor's hand, and so that within society an atmosphere may be established in which every oppressor thinks well about his end before committing oppression and refrains from repeating that oppression. The right of open ill-speaking is strictly limited; only the one who has been wronged may use it. The grounds for its permissibility are also limited: only the oppression done to a specific person, and this ill-speaking may be directed only against the one who committed the oppression. Within these limited circumstances, this ill-speaking is permitted because through it a great good is intended to be promoted. Moreover, through this ill-speaking the aim is not merely publicity against the oppression and the oppressor, but in essence that the oppressed may obtain justice and equity.

Islamic law protects people's reputation and honour only so long as they do not commit oppression and injustice. When they commit oppression, they are no longer entitled to have their good name legally protected. After the commission of oppression, the oppressed acquires the legal right to raise his voice against that oppression and, to a certain extent, to speak ill as well. This is the only exception concerning the oppressed; otherwise the general legal and moral code of Islam is that no ill-speaking against anyone is permitted.

In this way a kind of balance is established between these two aims of Islam. It seeks to establish a system of justice in which there is no room for oppression. It also seeks to establish a system of morality in which the modesty of the eyes and collective tolerance are not harmed.

Upon this, the Qur'an brings this concluding statement: "And Allah is ever Hearing, Knowing" (4:148). And at the end of the discourse too, the matter is linked to the Being of Allah, Glorified is He, whereas the beginning of the mention had been with the love of Allah.

(Verse) "Allah does not like the public utterance of evil speech" (4:148) (Allah does not like that a person should open his tongue in ill-speaking). This is said so that in a person's heart there remains alive the awareness that his intention, the causes of his ill-speaking, and then the words that come from his tongue and the accuracy and appropriateness of the accusations, are well assessed by Allah, because Allah hears, and He is fully aware of all the background to what is said, and whatever is hidden in hearts is also manifest to Him.

The Qur'an does not end the matter here with the mere prohibition of ill-speaking, that is, merely a negative command; rather, by stating the positive, it enjoins good. It draws attention to the fact that overlooking and forgiving evil is in any case very pleasing. Forgiveness is among the important attributes of Allah's attributes, although Allah has full power to call to account every sinner. Here a hint is given that the people of faith should develop within themselves the morals and attributes of Allah, to the extent that they have the capacity and to the extent that they are able to do so.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 4, verse 149:

(Verse) "Whether you do good openly or conceal it, or pardon an evil, indeed Allah is ever Pardoning, Competent [to punish]." (4:149) (Yet if you keep doing good, both openly and in secret, or at least pardon evil, then it is also the attribute of Allah that He is the Most Forgiving, although He has full power to punish.)

Thus the method of spiritual training in Islam raises the believing soul and the Muslim community one step further. In the first stage, it is said that it is not good for a noble person to open his mouth with abusive speech. In this stage, one exception is allowed: the oppressed may respond with abuse and also take his right and make the attainment of justice possible. At the second stage, the believers are encouraged that all of them should always strive for goodness, and to the one who has been wronged and who could take revenge by abusing in return, it is also said that if he forgives and overlooks, this is a most excellent act. This is a most sublime morality, provided that he has the power to take revenge and he prefers forgiveness and pardon over revenge. For what is the meaning of forgiveness without the power of retaliation? "The beggar's humility is his own vanity."

If they practice forgiveness and pardon openly, then the custom of forgiveness and pardon will spread in society and goodness will spread; and if they do this secretly, it will still accomplish the work of purifying the souls. Goodness is beneficial whether it is done openly or secretly. When forgiveness and pardon become common among people, the occasions for abusive speech will themselves gradually decrease, provided that the one who forgives is a person who has power to take revenge. But if a person's weakness is compelling him to forgive, there will be no benefit in it. This forgiveness and pardon should be adopted in emulation of the character of Allah. Allah shows forgiveness despite having power. (Verse) "Indeed Allah is ever Pardoning, Competent [to punish]." (4:149) (Allah is the Most Forgiving, although He has full power to punish.)

After this, the discourse turns toward the People of the Book. First, the discussion is about all the People of the Book; after that, especially some deeds of the Jews are mentioned, and at the end the Christians are criticized. The Jews used to speak harshly against Prophet Isa (peace be upon him) and Maryam (peace be upon her), and they used to slander their persons. In this part of the discourse, their abusive speech is also mentioned. In this way, the criticism directed at the Jews is also clearly connected with the two preceding verses, in which abusive speech is prohibited.

This criticism of the People of the Book, the Jews and the Christians, is also part of the struggle that the Muslim community faced in Medina with its enemies, a large part of which is explained in detail in this Surah and in Surah al-Baqarah and Surah Aal-e-Imran. Let the details of that struggle be seen in accordance with the Qur'anic order.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 4, verse 150–151:

The Jews claimed that they believed in their prophets, yet they rejected the messengerships of Hadrat Isa (peace be upon him) and Hadrat Muhammad (ﷺ). The position of the Christians was that they believed only in the messengership of Hadrat Isa (peace be upon him), and they too denied the messengership of Hadrat Muhammad (ﷺ). Along with this, they regarded Hadrat Isa (peace be upon him) as God.

The Qur'an Karim took a firm stand against the positions of both of them, and presented a comprehensive concept of belief in Allah and His prophets and messengers. Its summary is that it is wrong to make a distinction between Allah and His messengers, and it is also wrong to make a distinction among the messengers of Allah himself, believing in some and rejecting others; rather, it is necessary to believe in Allah and all His messengers without discrimination. This is the religion of Islam, and Allah does not accept any other religion, because the oneness of Allah and its demands can be fulfilled only in this manner.

The first requirement of the absolute oneness of Allah is that the religion of Allah is also one, whose bearers are all the messengers who were sent at any time for the guidance of mankind, and the rank and station of all the messengers to whom this trust was entrusted must also be one. Whoever denies the one office and one station of the messengers will be considered to be denying the oneness of Allah. From this a great concept of the oneness of Allah emerges, because for mankind the religion pleasing to Allah is in every case one; its foundation is one, and its source and origin is one. Therefore, how can a distinction among its representatives be reasonable?

The Qur'an Karim described the making of a distinction between Allah and the messengers in these words: "That they believe in Allah and reject the messengers." And it described the distinction among the messengers thus: "We will believe in some and will not believe in others." And about both these groups it said: (ان الذین یکفرون باللہ ورسولہ) (4:150) (Those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers). Thus, according to the Qur'an, believing in some of Allah and His messengers and not believing in others is also disbelief.

The truth is that faith is a single unit and it cannot be divided into pieces. The first step of faith is the affirmation of the oneness of Allah. The necessary requirement of acknowledging Allah as One without partner is that the system of life and the religion which Allah has chosen for mankind is also one, which is founded on the belief in Tawhid. The messengers who have come bringing this religion are also one, because they were all sent by Him, and they did not come of their own accord, nor have they remained separate from the will of Allah and His revelation. Their position has always been one and the same, so a single whole unit cannot be dissected and analysed. Whoever makes a distinction within this unity and oneness of faith will commit absolute disbelief, even if he imagines that he has believed in some parts and disbelieved in others. The recompense of such people in the sight of Allah will be that they will be given a humiliating punishment, all such people.

(اولئک ھم الکفرون حقا، واعتدنا للکفرین عذابا مھینا) (4:151) (They are the true disbelievers, and for the disbelievers We have prepared a punishment that will humiliate and disgrace them.) No kind of division is permissible. Among Muslims there is reverence and respect for all the messengers. In the view of Muslims, all heavenly religions are true; yet if their contents are distorted, then they will no longer remain religions, even though some parts of those religions may still exist in their original form, because religion is one unity, and the People of the Book understand this well. In religion there is one God; this one God has prescribed one religion for people. This religion is a complete methodology of their life. Allah has sent messengers so that all these messengers may call people towards this methodology and system. In the conception of Muslims, the caravan of faith is joined together like a row. Hadrat Nuh (peace be upon him), Hadrat Ibrahim (peace be upon him), Hadrat Musa (peace be upon him), Hadrat Isa (peace be upon him), and Hadrat Muhammad (ﷺ) lead this caravan, and between them there have passed other messengers whose names are not mentioned here. The genealogy of all these messengers is linked with this same caravan. All of them have been bearers of one great trust, and all these messengers have been inheritors of one truth and goodness, whose chain is long and blessed. There is no division in this chain, no messenger in it stands apart, there is no break within this chain, and the source of the inheritance of the true religion has been these very people. Apart from the line of these messengers, any religion or ideology is falsehood and misguidance.

This is the Islamic worldview, besides which Allah does not accept any other religion or way of life. And these are the people of Islam who deserve reward from Allah for their deeds, and who deserve His mercy and forgiveness too, if any shortcoming has occurred from them in their lives.

(Verse 4:152) "Those who believe in Allah and His messengers and do not make any distinction between any of them — to them He will surely give their rewards, and Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful."

(Translation of the verse as given in the Urdu rendering: "In contrast, those who believe in Allah and all His messengers and do not make distinction between them, We will surely give them their rewards, and Allah is most forgiving and merciful.")

Why has Islam been so emphatic in declaring the beliefs concerning Allah and the messengers to be a single unity? Because, in a believer's conception of the Divine, the belief in Tawhid (Oneness of God) holds a foundational place. This belief also accords with the concept of a single Director and Manager of this universe, who accepts no plurality and in whose presence no other manager can exist. Only a conscious human being who perceives the all-pervading Great Order (Namus-i-Akbar) operating within this universe, and for as long as his sight can reach, can adopt this very belief. This same outlook on life can give the People of Faith the form of a united caravan, which stands as one community against the ranks of disbelief and the party of Satan. But these People of Faith are not scattered and divided like those who hold views whose religion and doctrine, though originally revealed (samawi) in their source, were distorted by them, and who now do not stand in one rank as the true People of Faith do.

This is why the Qur'an declares only Islam to be the religion, and designates only the Muslims as "the best community (Khayr Ummah), brought forth for the sake of mankind." Those Muslims whose belief is correct, whose action and conduct conform to that belief and outlook — not merely those who were born into a Muslim household, nor merely those who have memorised the Kalimah of Islam and uttered it with their tongue.

After this explanation it becomes clear who they are that, on the one hand, create a separation between Allah and His messengers, and on the other hand, accept some of the messengers while rejecting others. They create a gap within the historical caravan of faith, they break into pieces that unity which Allah has established, and thus they deny that Oneness upon which the belief in faith in Allah rests.

After strengthening the first foundation of the Islamic conception of life concerning the messengers and their prophethood, and after making clear the reality of faith and the reality of disbelief, certain wrong positions of the Jews are brought under discussion in this context, which are also connected with the slander mentioned at the beginning of this section (para). In this, their position regarding the Prophet ﷺ and his prophethood is refuted, and the practice of their demanding miracles and signs from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is condemned. They make a distinction between their position and belief concerning Musa (Moses) (peace be upon him) and their position and belief about him. Then their position regarding Isa (Jesus) (peace be upon him) and his blessed mother differs from their position regarding Musa (peace be upon him). Yet the reality of all these prophets is one and the same throughout human history. Here, from the context of the discourse, it appears that perhaps the same Jews and People of the Book who stand before Muhammad ﷺ also stood before Isa (peace be upon him) and likewise stood before Musa (peace be upon him). The purpose of this is to emphasise the meaning that just as the messengers are one, so too are we one. Accordingly, the Qur'an manifests this disposition of theirs in the following words.

Arabian Peninsula: The Jews adopted an open and hostile stance against Islam and the Prophet of Islam. They constantly devised secret and extremely hostile plots against him, the details of which the Qur'an has described. Some of their colours we have already shown in Surah al-Baqarah, Surah Al 'Imran, and in the fifth part of this very Surah. What is being said in these verses is also one shade of this continuous stance of theirs.

Yet these Jews claim that they believe in Musa (peace be upon him) and do not affirm the prophethood of 'Isa (peace be upon him) and Muhammad ﷺ... By turning over this page of their history, it is shown that this habit of theirs is not a new habit. They are people of thick minds; they are convinced only by seeing tangible things. Just as these people were stubborn and contentious in the time of Musa (peace be upon him), and do not accept anything unless they are forced to accept someone's word by compulsion, so they are today as disbelieving, treacherous, and quick to break promises. They are the same liars and foul people. They are not steadfast on any position, nor do they refrain from slander. They are always slaves of greed, and worldliness is their creed. Eating people's wealth falsely and unjustly is their practice. It is also their ancient habit that these people turn away from Allah's command and do not give weight to the reward that He has with Him in the Hereafter.

The purpose of this campaign against them in these verses is precisely to lay out their reality openly before them and to shame them. Seeing the force and variety of this campaign, it becomes clear that there was a certain need at that time to expose the Jewish conspiracy, which they were plotting against Islam and the Prophet of the age. It is these very Jewish conditions and impure conspiracies that continue unchanged to this day against this religion and its adherents.

If these People of the Book are demanding of you today that you have a writing sent down upon them from the heavens — do not be distressed by their obstinacy, for this obstinacy of theirs is not astonishing, nor is it a new matter.

(Verse) "Fa-qad sa'alu Musa akbar min dhalika fa-qalu arina Allaha jahratan" (4:153) — So they had asked Musa for something even greater than this, saying: "Show us Allah plainly." The great miracles that Allah sent down through Musa (peace be upon him) could not awaken their sense. Even by these great miracles no tremor arose in their conscience, and these astonishing miracles could not incline their hearts towards guidance and obedience. These wretched people went further and demanded to see the Divine Being with their own eyes — plainly, openly. This was their arrogant disposition and demand, in which there was not even the freshness of faith; rather, the capacity for faith was altogether absent from their nature.

(Verse) "Fa-akhadhathumu as-sa'iqatu bi-zulmihim" — and because of this rebellion, a thunderbolt suddenly struck them. Yet even then Allah pardoned them, and He accepted Musa's (peace be upon him) supplication on their behalf and his humble entreaty to Him. The details of that supplication are in Surah al-A'raf (7:155).

(Verse) "Falamma akhadhathumu ar-rajfatu qala rabbi law shi'ta ahlaktahum min qablu wa iyya, atuhlikuna bima fa'ala as-sufahau minna, in hiya illa fitnatuka tudillu biha man tasha'u wa tahdi man tasha'u, anta waliyyuna faghfir lana warhamna wa anta khayru al-ghafirin (155). Wa-uktub lana fi hadhihi ad-dunya hasanatan wa fi al-akhirati inna hudna ilayk (156)" (7:155–156)

(When a violent earthquake seized them, Musa (peace be upon him) said: "O my Lord, if You had willed, You could have destroyed them and me before this. Will You destroy us for what some foolish ones among us did? This was only Your trial, by which You lead astray whom You will and guide whom You will. You are our Protector, so forgive us and have mercy upon us. You are the best of forgivers. And write for us good in this world and in the Hereafter; we have turned back to You.")

(Verse) "Thumma attakhadhu al-'ijla min ba'di ma ja'athumu al-bayyinat" (4:153) — Then they took the calf as a deity after clear signs had come to them. This calf was made of gold. It was fashioned by a man named Samiri, from the gold ornaments that they had taken from Egyptian women when they were leaving there. These people gathered around the calf and took it as their deity. Musa (peace be upon him) had gone to Mount Sinai at that time, where he was to speak with his Lord at an appointed time, where he was to be given the tablets of the Torah, guidance, and new light. (Verse) "Fa-'afawna 'an dhalika" (4:153) — Yet We pardoned them for this. But Jews, after all, were Jews. In dealing with them, only fear and force are of benefit.

(Verse) "Wa-atayna Musa sultanan mubina (153) wa rafa'na fawqahumu at-tura bi-mithaqihim wa qulna lahumu udkhulu al-baba sujjadan wa qulna lahumu la ta'du fi as-sabti wa akhadhna minhum mithaqan ghaliza" (154) (4:153–154) — We pardoned them. We gave Musa a clear authority, and We raised Mount Sinai above them and took from them a covenant to obey that authority. We commanded them to enter the gate prostrating, and We told them not to break Allah's law, and We took from them a firm covenant on this.

Here the question is: what is the authority (sultan) that Allah gave to Musa? It is most likely the law that was present in the tablets. Thus Allah's law is, as it were, authority and sovereignty from Allah, and any law or code other than Allah's will have no sanction or seal of acceptance from Allah. Practically too, laws and codes other than Allah's do not obtain dominion over hearts. That is why the laws people make for themselves have no value in the hearts of the common people. These laws can be enforced only when a jailer stands over them or the executioner's sword is over their heads. As for Allah's law, people bow before it with utmost humility, and their hearts incline to obedience. Within their hearts there is fear of violating the law, and fear of Allah's punishment is before their eyes. But the Jews, whose hearts were devoid of the consciousness of faith, flatly refused to accept the tablets of law given by Allah through Musa (peace be upon him). At this point Allah's wrath came upon them again, because by their nature and disposition they were deserving of it. Then they saw that a great rock was hanging over their heads; it appeared that it was about to fall upon them. They started, and immediately they affirmed their acceptance of this law and made a promise. A firm covenant was concluded, and it was concluded with great assurances. Yet previously they neither accepted nor were ready to make a covenant, nor were they ready to take up that ancient covenant... Allah here reminds them of this ancient trait of theirs. In this scene that Allah describes, there is a hard rock hanging over their heads, and on the other hand, they have hearts hard like rock in their breasts. Thus a correspondence is created between these two kinds of rocks within this scene. In this way the mode of expression becomes firm, definite and tangible, as is the general mode of expression of the Qur'an — that they should enter Bayt al-Maqdis prostrating, and that they should respect the Sabbath, which was made a day of joy for them at their own demand.

As soon as the terror of the hanging rock disappeared and that overpowering atmosphere ended, their steps slipped, and with pride they began to say that their hearts are not affected by any admonition. They are among people to whom nothing reaches, for their doors are closed. And after saying this, they committed all those evil deeds, the details of which Allah here tells His Prophet ﷺ. These are enumerated here so that the Messenger ﷺ may hold up a mirror to the Jews, to show them what they really are.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 4, verse 155:

(Verse) "Then, because of their breaking their covenant, and their disbelief in the signs of Allah, and their killing of the prophets without right, and their saying, 'Our hearts are wrapped up.'" (4:155) (Because of their breaking their covenant and because they denied the signs of Allah and killed many prophets unjustly, and went so far as to say that our hearts are protected in coverings.)... on their saying that our hearts are protected in coverings (qulubuna ghulf, 4:155). The criticism ends here, and the next verse answers their claim. They would make this statement when the Prophet ﷺ presented the Islamic call to them. They gave this reply either so that the Prophet ﷺ would lose hope in them and stop presenting the call to them in future, or they said it as a jest about the Prophet's ﷺ preaching, and by rejecting his call they were trying, as it were, to appear important, [claiming] that "we do not even pay heed to these things." Both of these may have been in their minds. In any case, Allah's answer comes thus:

(Verse) "Nay, Allah has set a seal upon them for their disbelief, so they believe only a little." (4:155) (In truth, because of their falsehood-worship, Allah has put a seal upon their hearts, and for this reason they believe very little...) The meaning is that their hearts are not wrapped up; rather, they reject the Islamic call because Allah has set a seal upon their hearts. This seal was also placed on their hearts because they made disbelief their practice, so their hearts became hard; they have become like inanimate objects and are buried under disbelief. They have no sense of the freshness of faith; the sense of the sweetness of faith has gone from within them. Therefore only a rare few of them accept faith. These rare ones are those who did not commit the aforementioned evil deeds, and therefore no seal was placed on their hearts; that is, those who kept the doors of their hearts open to accepting the truth, and by accepting the truth became honourable. Allah guided them and granted them faith. Such people among the Jews were very few, at the least, such as 'Abdullah ibn Salam, Tha'labah ibn Ya'mi (or Mu'ayyah), Asad ibn Ka'b (or Asad ibn Mahiyah), and Asad ibn 'Ubaydullah, may Allah be pleased with them all.

After this criticism and clarification, Allah the Exalted enumerates the causes for which these Jews became deserving of the treatment that was meted out to them. In this world, some extremely pure things were declared unlawful for them as a punishment, and in the Hereafter a punishment of fire was prepared for them, so that they would await it even before the Hereafter and the arrival of the Day of Resurrection.

(Verse 156) "And because of their disbelief, and their having uttered against Mary a tremendous slander." (Verse 157) "And their saying, 'Indeed, we killed the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, the Messenger of Allah.'" (4:156–157)

(Thus, in their disbelief they went so far as to level a grave accusation against Mary, and they themselves said that they had killed the Messiah, Jesus (peace be upon him), son of Mary, the Messenger of Allah.)

...When the Qur'an mentions any of their evil deeds, it invariably brings along their attribute of disbelief (kufr). Even when the killing of the Prophets is mentioned, this attribute is repeated: they killed the Prophets unjustly. The killing of the Prophets, whenever it occurred, was always unjust. The word "unjustly" has been brought as a statement of fact. Likewise, where it is mentioned that they uttered a tremendous slander against Mary (peace be upon her), this attribute is also mentioned there.

The accusation that they leveled against Mary was made only by the Jews. They charged Mary with having committed adultery with Yusuf the carpenter (may the wrath of God be upon them!). Then they boasted that they had crucified the Messiah, and, sarcastically, said: "We have killed the Messiah, son of Mary, the Messenger of Allah."

At this point the flow of the discourse pauses once again, and their claim is refuted in passing, and the truth is established and affirmed.

The Qur'an: 4:157–158

(Verse) "And their saying, 'Indeed, we killed the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, the Messenger of Allah'; and they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them. And indeed, those who differ concerning it are in doubt about it. They have no knowledge of it except the following of assumption. And they did not kill him for certain. Rather, Allah raised him to Himself. And ever is Allah Exalted in Might and Wise." (4:157–158)

(Translation of the Qur'an's meaning: Although in reality they neither killed him nor crucified him, rather the matter was made unclear to them. Those who differed about it are also in fact caught in doubt. They have no knowledge of it; they only follow assumption. They certainly did not kill him; rather, Allah raised him up to Himself. Allah is Mighty and Wise.)

In the matter of the killing of Jesus (peace be upon him), the People of the Book were in great confusion, and even the Christians themselves had serious misunderstanding about it. The Jews used to say, "We have killed Jesus son of Mary, the Messenger of Allah." They used the words "Messenger of Allah" for Jesus (peace be upon him) as a form of mockery. And the Christians' position was that he was crucified and buried, but after three days he rose again. Their history is silent about the birth and death of the Messiah in such a way that perhaps this event was not considered important. Neither of these two parties said anything with certainty about this great event, because these events occurred very quickly and passed out of sight. Various narrations spread, and truth and falsehood became mixed together. No one could say anything with certainty, and no one did; therefore, the only certain statement is the one made by Allah, Lord of the worlds.

Of the four currently recognized Gospels, which narrate the arrest of Jesus (peace be upon him), his death and crucifixion, and then his burial and resurrection, all these accounts were written in periods long after Jesus (peace be upon him) was raised. In that era, the disciples of the Messiah were persecuted, and the religion of the Messiah was suppressed. In an atmosphere of fear, secrecy, violence and exile, it was extremely difficult for any accurate and researched account to be written. In that period, countless Gospels were written. Around the end of the 200s (CE), four of them were selected and made the recognized ones. They were declared the official Gospels, and this declaration also had certain specific aims and was not free from doubt and suspicion.

Among the Gospels written after Jesus (peace be upon him) was the Gospel of Barnabas. This Gospel differs from those four selected and accepted Gospels. Regarding the event of Jesus' being raised up, this Gospel says:

"When the soldiers arrived with Judas at the place where Jesus was, the Messiah heard the mass of people approaching, and he cowered in fear in a corner of the house, while the eleven disciples (still) slept. When God, the One who is exalted, saw that His servant (Jesus) was in danger, He commanded His angels Gabriel, Michael, Raphael and Uriel to bring Jesus out of the world. The pure angels came and took Jesus out and lifted him up through the window that faced south, and took him to the third heaven and placed him in the company of the angels who glorify God forever. Judas, in time, entered the house through the same window through which Jesus had been taken up. The disciples of the Messiah were all (still) sleeping. Now, the strange God did a strange thing: the speech and face of Judas both changed, and he became like Jesus, to the point that we were certain he was Jesus. Judas, after waking us, began searching to find where the 'Master' (Jesus) was. We were astonished, and we said to him: O our Lord! You are our Master; have you forgotten us at this time?"

In short, no one among the Christians who wishes to investigate this matter finds anything reliable or conclusive in the existing records, because this event took place in the darkness of night before the break of dawn. The arguments put forward by later people were based on narration upon narration. The Qur'an, speaking on this matter, says:

(Verse) "And indeed, those who differ concerning it are in doubt about it. They have no knowledge of it except the following of assumption. And they did not kill him for certain. Rather, Allah raised him to Himself. And ever is Allah Exalted in Might and Wise." (4:157–158)

And before this, the Qur'an had stated decisively: (Verse) "And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them." (4:157)

The Qur'an does not here give the details of the raising of Jesus (peace be upon him): whether this raising was physical or spiritual, whether it occurred while he was alive or was only spiritual after death, and when and where this death (tawaffi) occurred. But the Qur'an says that they neither killed him nor crucified him. This act of killing and crucifixion happened to the person about whom they were made to suspect that he was Jesus (peace be upon him). Beyond this, the Qur'an does not give further detail here. However, in the second surah (Surah Al-Imran), Allah says: (Verse) "O Jesus, I will take you back (mutawaffika) and raise you to Myself." In this verse too, no details are given of the raising and the taking back (tawaffi); no time for that tawaffi is given, nor is the nature of the tawaffi described. In the method we have adopted in Zilal al-Quran, we also remain within the shade of the Qur'an and do not go into the details; therefore we have no evidence regarding the manner of tawaffi. Nor is there now any means to obtain such details. Merely transmitting fabrications and legends would serve no purpose.

Now we return to the original subject and to the rebuke that the Qur'an directed at the People of the Book.

The Qur'an does not here give the details of the raising of Jesus (peace be upon him): whether this raising was physical or spiritual, whether it occurred while he was alive or was only spiritual after death, and when and where this death (tawaffi) occurred. But the Qur'an says that they neither killed him nor crucified him. This act of killing and crucifixion happened to the person about whom they were made to suspect that he was Jesus (peace be upon him). Beyond this, the Qur'an does not give further detail here. However, in the second surah (Surah Al-Imran), Allah says: (Verse) "O Jesus, I will take you back (mutawaffika) and raise you to Myself." In this verse too, no details are given of the raising and the taking back (tawaffi); no time for that tawaffi is given, nor is the nature of the tawaffi described. In the method we have adopted in Zilal al-Quran, we also remain within the shade of the Qur'an and do not go into the details; therefore we have no evidence regarding the manner of tawaffi. Nor is there now any means to obtain such details. Merely transmitting fabrications and legends would serve no purpose.

Now we return to the original subject and to the rebuke that the Qur'an directed at the People of the Book.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 4, verse 159:

﴿And there is none of the People of the Book but will believe in him before his death, and on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them.﴾ (4:159)

Among the early righteous scholars (salaf al-salih) there has been difference of opinion regarding the meaning of this verse. The reason for this difference is that scholars have differed about the referent of the pronoun in "mawtihi" (his death). If its referent is Hadrat Isa (peace be upon him), then the meaning is that there is none among the People of the Book who will not believe in Hadrat Isa (peace be upon him) before the death of Hadrat Isa (peace be upon him). In this case, these scholars hold that Hadrat Isa (peace be upon him) will descend before the Day of Resurrection.

According to the second interpretation, the pronoun in "mawtihi" refers to the People of the Book. That is, every person from the People of the Book will believe in Hadrat Isa (peace be upon him) before his own death. This is because, at the moment of the agony of death (sakarat al-maut), the truth becomes clear to the dying person, but at that time, if someone believes, that belief is of no benefit to him.

In my view, this second opinion is more worthy of preference, and the reading of Hadrat Ubayy (may Allah be pleased with him) also points to it. ﴿(Illa li-yu'minunna bihi qabla mawtihi)﴾ (4:159) (there is none among the People of the Book who will not believe in him before their death). According to this reading, the pronoun can refer only to the People of the Book. In this case, the meaning is that those Jews who deny Hadrat Isa (peace be upon him), who remain firm on this position until now, and who hold the belief that they killed him and crucified him, whoever of them dies will at that very moment (that is, at the time of death throes) have it made clear to him that Hadrat Isa (peace be upon him) was upon the truth and that his prophethood was true. So he will believe in Hadrat Isa (peace be upon him) in the state of death throes, but at that time believing is no longer beneficial. On the Day of Resurrection, Hadrat Isa (peace be upon him) will himself be a witness against them.

Here the story of the crucifixion ends. After this, the discussion turns to other evil deeds of the Jews, and it is explained what punishment Allah gave them in this world for these evil deeds, and what has been prepared for them in the Hereafter.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 4, verses 160–161:

﴿So because of the wrongdoing of those who were Jews, We made unlawful for them certain good things that had been lawful for them, and because of their hindering many from the way of Allah, and their taking of usury, though they had been forbidden from it, and their devouring of the wealth of people by false means. And We have prepared for those among them who disbelieve a painful punishment.﴾ (4:160–161)

(In short, because of this oppressive conduct of these Jews, and because they hinder many from the path of Allah, and take usury, which they had been forbidden, and consume people's wealth by illegitimate means, We made unlawful for them many good things that had previously been lawful for them, and We have prepared a painful punishment for those among them who are disbelievers.)

Thus, through this verse, some further abominations were added to their previous evil deeds. It was made clear that they have no occupation other than barring people from the way of Allah. It is as though they are engaged in such work day and night. Moreover, they are engaged in usurious dealings day and night, and they do not do this merely out of ignorance, nor because they were not warned about it; rather, they were expressly forbidden from it in clear words, yet they still insisted on it and continued to consume people's wealth unjustly. They consumed it through usury and also through other means.

Because of these abominations and the crimes mentioned in the earlier surahs, Allah made unlawful for them some of the good things that had been lawful for them, and Allah has prepared a severely painful punishment for the disbelievers.

In this campaign against the Jews, the mask was stripped from their faces and cast aside, and some events from their history were presented so that it might be known what their history is. The pretexts they made and their obstinacy were exposed, and it was made clear that they are by no means people who accept guidance, and that they maintained this same attitude toward their leader, their deliverer, and their great prophet. Their habit has always been to be very bold and swift in mistreating the righteous and the prophets and in speaking evil against them. They have continued to kill the prophets and then, instead of showing remorse, have taken pride in that killing. As a result of these statements, the web of Jewish deception and intrigue that they had spun against the ranks of Islam was torn apart. Their conspiracies failed, and their secret friendships with the Muslims were severed. Thus the people of Islam came to know well the true nature of the Jews, and recognized their conspiracies against Islam and the means and instruments used in them. They came to know how they form factions against every truth, whether that truth arises from within their own ranks or is found among other nations outside them, because they have always been enemies of truth and of the people of truth. They have always uprooted guidance and the guides, and they have done this in every age and every era. Their conduct toward their enemies was of course such, but they have done the same even to their friends. Therefore, in every age, it is the duty of every Islamic movement and Islamic society to remain wary of the Jews, because their very nature is such that they are personally enemies of truth. Enmity toward truth is filled within their hearts. Their hearts have become hard. They bow their heads only before the one who beats them with clubs, and they accept the truth only when a sword is hanging over their heads.

This introduction of such people was not only for the Islamic community that was working in Medina, because the Qur'an is a guide for this ummah for as long as this ummah exists. If this ummah wishes to take guidance from the Qur'an about its enemies, it will find guidance in it. Whenever this ummah wishes to take any admonition from it, this Book gives it admonition. This Book gave the ummah guidance, admonition, and understanding concerning the Jews, and as a result the necks of the Jews bowed before the Muslims. When this ummah abandoned the Qur'an, it became a slave of the Jews. We see that this ummah is fully gathered, yet a small Jewish community prevails over it. Why? Because it is heedless of its Book and its guidebook. It is running away from the guidance of the Qur'an. It has cast it behind its back, and this ummah is obeying the sayings of so-and-so and so-and-so. This ummah will remain a victim of Jewish conspiracy in this way, and it will remain under the displeasure of the Jews in this way, for as long as it does not return to the Qur'an.

This discourse does not end until encouragement is given to some good people who have come out from among the Jews, and their courage is praised, for they leapt forth and accepted the truth. The Qur'an confirms the knowledge and faith of those people because of which they entered the community of Islam and accepted the religion revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). That knowledge was what descended upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and what had descended upon the prophets before him. They had greater firmness in the knowledge because of which they came to faith.
