(Verse 166)

The People of the Book deny this final Messengership, although it is entirely in accordance with the sunnah (established way) of Allah, who continues to send Messengers as bearers of good news and as warners, so that they may guide people and so that people have no argument before Allah on the Day of Resurrection. Moreover, the People of the Book accept all the Messengers before Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: the Jews accept all the Messengers before Prophet Isa (peace be upon him), and the Christians accept Prophet Isa (peace be upon him) and all the Messengers before him. If, despite these realities, they do not accept it, then so be it. (But Allah bears witness that what He has sent down to you, O Prophet, He has sent down with His knowledge, and the angels also bear witness; although Allah's witness alone is sufficient.)

In this verse there is the testimony of Allah to the truth of the Qur'an, and after Allah, the testimony of the angels, and among these angels are those who brought this Qur'an down upon the Noble Messenger ﷺ. These two testimonies nullify the claim that the People of the Book make. If Allah bears witness, then what is the significance of their denial? If the angels are witnesses, then what meaning does their denial hold? And since the testimony of Allah alone is sufficient, ...

By this testimony, Allah gave consolation to the Prophet ﷺ, because the Jews, along with their denial of the truth, were busy day and night with conspiracies and intrigues.

Furthermore, through this testimony it is also desired to reassure the Muslims, so that they may firmly stand by their position. This assurance was given at a time when they were newcomers in Madinah. In that period the Jews of Madinah had raised a storm of propaganda against Islam and the Muslims, and by various methods and approaches they were intent on eliminating Islam; the Qur'an also gave a thorough response to this in the surahs revealed during that period.

Here, now, a threatening warning is given to those who reject the truth. After the testimony of Allah and the angels, a warning is now the appropriate manner toward them, because despite this testimony, people were entangled in obstinacy and aversion.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 4, verses 167–169:

(Verses) 167 to 169.

These attributes and these judgments, although they are general, apply first of all to the Jews, and their stance towards the religion of Islam and its followers has been this. Rather, the Jews adopted this same attitude towards every true religion. These Jews may be those who were present in Madinah at the beginning of Islam, or those who were present at the time of Hadrat Isa (peace be upon him), or those who existed after them up to the present, or those who exist today in our era. Among them, only rarely have there been people who opened their hearts to Islam and were blessed with guidance.

Whether they are Jews or those people upon whom the attribute of disbelief and the attribute of blocking the path of Islam apply, they have certainly gone astray and have moved very far from the path of truth. They forgot the path to which Allah had guided them, and they abandoned the way that was the straight path of life. They went astray intellectually, conceptually and doctrinally. They went astray in their conduct, in their society and in their manners. They went astray in this world and they went astray in the Hereafter. They went so far away that there is no hope of their return. (Verse) "ḍalloo ḍalālan baʿīdā" (4:167) (They have wandered very far from the path of truth).

(Verse) "Inna alladhīna kafarū wa ẓalamū" (4:168): "Indeed, those who disbelieved and committed injustice." Disbelief itself is injustice. It is injustice against the truth, injustice against the human soul, and injustice against all people. The Qur'an sometimes applies the term injustice to disbelief as well. For example, "Inna ash-shirka la-ẓulmun ʿaẓīm" (Indeed, shirk is a great injustice), and elsewhere: "Wa man lam yaḥkum bimā anzala Allāh fa-ulāʾika humu aẓ-ẓālimūn" (Those who do not judge by what Allah has revealed are the wrongdoers). In the verse before this one, those who do not judge by what Allah has revealed were described as disbelievers. (A detailed discussion of this will come in Surah al-Ma'idah in this part.) These people did not only commit the injustice of shirk, but along with it they also committed the act of blocking the path of Allah. Thus, in a sense, these people have gone very far in disbelief, or have crossed the limits in injustice. After this, Allah also fixes the punishment of the Hereafter for them.

(Verse) "Inna alladhīna kafarū wa ṣaddū ʿan sabīli Allāhi qad ḍalloo ḍalālan baʿīdā (167). Inna alladhīna kafarū wa ẓalamū lam yakuni Allāhu liyaghfira lahum wa lā liyahdiyahum ṭarīqā (168). Illā ṭarīqa jahannama khālidīna fīhā abadā, wa kāna dhālika ʿalā Allāhi yasīrā (169)."

Those who themselves refuse to accept these (revelations) and block others from the path of God have certainly gone far away from the truth in misguidance. Likewise, those who adopted the way of disbelief and rebellion, and resorted to oppression and tyranny, Allah will certainly not forgive them, and He will not show them any path except the path of Hell, in which they will remain forever. For Allah this is not a difficult matter.

It is not the way of Allah to forgive such people, since they have gone very far and have closed the doors of mercy and forgiveness upon themselves. Now it is not befitting the majesty of Allah to guide them to any path other than the path of Hell. This is because they themselves have closed all the paths of guidance for themselves, and they have themselves erected barriers across all those paths, and have kept open only the path of Hell for themselves. And on the path of Hell too they have gone very far, and they have become permanent travellers on that road. These people will keep treading it, because they have made disbelief, injustice and blocking the path of Allah their constant occupation, and from them now there is only this expectation, that they will proceed further only on this path.

(Verse) "Wa kāna dhālika ʿalā Allāhi yasīrā" (4:169): "And for Allah this is not a difficult matter." He has full dominion over His servants. Between Him and any of His servants there is neither lineage nor kinship. For Him, punishing everyone is very easy. No servant has any power or any strategy against Allah through which he could create difficulties for Him.

The Jews, like the Christians, used to say that they are the sons of Allah and His beloved. They also used to say, "Lan tamassanā an-nāru illā ayyāman maʿdūdāt" (The Fire will not touch us except for a few counted days), and they also used to say that they are the people pleasing to Allah. When the Qur'an was revealed, it negated all these claims, and it placed each person in his proper station: that all are servants, and if they did good deeds they will be rewarded for them, and if they did evil deeds and were not given the opportunity of repentance and seeking forgiveness, they will be punished, and this is not a difficult matter for Allah.

After these clarifications, at this point, a general call is made to the whole of humanity: this Messenger has come to you with a truth. If anyone believes in it, it will be a kind of good for that person himself, and whoever chooses disbelief, Allah will suffer no loss from it. He is free of need from all. His power dominates all. And whatever is in the heavens and the earth belongs to Him. He knows everything and governs all affairs according to His knowledge and wisdom.

(Verse) No. 170.

Before this general call, the Qur'an refuted all the fabrications of the People of the Book (Ahl al-Kitab). It described the nature of the Jews, their vices, and their historical misdeeds, and it showed that they have always been obstinate. They treated Musa (peace be upon him) in this same way, even though Musa (peace be upon him) was their great leader, prophet, and deliverer. Moreover, before this general call, Allah had also explained the reality of prophethood and the purposes for which prophets are sent. For these purposes, it was necessary that messengers be sent, and it was also necessary that Muhammad (ﷺ) be sent last, because this final Prophet is for all the worlds. His call is "for all mankind," whereas every messenger before him was sent only to his own people. However, when the line of prophethood was decided to end, it was necessary that the Seal of the Prophets (Khatam al-Nabiyyin) bring a message for the entire world. ﴿So that people will have no argument against Allah after the messengers﴾ (4:165). That is, after the messengers have been sent, people should have no excuse before Allah.

If the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ) were not universal, and if it did not apply to the people of the whole world, then the peoples and nations who came after him would not have had the proof established against them until the Day of Resurrection. Instead, they could argue against Allah that no messenger had ever been sent to them at all. Therefore, by making the prophethood of the Messenger (ﷺ) general for all people and all times, and by declaring it the final prophethood, this argument was completed. Accordingly, the claim that no prophet would come after Musa (peace be upon him), or that no prophet would come after Isa (peace be upon him), would be contrary to the attribute of Allah's justice. For how is it possible that Allah would reward and punish people without sending a messenger? It is undeniable that before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the prophethood of no prophet or messenger was universal. Therefore, a universal prophethood was needed. This universal prophethood was the demand of Allah's attribute of justice and of His mercy toward people. And it was true when Allah said that He sent you as a mercy to the worlds. You were a mercy in this world and you will be a mercy in the Hereafter, as is evident from the meaning of this verse.

Lesson 44 at a Glance:

This lesson deals with the Christians among the People of the Book, just as the previous lesson dealt with the Jews. In both cases, the address is to the two groups who were engaged in excess and deficiency regarding Christ (Masih) and Mary (Maryam).

In the previous lesson, the Qur'an answered the myths of the Jews about Isa (peace be upon him) and his mother, and it explained the correct situation regarding the crucifixion of Isa (peace be upon him). Truth was defended against the Jews, their statements, their beliefs, and their obstinacy.

In this lesson too, the subject is truth, and the address is directed to the Christians themselves. They too went to extremes regarding Christ (peace be upon him). Among some nations, alongside the simple beliefs of Christianity, idol worship also became part of their ideas. When these nations accepted Christianity and established strong ties with it, Greek mythological concepts, Roman tales and stories, the superstitions of the ancient Egyptians, and the idol worship of the Hindus, among others, entered their beliefs.

When the Qur'an was revealed, the beliefs of the People of the Book had undergone extreme distortions. The Qur'an refuted the mythical stories that had entered their beliefs and pointed out all their deviant beliefs. Similarly, those who adhered to the religion of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and who considered themselves upon the true faith (Din Hanif), also experienced a deep deviation in their beliefs. Stories, legends, and the false practices of the Jahiliyyah had entered their concepts too. These people were also present in the Arabian Peninsula.

Islam came so that it might correct the beliefs of all human beings regarding their God, and so that it might save people from every kind of deviation and corruption. It came to eliminate every kind of excess and extremism in beliefs, and to set human thought on the straight path. In this way, Islam corrected the concept of monotheism (tawhid) of Aristotle, which he presented in Greece before the birth of Isa (peace be upon him). Likewise, it corrected the ideas that Plato presented in Alexandria after the birth of Christ. Moreover, all the ideas that so-called great minds presented in the field of theology after these two were, without exception, clear examples of misguidance and confusion. These were the product of human intellect, and all these ideas needed a message sent from Allah to guide them and to rescue these lost people from the mirage.

The issue presented here is the doctrine of the Trinity (Tathlith), in which the Christians fabricated the story that Christ is the son of God. By refuting this false belief, the correct monotheistic belief was explained in a right and straightforward manner.

When Islam came, the belief prevalent among the various sects of Christians was that God is one in three persons (aqanim thalathah): the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. Among these three, Christ was the Son. After that, their sects and schools of thought differed about Christ: whether he had a divine nature, or a human nature, or a combination of both. Then, despite the difference of natures, was his own status one, or were there different aspects? Or was he eternal like the Father or not, and so on. Clashes also occurred between these differing schools of thought, and they inflicted severe persecution upon one another. (Its details will be given at the time of explaining the verses in this surah.) Historical research shows that the doctrine of the Trinity, the doctrine of the divinity of Christ as a prophet, the doctrine of the divinity of Mary, and the inclusion of Mary in various forms of the Trinity were not all part of early Christianity. These beliefs entered Christianity at different periods of history, and various idolatrous nations entered Christianity in droves and kept bringing idol worship with them, because their conceptual purification had not taken place when they accepted Christianity. It appears that the Trinity was taken from some ancient Egyptian religions, such as the triads of Osiris, Isis, and Horus, and many other trinities in those religions are the source of this belief.

Among the Christians too, sects holding to the belief in monotheism have always existed, and throughout the entire history of Christianity these monotheists have suffered severe persecution, especially at the hands of the Roman church. As has always been the practice of the people of monotheism, they resisted these persecutions with fearless steadfastness. These persecutions continued until the sixth century CE by various societies that supported the government. The persecutions inflicted upon these monotheists included mass killings, exile, and all other kinds of oppression.

To this day, there is a deep uneasiness in the minds of the thoughtful people among the Christians regarding the doctrine of the Trinity. The people of the church (Ahl al-Kanisah) implant it in people's minds in various ways, and their final stratagem is that they declare it to be one of the unknowns (yak az majhulat), saying that its true disclosure will occur when all the secrets of the heavens and the earth are unveiled.

Mr. Peter, the editor of the journal "Usul Wuqu'," who is among the prominent expounders of the doctrine of the Trinity, says: "We have understood it in this way only to the extent of the limits of our intellect, and we hope that in the future we will be able to understand this belief well, when Allah lifts the veil from the secrets of the heavens and the earth." (See Nasraniyyat by Abu Zahra.)

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 4, verse 171:

Number 171.

The Christian doctrine of the Trinity is excessiveness in religion (ghuluww fi al-din), a transgression of bounds, and a turning away from the truth. For this reason the People of the Book are invited to say about God only what is true, such as that God has a son, or that He is one of three.

Their doctrine of the Trinity has changed through different periods in line with the ups and downs of their intellectual currents. But because of the natural human aversion to attributing a son to God, and because of the rationalism of the modern age, they explain this "sonship" in such a way that this son was not born in the manner in which ordinary human beings are born; rather, its reality is like the love a father has for a son. And they explain "one of three" in the way that one being has three attributes. Although to this day they have not succeeded in bringing these incomprehensible and contradictory concepts within the grasp of human understanding and perception, they have finally declared that they are mysteries of the unseen, and that their reality will be understood only when God lifts the veil from the secrets of the heavens and the earth.

God's Essence is free from partnership and resemblance, and the belief that God is the Creator necessarily entails that His Essence is separate from His creation. The separation between Creator and creature, and between Owner and owned, is an intelligible concept, to which this verse points.

(Verse) "Innama Allahu ilahun wahid, subhanahu an yakuna lahu walad, lahu ma fi as-samawati wa al-ard" (4:171) (God is indeed only one God. He is exalted above having a son. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth.)

If people find it strange that Prophet Isa (peace be upon him) was born without a father, and that it appears contrary to what they see day and night in this world, this astonishment arises because this event lies somewhat outside the familiar and customary course of things. But what people see every day is also not the whole reality; the laws according to which this universe runs before them do not confine the complete Sunnah of God within them. God is the Creator of these Sunnahs and laws. He repeats them, and He can also dispose of them in whatever way He wills. His will is subject to no limit or condition.

(Verse) "Innama al-Masihu Isa ibnu Maryam rasulu Allah wa kalimatuhu alqaha ila Maryam wa ruhun minhu" (4:171) (The Messiah, Isa son of Maryam, was nothing but a messenger of God and His word which He directed to Maryam, and a spirit from Him, which took the form of a child in Maryam's womb.)

In brief, he is a Messenger of God, and his position is no different from the position of other Messengers. He holds the same station as Prophet Nuh, Prophet Ibrahim, Prophet Musa, and Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), and he is one of that chosen company and those selected for the office of prophethood, who were sent from time to time over the longest span of human history.

(Verse) "wa kalimatuhu alqaha ila Maryam" (4:171) (a word which He directed to Maryam). A more readily understood interpretation is that God created Prophet Isa (peace be upon him) directly by His command. The Qur'an uses the words "Kun fayakun" (Be, and it is) for this creative command and decree. God directed this command to Maryam, and Prophet Isa (peace be upon him) came into being in her womb; this happened without the seed of any father. That is, it did not occur in the manner of the ordinary routine of human life, and this word of God is that which brings every thing from non-existence into existence. Therefore there is nothing astonishing in His bringing Prophet Isa (peace be upon him) into being in the womb of Maryam by His command and by the breathing of His spirit. (Verse) "wa ruhun minhu" (4:171) ("and a spirit from Him").

All adherents of the revealed scriptures accept that God fashioned Adam from clay and, after shaping him, breathed into him a spirit, whereupon he took human form. In another place God says:

(Verse) "Idh qala rabbuka lil-malaikati inni khaliqun basharan min tin. Fa-idha sawwaytuhu wa nafakhtu fihi min ruhi faqa'u lahu sajidin" (38:71–72) (When your Lord said to the angels: "I am going to create a human being from clay. When I have fashioned him and breathed into him of My spirit, fall down before him in prostration.")

And the same was said regarding Prophet Isa (peace be upon him):

(Verse) "Wa allati ahsanat farjaha fa-nafakhna fiha min ruhina" (21:91) ("And she who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into her of Our spirit.")

Therefore, according to the Qur'an, the spirit breathed into Maryam and the description the Qur'an gives of it are of the same kind as the description it gives concerning Prophet Adam (peace be upon him). In both places the breathing of spirit is mentioned, and none among the People of the Book maintains that Adam is the son of God, even though they all believe in the story of the creation of Adam and in the breathing of spirit into him. Nor do they maintain that Adam is one of the divine hypostases (aqanim), as they maintain concerning Prophet Isa (peace be upon him). Yet between Adam and Isa (peace be upon him) there is complete similarity in respect of creation and the breathing of spirit. Indeed, Adam was born without father and without mother, whereas in the case of Isa (peace be upon him) there was, by general agreement, a mother. This same reality is presented by the Qur'an elsewhere:

(Verse) "Inna mathala Isa 'inda Allahi kamathali Adama khalaqahu min turabin thumma qala lahu kun fa-yakun" (3:59) ("The likeness of Isa before God is like the likeness of Adam: He created him from dust, then said to him, 'Be,' and he was.")

Human beings are astonished that personal desires and the erroneous notions of idol-worship have turned the very simple and intelligible question of the birth of Prophet Isa (peace be upon him) into such a riddle, which for centuries kept the minds of many generations troubled. But when the Qur'an comes, it resolves this matter with great simplicity, with a single stroke, and the real truth becomes clear and manifest.

He who, by creating Prophet Adam (peace be upon him) without parents and granting him a spirit, and making him distinguished and superior to all creatures, is the same Being who brought Prophet Isa (peace be upon him) into being without a father. Why does this appear astonishing to you? This is also a form of life, and that is also a form of life. God's word is extremely clear, simple and intelligible, in comparison with those riddles that became prevalent among Christians and whose extreme point was the resolution declaring the divinity of the Messiah. They arrived at this conclusion solely because he had no father; and as a result of this they came to believe in three hypostases of God, although He is free of and far above such a notion.

(Verse) "Fa-aminu billahi wa rusulihi wa la taqulu thalathatun intahu khayran lakum" (4:171) ("So believe in God and His Messengers, and do not say, 'Three.' Desist; it is better for you.")

Within this call to believe in God and His Messengers are included Prophet Isa (peace be upon him) as a Messenger and Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) as the Seal of the Prophets. It also includes the call to give up the myths and false claims you hold concerning Prophet Isa (peace be upon him). Its details are coming in their appropriate place later.

(Verse) "Innama Allahu ilahun wahid" (4:171) (Indeed God is one God). His oneness is testified by the single consistent order running through this universe. The unity of all creation is placing the nature of the entire cosmos upon a single course, and this course is that God said "Be," and everything came to be. Then human reason also bears witness to one God, because the existence of a single governing God is intelligible to man. Human reason cannot conceive of a creator resembling creatures, nor can it conceive of three creators, and it is simply not comprehensible that there could be three and also one.

(Verse) "Subhanahu an yakuna lahu walad" (4:171) (He is exalted above having a son). A son is had because the father is mortal, and in that case the continuity of the line is desired. God is everlasting, abiding forever. What need has He to take as a son one who is mortal, when all that is in the earth and in the heavens belongs to Him?

(Verse) "Lahu ma fi as-samawati wa al-ard" (4:171) (To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth). It is sufficient for servants that they all establish their bond of servitude to God. He is the Guardian and Protector of all, and the Sustainer of all. What need is there, then, to seek a kinship with God? The relationship between God and His servants is that God is their Guardian and Trustee: (Verse) "wa kafa billahi wakilan" (4:171) ("And God is sufficient as Trustee").

Thus the Qur'an makes this truth clear to this extent and gives its judgment concerning the belief about Prophet Isa (peace be upon him). At the same time people are made to feel and realize that God is also their Guardian and Protector. God is constantly watching over them. He is also the Guardian of their needs, and the One who arranges their interests, so that they may entrust all their affairs to Him with tranquility.

Now the discourse advances further, and we come to a very great and important doctrinal matter: the conviction and belief that arises in a person's heart and mind as a result of the belief in Tawhid, namely that God is the Creator and Owner, and in response to this the human being is the owned and the servant. Therefore two realities, or two components of the belief in Tawhid, are essential parts of it: that God is the Sovereign and people are the subjects; God is the Deity and the one worshipped, and people are the worshippers and slaves; and that servitude and bondage are for all existence on this earth, and all kinds and species of existence are in His service.

Here the Qur'an corrects the belief of the Christians, according to which they regarded the angels also as sons and offspring of God, or associated them with God in divinity, just as they associated Prophet Isa (peace be upon him) in divinity.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 4, verses 172–173 (part 1 of 2):

(Verse) Nos. 172 to 173.

The Qur'an has made a great effort to instil the belief in Tawhid (Oneness of God) in people's minds: a unity that contains no trace of shirk (associating partners with God), and that implies no likeness whatsoever to Allah. The Qur'an has stated that there is nothing like Allah and no thing resembles Him. In His essence (mahiyyat) He has no partner; in His attributes (sifat) He has no partner; in His distinctive qualities (khasiyyat) He has no partner. The Qur'an also permits only one relationship between the Creator, Allah, and creation, and that is the truth that all things other than Allah (including living creatures) are His servants and obedient subjects. Whoever studies the Qur'an will see that it lays great emphasis on making this truth firmly established, and that every aspect of this truth has been brought under discussion, so that no shade, doubt or complexity remains in the human mind.

Further, the Qur'an also claims that this is the truth with which Allah sent all the Messengers. Therefore, whenever the Qur'an narrates the lives of each Messenger, and whenever it presents the summary of each Messenger's call, it says that the call of all the Messengers was towards the belief in Tawhid. This was the creed of the prophethood of Nuh (peace be upon him), and the axis of the prophethood of the final Prophet, Hazrat Muhammad (ﷺ), was also the belief in Tawhid. In the call of every Messenger this sentence has been fundamental: (Ya qawmi u'budullaha ma lakum min ilahin ghairuh) "O my people! Worship Allah; for you there is no god other than Him."

Therefore, it was a most astonishing thing that any person or people among the followers of these heavenly religions should distort the belief in Tawhid, although in those religions the belief in Tawhid has been the central point, and those religions have presented it in a most definite and decisive manner. So how could it be possible that the followers of any heavenly religion would attribute sons or daughters to Allah, or that the Divine Being would be united with some creature in the form of hypostases (aqanim)? Clearly, such beliefs can only have been borrowed from outside idol-worshippers.

In Islam, divinity (uluhiyyah) and servitude (ubudiyyah) are mutually opposed; this is the foundation of Islam. Between Allah and the servant there can be no relationship other than that of ruler and ruled, and of deity and worshipper. The ruled and the worshipper will be the creature, and the ruler and the deity will be Allah.

As long as people do not accept this straightforward view and belief, neither their lives can be set right nor their conceptions can be correct; otherwise, some shade, some admixture and some doubt will necessarily remain in their thoughts.

Yes, it is true that people's lives cannot be set right, nor can their thinking attain stability, until they are convinced of this relationship between themselves and their Lord: that the Lord is their ruler and they are His subjects; the Lord is the Creator and they are the creation; the Lord is their Owner and they are His possessions. All these servants and creatures are alike in this status. None of them is a son of Allah; there is no union of anyone with Allah; therefore there is no kinship between anyone and Allah, except that whoever has a store of faith and deeds and presents that store before Allah with a sincere inclination of heart, and this nearness is that which every person among His creatures can attain with Allah. As for the claim that someone is a son of Allah, or that Allah has united Himself with someone, this is not attainable by any human being.

Until this truth is firmly settled in the depths of people's hearts, that they are all servants and slaves of the one Lord, their lives cannot be set right, nor can their mutual relations be established, nor can they properly discharge the duties of life. The result of this conception is that all stand at an equal distance from the Supreme Ruler of rulers, and drawing near to Him is open to all. Thus there will be complete equality in status among all of mankind, in that their distance from the King of kings will be equal; and the false and counterfeit claim that there can be any intermediary between Allah and the servant will be utterly nullified. According to this conception, all the rights that any individual, lineage or ruling class has acquired for itself, claiming that they are distinguished from other people in their relationship with the Lord, become baseless. Without this conception, true equality among the common people cannot be established, nor can any system of human life or any society be founded on the principle of equality.

Therefore, from this perspective, the belief in Tawhid does not remain merely a matter of a single unitary idea that firmly settles in a person's mind and that is all; rather, the belief in Tawhid also becomes a system of life, a social bond, and a matter of international relations, that is, sociology, among the various generations and nations of mankind.

The truth is that Islam, by giving mankind the belief in Tawhid, has granted it a new life and a renaissance. Under its influence, a person, freed from the servitude of all human beings, becomes the servant of the one Lord, the Majestic. This is the reason why no church has ever been established in the history of Islam which would make people its subjects on the basis of this conception of life, that it is the representative of the Son of God, or the representative of that hypostasis which is complementary to the hypostases of Allah. For this reason, a theocratic system has never been established over Muslims in Islamic history, in which a king would adopt for himself the title Zill Allah fil-Ardh (Shadow of Allah on earth), in such a way that he has the right to rule from Allah, or that he can legislate on Allah's behalf because he is a kinsman of Allah, or because Allah has delegated His powers to him.

The church and the Pope reserved this right for themselves. Likewise, the followers of Peter also claimed this right for themselves. In Europe, people kept assigning this right to themselves under the doctrines of sonship and the union of hypostases. When the Crusaders began wars against the Muslims and kept fighting them, then, along with their defeat in the Crusades, they were also defeated by the Islamic doctrine of Tawhid. As a result of these wars, a movement for religious reform began within Europe, and the movements of Martin Luther, Calvin and Zwingli arose, which scattered to pieces the false conceptions of the church. All these reformers were influenced by the straightforward conception of life in Islam. They rejected the theory of the sanctity of man, or the notion that Allah had delegated His powers to someone, because they saw that in Islam there is one God, and in contrast all people are servants, and there is no intermediary between them.

For this reason, the divinity of Christ was decisively refuted in the Qur'an. Likewise, the divinity of the Holy Spirit was also refuted, that he is one of the three hypostases. In short, in no form was the doctrine of divinity left unrefuted, whoever might adopt this doctrine. The Qur'an decisively declares that Isa son of Maryam is a servant of Allah, and that he never regarded being a servant of Allah as a disgrace; likewise, the honoured angels are also servants of Allah, and they too have never considered their status as a disgrace. All creatures are in His servitude, and soon they will be gathered before Allah collectively. Those who consider servitude to Allah a disgrace and an insult should await a painful punishment; and those who consider themselves servants and slaves of Allah should hope for reward and favour.

(Verse) "Lan yastankifa al-Masihu an yakuna 'abdan lillahi wa la al-malaikatu al-muqarrabun. Wa man yastankif 'an 'ibadatihi wa yastakbir fasayahshuruhum ilayhi jami'a. (172) Fa-amma alladhina amanu wa 'amilu al-salihati fayuwaffihim ujurahum wa yaziduhum min fadlih. Wa amma alladhina istankafu wa istakbaru fayu'adhdhibuhum 'adhaban alima, wa la yajiduna lahum min dunillahi waliyyan wa la nasira. (173)" (4:172–173)

"The Messiah has never considered it a disgrace to be a servant of Allah, nor do the closest angels consider it a disgrace. Whoever considers the worship of Allah a disgrace and behaves arrogantly, then a time will come when Allah will gather them all and present them before Himself. At that time, those who believed and adopted righteous conduct will receive their rewards in full, and Allah will bestow upon them more from His grace. And as for those who considered servitude a disgrace and acted arrogantly, Allah will punish them with a painful chastisement, and they will not find, apart from Allah, any protector or helper among those upon whose protection and assistance they relied."

Hazrat Masih ibn Maryam does not consider himself above the station of servitude to Allah, because he is a Prophet and Messenger of Allah. He knows better than all people the stations of divinity and servitude. He knows well that divinity and servitude are separate realities, and that there can be no union between them. He knew best that he was one of Allah's creatures, and a creature of Allah cannot be like Allah; nor can it be a part of Allah. And he knew best that the duties of servitude are to be performed before Allah alone. He knew well that performing the servitude of Allah is a reality, and it has been so strongly emphasised that no deficiency or excess can occur in it, because only the unbelievers, who do not acknowledge Allah's creation and origination, can deny the servitude to Allah; and that servitude is the rank and honour which Allah gives to His Messengers when they attain the highest and most excellent stations. The same is the case with the honoured angels, among whom is the Holy Spirit. Their condition is the same as that of Hazrat Isa (peace be upon him) and all the other Messengers: they are servants of Allah. Therefore, what can be said of those followers of Hazrat Masih who deny, in respect of Hazrat Masih, that which he himself was appointed to?

(Verse) "Wa man yastankif 'an 'ibadatihi wa yastakbir fasayahshuruhum ilayhi jami'a (4:172)" (Whoever considers the worship of Allah a disgrace and acts arrogantly, a time will come when Allah will gather them all and present them before Himself.) Therefore, if they consider the servitude of God a disgrace for themselves and show greatness against Allah, then their deeds will by no means save them from standing before Allah, because Allah is the absolute ruler over all people, and before Allah's sovereignty the nearest servants and all people are alike.

As for those who recognised the truth and acknowledged the servitude of Allah, and who did righteous deeds, because doing righteous deeds is the necessary fruit of acknowledging the servitude of Allah, Allah will give them their reward in full, and will further bestow His grace upon them over and above that reward.

(Verse) "Wa amma alladhina istankafu wa istakbaru fayu'adhdhibuhum 'adhaban alima, wa la yajiduna lahum min dunillahi waliyyan wa la nasira (4:173)" (And those who considered servitude a disgrace and acted arrogantly, Allah will punish them with a painful chastisement, and they will not find, apart from Allah, any protector or helper among those upon whose protection and assistance they relied.)

Allah does not demand from His creatures the acknowledgement of servitude and the worship of Himself because Allah has any particular need of their acknowledgement of servitude or worship. He is the self-sufficient King. Nor is it that if these people serve Him, His rule and dominion will increase, or that if they do not do so, His kingdom will be diminished. Rather, Allah's purpose is that people should understand the meaning of Allah's lordship and sovereignty, correct their conceptions and beliefs, and reform their feelings and their consciousness, as a result of which their lives and the manner of their lives will be reformed of their own accord. This is because no system of life can be peaceful and secure, and no conception or belief can be firm and stable, unless it is firmly grounded in its foundation. No concept of life and no system can be stable without the sovereignty of Allah and the servitude to Allah, and without it, good signs cannot appear in life.

Allah wills that this truth, with all its aspects described above, should settle in people's minds, and that a detailed picture of their lives should be formed upon it, so that they may come out of the servitude of human beings and enter exclusively into the servitude of Allah. Let them know who the true sovereign of this entire universe and this earth is. They should bow before no one but Him. They should follow His system of life and His method alone. They should obey His Shari'ah alone. They should obey only those rulers who implement Allah's system of life. Allah's intention is only that they should know that all servants are, without exception, servants of Allah. Allah wills that the servants of Allah should walk with heads held high before other people, and if they bow their heads, they should bow them only before Allah. Allah wills that people develop a consciousness of their own dignity in the face of tyrannical, domineering rulers who are rebels against Allah. When people prostrate and bow before Allah, it is their duty to remember Allah alone and to remember no one besides Him. It is Allah's purpose that these people understand well that nearness to Allah is not attained through kinship and lineage. This nearness is attained only through taqwa (God-consciousness) and righteous deeds. The building of this earth and good deeds are the means of closeness and nearness to Allah. Allah wills that people perceive the reality of lordship (rubbubiyyah) and sovereignty (hakimiyyah), and that they recognise well their station of servitude. They should hold dear the sovereignty of Allah with ghairah (zeal) and hamiyyah (protective honour), and whoever seeks to share in Allah's right of sovereignty, they should stand as a barrier against him and reserve all rights of sovereignty exclusively for Allah. In this way their lives will be set right. They will progress, and they will be honoured upon the foundation of servitude.

The realisation of this great truth, the turning of all humanity toward Allah alone, the binding of all hearts to Allah, the grounding of all deeds in fear of Allah, and the basing of the whole system of life of all people on Allah's permission and command, having abandoned everything else, and so on — these are all matters which are a great treasure of goodness, freedom, justice and steadfastness in this world. Through them the wealth of humanity increases both in this worldly life and in the Hereafter. In short, this is an equipment by which freedom, nobility, justice and steadfastness will flourish in this world; and as for the end of such virtuous people in the Hereafter, Allah's grace will be upon them, His special favour will be theirs, and they will receive the special bounty of Allah.

It is our duty to reflect, in the light of the points stated above, on the requirements of Islam and faith, and to decide that such faith has been the foundation of the messages of all the Messengers. In later periods this original form of faith suffered distortion and change. From this true standpoint of faith it will become clear that, through faith, humanity will receive a new birth, and in that form faith will be a station of nobility and a declaration of freedom. As a result, the establishment of justice and equity will follow, and man will emerge from the servitude and slavery of man.

Those who regard the servitude of Allah as beneath themselves, and then fall into countless and endless other servitudes on this earth, ultimately become slaves of their own carnal desires. Then they become slaves of superstitions and myths, to the point that they become slaves of their fellow human beings, and their foreheads then bow before those humans. Then, in their lives, in their administration, in their laws, and even in their standards of good and bad, humans like themselves become the rulers. Yet in the reality of the matter, both are equal and alike as humans; but by obeying others besides Allah in this way, they have accepted others besides Allah as their deity. This is their position in this world, that they became slaves of people like themselves; and at the end, their position will be this:

﴿So He will punish them with a painful punishment, and they will not find for themselves, besides Allah, any protector or any helper﴾ (4:173)

This is an important issue in the Islamic view of life, which the Qur'an presents in this verse. Through it, the People of the Book, namely the Jews and Christians, were refuted at that time, and until the Day of Resurrection it remains a milestone for us.

In the previous lesson, by criticising the Jews, it was explained that, O people, Allah is the witness to the Messengership of Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), a testimony which is a decisive proof. Similarly, here, by refuting the Christians, all people are again invited to recognise that this Messengership is a proof from Allah. It is a new light by which the darkness of ignorance will be dispelled and all doubts will be removed. Whoever seeks guidance from it and holds fast to it firmly, upon him will be Allah's mercy, Allah's grace will embrace him, and in that light and guidance he will find the straight path.

It is our duty to reflect, in the light of the points stated above, on the requirements of Islam and faith, and to decide that such faith has been the foundation of the messages of all the Messengers. In later periods this original form of faith suffered distortion and change. From this true standpoint of faith it will become clear that, through faith, humanity will receive a new birth, and in that form faith will be a station of nobility and a declaration of freedom. As a result, the establishment of justice and equity will follow, and man will emerge from the servitude and slavery of man.

Those who regard the servitude of Allah as beneath themselves, and then fall into countless and endless other servitudes on this earth, ultimately become slaves of their own carnal desires. Then they become slaves of superstitions and myths, to the point that they become slaves of their fellow human beings, and their foreheads then bow before those humans. Then, in their lives, in their administration, in their laws, and even in their standards of good and bad, humans like themselves become the rulers. Yet in the reality of the matter, both are equal and alike as humans; but by obeying others besides Allah in this way, they have accepted others besides Allah as their deity. This is their position in this world, that they became slaves of people like themselves; and at the end, their position will be this:

﴿So He will punish them with a painful punishment, and they will not find for themselves, besides Allah, any protector or any helper﴾ (4:173)

This is an important issue in the Islamic view of life, which the Qur'an presents in this verse. Through it, the People of the Book, namely the Jews and Christians, were refuted at that time, and until the Day of Resurrection it remains a milestone for us.

In the previous lesson, by criticising the Jews, it was explained that, O people, Allah is the witness to the Messengership of Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), a testimony which is a decisive proof. Similarly, here, by refuting the Christians, all people are again invited to recognise that this Messengership is a proof from Allah. It is a new light by which the darkness of ignorance will be dispelled and all doubts will be removed. Whoever seeks guidance from it and holds fast to it firmly, upon him will be Allah's mercy, Allah's grace will embrace him, and in that light and guidance he will find the straight path.

(Verse 4:174) "O mankind, there has certainly come to you a clear proof from your Lord"

The Qur'an is a speech that contains such evidences that it is evident it is not the speech of a human being. Within it are found the signs of divine craftsmanship, and these signs distinguish it from human speech. In the word of God, the arrangement and flow of its words is worth observing. And the eloquence and rhetorical excellence of the Word of God is a matter that cannot be denied; indeed, some incidents have been witnessed that seem unbelievable. For example, people who are completely unfamiliar with the Arabic language also cannot help but be moved when they hear the recitation of the noble Qur'an.

Once, we were travelling on an ocean liner, crossing the Atlantic towards America. We arranged the Friday prayer on the deck. Six of us were citizens of different Arab countries, and some others were of different nationalities, and there were also Nubian Abyssinians who were part of the ship's crew.

I delivered the sermon, and in the sermon I recited some verses of the noble Qur'an. All the people on the ship were surrounding our congregation for prayer. They were people of different nationalities. They were looking on attentively.

After the prayer, many people came to us and kept expressing their impressions. But among them, a lady from Yugoslavia was very deeply moved. Tears had come into her eyes and her hands were trembling. In her weak English she began to say to us: "I could not help being affected by the humility and devotion within your worship. I do not know a single word of your language, but there is a vocal melody in this language that I have never seen before." After this she said that some sentences in the preacher's sermon were extremely distinguished, and they had a great effect upon her. I understood that those particular phrases were the parts and fragments of the Qur'anic verses that are exceptionally distinguished in their eloquence and rhetorical excellence.

I do not say that this is a general rule among those who do not know Arabic, and that every recitation of the Qur'an necessarily has such an effect upon its listeners; but there is no doubt that this is a clearly evident attribute of the Qur'an, that its sound enchants even those people who do not know Arabic at all.

As for those who have a special taste for Arabic and who are acquainted with the various styles of Arabic, the strange and wondrous accounts of the effects of the Qur'an upon them are part of history. When the Messenger himself recited the noble Qur'an to the people of the Ka'bah, the story of Akhnas ibn Shariq, Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, and Abu Jahl is very famous. Its details are mentioned in the Sirah of Ibn Hisham.

It is said that one night Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, Abu Jahl, and Akhnas ibn Shariq al-Thaqafi, an ally of Banu Zuhrah, set out from their respective places in order to listen to the speech of the Messenger, as he used to recite at night in his house during prayer. Each of them sat down in a place and kept enjoying the recitation of the Qur'an. None of them was aware of the others. They kept listening to the word of God during the night until dawn broke. When they began to return, they met one another on the way. They reproached one another harshly, and they noted that if some ordinary person had seen them, he would fall victim to this influence. Then they returned. When the second night came, again all three could not restrain themselves and sat down in their respective secret places, listening to the Qur'an throughout the night. When morning began to break, by chance again the three met on the road and reproached one another as before. When the third night came, these three again arrived to listen to the Qur'an, and they kept listening until late. When they were returning in the morning, they saw one another on the road again. This time they said that unless we take an oath, we will not be able to stop. Then they made a covenant by oath and went to their homes.

This was one story, of those people who have a taste for the Arabic language and the Qur'an. In whatever age they live, they know that the Qur'an itself is an authority and a proof, and is a miracle both in its wording and its meaning.

As far as the miracle of meaning is concerned, the thought that the Qur'an presents, the system of life it puts forward, and the picture of life it prescribes, we cannot give the details of these here. But from all these aspects too, the Qur'an is a miracle, and within it is proof and authority. From this it becomes known what the source and origin of the Qur'an is, and that it is not human speech. Its manner and style of expression is such as is not found in any human speech. Therefore (verse) "And We have sent down to you a light" (4:174), "and We have sent down to you a light that shows you the clear path." ...... A light in whose rays the true reality of things is seen, and seen very clearly, and in whose light a person at the crossroads of life sees correctly the path of truth among the paths of truth and falsehood, both in the inner paths of the self and on the outer highways of life. The self that is illumined by the light of the Qur'an sees its environment clearly.

Before this light the mist dissolves, the atmosphere opens, and then the reality appears clear and plain. When this light is attained by the human self, the person begins to laugh at himself, that the truth was really so plain, yet it is surprising that he could not see it.

And when a person lives for some time with his spirit within the Qur'anic atmosphere, and takes from the Qur'an his concepts, the standards of good and bad, and his values, then he sees all matters with great ease, great simplicity and great clarity, and then he comes to understand that many decisions he had made, which were a cause of perplexity for him and which he could not understand, now become easily understandable to him. Now realities are easily made clear, the further impurities that were attached to realities are removed, and all realities sink into the mind in the way that they have just come forth pure and clean from God.

How few words have been used: "And We have sent down to you a manifest light" (4:174). I have made the explanation and commentary of these words only for the sake of the person who has found within himself some light of the Book of God, not for the one in whom there is no gleam of this light at all. This spiritual light can be attained when a person makes heartfelt effort for it and develops personal taste. Along with this, I also have experience in Qur'anic sciences and possess the ability to receive light directly from the Qur'an.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 4, verse 175:

No. 175.

When a person develops a taste for faith, he immediately begins to strive to come under the protection of Allah, provided that his faith is sound and the human self has come to know the reality of Allah and understands what the meaning of servitude to Allah is. When someone grasps this reality, no path remains before him except to arrive under the protection of Allah, because Allah alone is the owner of sovereignty and power. And Allah takes such people under the shade of His mercy and grace. In this world too, the mercy of Allah overshadows them, and in the Hereafter too they receive mercy and grace and bounty; they are successful in the immediate life and successful in the life to come. Thus, true faith is like a lush, dew-laden garden with dense shade, in which the human soul, the restless soul, the bewildered and troubled soul, finds the most pleasant breeze and attains peace and tranquility.

Collectively, faith is a principle of life upon which social life is lived with purity, dignity, nobility, freedom and stability. Every human being comes to know well that he is only the servant of Allah and that he is the master of all the things in this universe other than Him. Such a concept is absent from any system other than the system of life based on Islamic faith. Islam alone is a system in this world whose sole aim is to free people from the servitude of people like themselves and to bring them into the servitude of Allah alone. This outlook is attained by a person when he regards Allah alone as his ruler, and all people, without exception, stand in one row as servants of Allah. Sovereignty and rulership become exclusively for Allah, and a person does not remain the slave of another person. In other systems, although he may appear free outwardly, in reality he is the slave of others.

Therefore, those who believe are, in any case, within the mercy and grace of Allah. They remain within mercy in this life and also within mercy in the life of the Hereafter.

﴿And He will guide them to Himself on a straight path﴾ (4:175). In the phrase, the word "ilayhi" ("to Himself") appears to show that a person advances step by step towards Him. Allah, as it were, takes the hands of the believers and leads them forward towards Himself. They are being taken, by the most straight path, towards Allah. They advance step by step towards Allah. Only the person who has, with insight, developed faith in Allah within himself and has firmly grasped the path of faith can perceive the beauty and sweetness of worship through this single word. He has firm certainty that he is on the path of truth; he feels at every moment that he is a traveller on the path of truth, with the roads before his eyes, and that he is always moving forward on the straight path with a clear policy. This is a meaning connected with the taste of certainty, and its realisation is not possible until taste and palate are sound.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 4, verse 176:

(Ayat) Number 176.

This is the last lesson of this surah. The surah began with the establishment of family relationships. It began with setting right the relations among the members of the family, and in between it also described some important collective matters. Now this last lesson is about the inheritance of kalalah. According to Hazrat Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) and the other Companions, kalalah is the one who has no children and no parents.

Some rulings about kalalah had already come at the beginning of the surah, at the place where inheritance was described. For example, if the kalalah has no male agnatic heirs (asabat) and those entitled to his inheritance are only maternal brothers and sisters, there Allah the Exalted said:

(Ayat) "Wa in kana rajulun yurathu kalalatan aw imra'atun wa lahu akhun aw ukhtun fa likulli wahidin minhuma al-sudus; fa in kanu aktharu min dhalika fa hum shurakau fi al-thuluth min ba'di wasiyyatin yusa biha aw dayn ghayra mudarr, wasiyyatan min Allah, wallahu 'alimun halim." (Surah 4, verse 12, final part)

"And if a man or a woman whose inheritance is to be divided has no children and his parents are also not alive, but he has a brother or a sister, then each of the brother and sister will receive a sixth. And if the brothers and sisters are more than one, then all of them will share in one third of the estate, after the will that has been made is fulfilled and the debt that the deceased has left is paid, provided it is not harmful. This is a command from Allah, and Allah is All-Knowing and Forbearing." (Verses 11-12)

Now the second form of kalalah is described, which was not mentioned there. If the deceased has no parents and no children, and there is only one full sister or a sister from the father's side, she will be entitled to half of the estate. But if such a sister dies, her entire estate will be taken by this brother. Apart from the shares of the creditors, if this woman has no parents and no children... Yes, if the deceased has two sisters instead of one, whether full sisters or only from the father's side, they will be entitled to two thirds. If there are many brothers and sisters, then according to the principle the share of the male will be equal to two shares of the female. Yes, it is worth noting that if full brothers and sisters are present, then only the sister or brother who shares only through the father will be excluded.

This verse of inheritance concludes, and with it this surah also concludes. And at the end comes that same Qur'anic admonition and conclusion: that the final outcome and return of all matters is to Allah alone. In this way, adherence to the Shariah is made obligatory in all rights and obligations, and in all financial and non-financial affairs.

(Ayat) "Yubayyinu Allahu lakum an tadillu, wallahu bikulli shay'in 'alim." (4:176) "Allah makes clear to you the rulings, so that you do not go astray, and Allah has knowledge of everything."

This is an extremely comprehensive verse. Allah has knowledge of everything: of inheritance and of other matters, of family relationships and of collective affairs, of rulings and of legislation. Either you will follow Allah's commands in every matter, or you will fall into misguidance. You have only two ways of living your life; there is no third way. Either there is the path of guidance, which Allah has explained, or there is another path, which is misguidance. Allah has spoken the truth: (Ayat) "Fa madha ba'da al-haqqi illa al-dalal" — "What is there after the truth but error?"
